letters.headline: Meet Ellen Paul
paragraphs: I felt it important to bring attention to the new Democratic candidate for the state representative seat for the 55th State District, Ellen Paul.

I had the privilege of listening to and hearing Ellen speak recently about her bold decision take action and challenge Republican Steve Weir for the state rep seat for the 55th District (which includes a small sliver of Glastonbury as well as Bolton, Andover ,Marlborough, and Hebron). This district has been represented by a Republican for 40 years.

Ms. Paul is a young mother, a Connecticut native who lives in the 55th in Glastonbury, and has been a librarian. She has become increasingly frustrated by the recent challenges librarians all over the country have faced to their ability to provide the public with unlimited access to facts and books on all topics. She is committed to protecting and fighting for First Amendment rights and the importance of facts, and reduced energy costs, our basic right to free and fair elections, and access to healthcare
Although do not live in her district, I have contributed to her campaign, will write postcards to residents in her district informing them of her candidacy and knock on doors for her.

She is a very impressive young woman willing step up at a very contemptuous time, to preserve building blocks of our democracy that are eroding before our eyes. If Ellen Paul wins this seat, she can begin to turn the tide as did the Democratic representatives in many districts, the most recent of which is Emily George in Palm Beach County, Fla., which includes Mar-a- Largo.
I urge you to read more about her and decide if you too will step up to support her, and impact so much more than just a local election in Connecticut

letters.headline: District 55 Deserved Better
letters.note: Wilkinson is a member of the Marlborough Democratic Town Committee but is speaking as an individual.
paragraphs: At a time when families across Connecticut are struggling with rising costs, it is disappointing that state Rep. Steve Weir voted against roughly $630,000 in new funding for his hometown Hebron and communities across District 55, including Andover, Marlborough, and parts of Glastonbury, and Bolton.

What kind of representative puts partisan politics ahead of direct relief for the people he was elected to serve? Residents are feeling pressure from higher grocery bills, gas prices, housing costs, utilities, and taxes. Yet when an opportunity came to bring funding back to our communities, Rep. Weir voted no.
Thankfully, SB 1 funding passed despite his opposition. That means real support will still reach local towns and residents who need it.
Voters should remember this on Nov. 3. District 55 deserves a representative who will fight for our communities and our tax dollars – not vote against them.

letters.headline: Weir Voted ‘No’
letters.note: Cremé is a member of the Andover Board of Education but said he writing as an individual.
paragraphs: Steve Weir voted ‘no.’ $630,000 in education funding for our local towns. Steve voted against it. Of course he did. This was a bill that would help his constituents. His loyalties were clearly not with the towns he represents. Last week, the Connecticut House passed a budget adjustment, 127 to 21. It sends roughly $270 million in new aid to Connecticut towns: $183 million to supplement K-12 school funding and $100 million in general municipal grants. For the five towns of the 55th District -- Andover, Bolton, Glastonbury, Hebron, and Marlborough -- that works out to roughly $630,000 in new state aid for fiscal year 2027. Hebron alone gets $270,000. Andover gets nearly $98,000. Marlborough, $149,000.

This was not a party-line vote. Of the 47 Republicans on the floor, 26 voted ‘yes.’ Weir’s neighbor in the 8th District, Tim Ackert, voted yes. So did Aniskovich, Bolinsky, and 23 more. A clear majority of House Republicans saw the same bill Weir saw, weighed the same fiscal concerns, and voted to send the money home. Weir was in the minority of his own caucus.

This is also not the first time. In 2024, Weir sent a flyer touting his “legislative accomplishments.” It turned out that his proudest achievements were losing committee votes on bills that never reached the floor and then voting with everyone else on bills that passed unanimously. Two years later, when an actually contested bill comes along that delivers real money to the towns he represents, he votes against it. At some point this stops being a philosophy and starts being a pattern. For this week’s vote, Weir’s comment was “The process is BROKEN…… twelve hours to thoroughly comb through a 700-page document is just simply not enough.”

His opponent, Ellen Paul, has said she would have voted ‘yes.‘ Of course she would have. Born and raised in eastern Connecticut, a former aide to Congressman Joe Courtney, now executive director of the Connecticut Library Consortium, raising two daughters in our public schools – Ellen understands what $270,000 means to Hebron’s school budget. She understands that towns absorbing rising costs need state partners, not lectures about the spending cap.
A ‘yes’ vote on SB 1 wasn’t a partisan vote. It was a vote for your town. Steve Weir voted ‘no.’ Ellen Paul would have voted ‘yes.’ That’s the choice.

letters.headline: Steve Weir’s Other Constituents
letters.note: Sauyet is co-chair of the Andover Democratic Town Committee and a member of the RHAM Board of Education, but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: You should know what your representative did on May 6.

It was the last day of the legislative session. Senate Bill 274 was on the floor. The bill would have done two things: increased penalties when landlords rack up repeat fire and building code violations, and required non-resident apartment owners to register with the towns where their buildings sit. It was the response to the Concierge Apartments disaster in Rocky Hill, where an outof-state private equity firm let a complex deteriorate until thousands of tenants were displaced at public expense. The bill had passed the Senate. It had cleared the Planning and Development Committee unanimously.
Steve Weir killed it.

He didn’t vote against it. There was no vote – Steve made sure of that. He and a handful of allies threatened to talk until midnight, knowing the clock would run out. Majority Leader Rojas pulled the bill. The bill died.
Why does Steve care so much about non-resident apartment owners? Funny you should ask.

Steve sits on the board of the Connecticut Apartment Association — the trade group for apartment owners. By CTAA’s own rule, his seat has to be held in the name of a company. He owns commercial real estate at 60 Village Place in Glastonbury through an LLC, appraised at $1.69 million. On the House floor that day, he called himself “a service provider to apartments.” In a 2024 candidate questionnaire, he said he spends “most of his time” on his commercial property. His “About” page mentions the CTAA board seat, but not the commercial real estate, or the CTAA rule requiring the seat to be held in a company’s name.

So when the General Assembly tried — for the first time in years — to give towns real tools to deal with bad-acting absentee landlords, the representative for Andover, Bolton, Glastonbury, Hebron, and Marlborough made sure they didn’t get them. He killed it on behalf of a constituency that doesn’t live here, doesn’t vote here, and doesn’t pay our taxes.

We haven’t even touched on his record on rentincrease notices, on housing code liens, on the rights of mobile home park residents to buy their own parks. That’s a longer conversation — and the full public-records picture is at andoverct.info/reports/weir-businesses.
For now, ask Steve who he was working for on May 6. And ask him why he didn’t tell us.

letters.headline: Ellen Paul for the 55th!
letters.note: Louden is co-chair of the Andover Democratic Town Committee but said she is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: Democrats from the five towns in the 55th District – Andover, Bolton, Glastonbury, Hebron, and Marlborough – are thrilled to select Ellen Paul as our candidate to represent the District in the Connecticut General Assembly! Ellen will be officially endorsed at a convention on May 20th at 7 p.m. at the Hebron Senior Center.

Ellen is ready to fight for the 55th District and to secure the resources we need to make it more affordable, to strengthen our schools, and to defend our values. Ellen believes that her values of respect, tolerance, honesty and integrity are under attack. Like the rest of us, she saw the devastating effects the Trump presidency was having on our State and knew that it was time to step up. Ellen is running to ensure that families, children, seniors and workers have our fair shot at the American Dream.

Ellen is a lifelong resident of eastern Connecticut and lives in Glastonbury with her husband, Steven, and their two daughters, who attend elementary school in town. Her credentials for the position of state representative are impressive. She worked as an aide to U.S. Congressman Courtney for five years and learned firsthand how a capable representative can benefit one’s district. As the current Executive Director of the Connecticut Library Consortium, Ellen has been involved in statewide policy initiatives related to libraries and understands the legislative process and the work and collaboration required to get bills passed into law. Her professional and personal background have prepared her very well to represent our 55th District.

Key issues on which Ellen hopes to focus are education funding for small towns, for which her work as a librarian and as a mother makes her a particularly capable advocate, and lowering energy costs in the State. She would have voted in favor of a number of pieces of legislation on which the district’s current representative, Steve Weir, voted “no”; he was one of only a few Republicans in the legislature, for example, who voted against increasing state funding for the schools in the 55th!

Ellen is knocking on doors of homes in all five towns in the district to meet with Republicans, unaffiliated voters, and Democrats to hear their concerns and to tell them about herself and her objectives if elected. You can learn more about Ellen and her candidacy on her website: EllenforStateRep. com.

letters.headline: Reservations with Weir
letters.note: Welch-Collins is a member of the Marlborough Democratic Town Committee, but is speaking as an individual.
paragraphs: I am writing with concern over Representative Weir’s vote on May 2nd against roughly $630,000 in new state aid to the five towns of the 55th House District.

In a year where municipalities in the 55th have been struggling with very challenging municipal budgets, voting against the opportunity to shift the tax burden away from the property of residents seems uniquely short-sighted. This aid was split between K-12 school aid and general municipal grants and reflects an increased awareness that the property tax burden is increasingly untenable for many residents of our region.
I have profound reservations about the dissonance between this vote and the fiscal realities within the 55th district.

letters.headline: Goodbye, Steve Weir
letters.note: Salvador is a member of the Marlborough Democratic Town Committee, but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: In a republic, we vote for people to represent us in government. When those representatives consistently vote “the party line” instead of the spirit of bipartisanship, most voters are disenfranchised. A representative who frequently votes in opposition to the majority of their party in favor of the “party line,” especially when the party votes in a bipartisan manner, accomplishes nothing. The constituents are not being heard.

The 55th District of Connecticut is losing its voice in what happens in Connecticut. Steve Weir has voted against the majority of the Republican Party 98 times! His own party! Ninetyfive of those occasions he voted to the right of the majority of Republicans. In 2024, Weir was the only Republican voting ‘no’ on a bill to enforce boating laws on waters near CT borders, while 52 Republicans voted ‘yes.’

There are 18 bills where the Republican majority (85% or higher) voted ‘yes,’ while Mr. Weir voted ‘no.’ Among those were a bill to recognize and honor Connecticut military veterans, a bill establishing a Parkinson’s disease research account, a bill making it a deportable offense to assault a law enforcement officer, a firefighter, or other first responder, and a bill to redefine “animal,” to regulate breeding kennels, provide certain procedures controlling rabies and make other minor changes to domestic animal related statutes. All of these bills became law. No thanks to Steve Weir.

The Connecticut Constitution requires legislative ratification of contracts negotiated by the executive branch and state employee unions. There were six times when Steve Weir voted against ratification when the vast majority of Republicans voted ‘yes.’ Weir is a ranking member of the Labor and Public Employees Committee. His ‘no’ votes have been consistently been more anti-labor than other available options while the majority of Republicans vote yes.

Steve Weir is not representing the 55th District of Connecticut. Weir frequently opposes his own party. How can Weir represent Republicans in our district with a record like that? With many Connecticut Republicans working with Democrats on bipartisan legislature, we are left with a representative who leaves us with a voice not heard.

The cry of “Taxation without Representation” was a driving force in the American Revolution. It was about laws being passed with no say from the colonies. Weir, by voting to the extreme right, is leaving the 55th District with no voice. It is time to say goodbye to Mr. Weir.

letters.headline: Who Does Weir Represent?
paragraphs: Why did Steve Weir, our elected representative of the 55th House District, choose to vote against much-needed state aid to its five towns?
The budget that he voted against on May 2 allocates over $600,000 towards our five towns to help relieve our stressed municipal budgets and lighten the load on us, the taxpayers.

Thankfully, it passed with overwhelming bipartisan support – but not from Weir. I think it’s worth asking as his current term draws to a close: Who exactly does Steve Weir represent? And does he really have the voters of the 55th’s interests at heart?

letters.headline: Seniors Be Aware!
paragraphs: In reviewing the outcomes from the most recent legislative session I was alarmed to see that our state representative from the 55th, Steve Weir, voted to reject $630,000 in state aid to our district. Thankfully, he failed to prevent this economic aid from returning to the taxpayers of our towns but I am concerned that we will not be so fortunate in the future.

As we continue to watch difficult municipal budgets force small towns, in particular, to struggle with rising property taxes and an increasing population of retired seniors, we need to ensure our representatives in Hartford are fighting to bring tax dollars back to our district.
Seniors, in particular, should pay close attention to how our interests are being represented as taxes rise and towns are forced to bear the burden.

letters.headline: A Profile in Filibuster
letters.note: Sauyet is co-chair of the Andover Democratic Town Committee and a member of the RHAM Board of Education, but he said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: We all know the great threats to Connecticut liberty. The overreaching regulator. The meddling bureaucrat. And, this spring, a bill asking out-of-state apartment owners to register with the towns where their buildings sit.

Senate Bill 274 grew out of the Concierge Apartments disaster in Rocky Hill, where an out-of-state firm let a complex rot until thousands of tenants had to be moved into hotels at public expense. The bill did two modest things. It raised penalties on landlords who rack up repeat fire and building-code violations, and it asked absentee owners to tell the towns they exist. It passed the Senate. It cleared its committee unanimously. The sort of thing most of us assumed was already the law.
Our representative, Steve Weir, drew the line.

He did not vote against it, exactly. Voting leaves a record. Instead, on the session’s last day, he and a few allies threatened to talk, and talk, and talk until the midnight deadline ran out and the bill quietly died, untouched by anything so vulgar as a roll call. It is a strange kind of courage, the heroism of running out the clock so that no one ever has to say where they stood.

I have tried to reconstruct the principle. A bold stand for the right of absentee landlords to stay anonymous? A defense of the crumbling stairwell against the tyranny of the smoke detector? Whatever it was, he held firm where the Senate and a unanimous committee had seen no fight worth having.

It may help to know that our representative sits on the board of the Connecticut Apartment Association, has called himself “a service provider to apartments,” and owns commercial property through an LLC. None of it appears in his official biography, though I suppose a man cannot list everything.
I do not expect my representative to vote for every bill. I would settle for him letting this one come to a vote.

letters.headline: Thank You, Mr. Weir
letters.note: RHAM High School 10th Grade Student
paragraphs: I was very thankful to be a part of the helicopter presentation and tour that Mr. Weir was willing to put on for the aerospace class. His selflessness in taking time out of multiple days of his schedule to come and present to ready-tolearn high school students was very appreciated. I know that not many people in high school aerospace classes would get a chance to see a live model of what they are studying up close.

We were very happy to welcome Mr. Weir and let him share his knowledge with us. Mr. Weir even let me come attend the presentation and check out his helicopter, knowing my passion for aviation, although I am not currently in that class. That shows an excellent inclusivity of others. Thank you again for coming to present at RHAM for us!

letters.headline: Weir’s Vaccination Stand
letters.note: Wilson is a member of the Marlborough Board of Education, but said she is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: I was appalled to discover recently that Steve Weir voted against the Connecticut legislation passed to ensure the integrity of vaccinations in our state. The bill sought to ensure that the state would be able to make recommendations and continue traditional vaccine standards, given the recent federal chaos and meddling of vaccine recommendations by HHS and the CDC. The law did not make any changes, simply provided local, evidence-based control over vaccinations in the event of federal interference on this very important health and safety issue. It was endorsed by the Connecticut Hospital Association.
Let your voice be heard on Election Day and let’s find someone else in the 55th District to lead us on this and other very important issues.

letters.headline: In Our Best Interest?
paragraphs: Drive through Hebron and you see a town that runs lean. We argue over the school budget every spring. We watch the mill rate. We know what a few hundred thousand dollars means here, because we feel it on every tax bill.

So $270,166 is not a rounding error to us. That is what Senate Bill 1, the state budget adjustment, was set to send Hebron in new aid this year, money that takes some of the weight off local property taxpayers who are already stretched.
On May 2, the House passed that budget, 127 to 21. The money was real and headed our way. And our own representative, Steve Weir, voted ‘no.’

I keep trying to picture how that goes. The state offers Hebron $270,000 toward costs we would otherwise cover ourselves, and the man we sent to Hartford says no thank you, not for this town, not this year.
What makes it stranger is that 28 of the 49 Republicans in the chamber voted ‘yes.’ They brought the money home. Weir didn’t.
I don’t need my representative to love every state budget. I do need him to fight for Hebron’s share of it. On May 2, he did the opposite.

letters.headline: Can We Support Weir?
paragraphs: Is Connecticut’s 55th district receiving exemplary representation from Steve Weir? Other writers pointed to his votes not being in our interests – we who are his constituents. The $630,000 he voted against for the extra school funding for our district towns doesn’t make sense. Is there an ideological reason driving him? We all know how much we need these funds given how tight our town budgets are.
Voting at a time when our country celebrates 250 years since our founding underlines the importance of having exemplary people represent us at all levels of government.

And Weir stood up for the administration’s war against the universities in his 2025 Hartford Courant op-ed. He must know that the now-vice president made a speech five years ago (September 2021) stating “universities are the enemy” at the Teneo network conference. The initiative was launched to diminish those who may challenge unchecked federal power.

Can we support Steve Weir who is not supporting us, his constituents? Can we support this candidate for the 55th District who stands up for an administration seeking absolute power over our lives, making state and local governments useless? Isn’t this contrary to the reasons “we the people” established this country where “all men are created equal?”

letters.headline: Paul Over Weir
paragraphs: I do not know state Rep. Steve Weir personally. People who do know him have told me he is a personal, likeable individual who participates and helps out in community affairs a great deal. However, despite his affable character, he does not serve the towns he represents very well as a state legislator. His vote against the state providing additional funds to the towns he represents, towns that are having tough budget years, is evidence that he does not appreciate the financial struggles the towns and his constituents are going through this year. Fortunately the bill passed with the help of some of Republican Representative colleagues of Mr. Weir who understood such struggles of towns and their constituents. His delaying of Senate Bill 274 which would help identify individual owners of apartment complexes so they could be held accountable for the poor conditions of their apartments shows he is not on the side of people who desire a habitable place to live.

The 55th state legislature district has elected Republican representatives for several decades. For most of that time the legislature has had a majority of Democrats in the legislature. As, such our 55th district representatives have not been in the room where legislative priorities are decided and which of the many bills will be put on the floor for a vote. The only actions that the minority party representatives have are to delay bills that they might not want to be put to a vote and to hope that the Democrats will listen to their ideas. State Sen. Cathy Osten has had to fight alone for grants to the 55th towns and for legislation that will benefit the 55th.

I believe that electing Ellen Paul as state representative would help Cathy in such fights as a partner, not as an opponent as Rep. Weir demonstrated with his vote against additional monies for the 55th. Ellen has a great background as a staff member of a U.S. representative and for working with people as a librarian, a job that entails contact with numerous and diverse people. I hope that you will join me in voting for her.
I write this as an individual, but I am proud to be a member of the Marlborough Democratic Town Committee.

letters.headline: Disappointed in Weir’s Vote
paragraphs: Earlier this year, millions of Americans were shocked and outraged by the scenes of masked, unidentified federal agents brutally seizing and, in some instances, shooting members of the community in Minnesota. Polls show that the vast majority of Americans reject this kind of lawless, violent behavior and want the immigration laws to be enforced by federal agents who receive the proper training and are directed by their superiors to respect the civil and constitutional rights of U.S. citizens and immigrants.

These were the goals that were embodied in a recently-enacted Connecticut law called SB397. SB397 creates “protected areas” like schools, hospitals and churches where federal agents cannot arrest people for violations of immigration law unless they have an arrest warrant issued by a judge. It prohibits agents from wearing masks (unless they are working undercover or outdoors in freezing temperatures) and requires them to wear identification (again, unless they are undercover). It fills a gap in the law by creating a right to sue federal agents in state court if they violate a person’s constitutional rights. It also imposes stricter training requirements for law enforcement officers and bans police departments in Connecticut from hiring former Federal agents who were found guilty of misconduct. Finally, SB397 restricts the amount of time that data from automatic license plate readers can be retained to 21 days and bans the use of that data in connection with investigating acts of protected speech, immigration enforcement and reproductive and transgender healthcare.

SB397 is not “anti-police” or “anti-ICE.” It is a common sense reaction to the abuses millions of Americans witnessed on the streets of Minneapolis. I think we can all agree that we want a nation where the laws are enforced, including the immigration laws. But those who are entrusted with the enforcement of the laws should also behave in accordance with those laws.

That is why I am disappointed that the 55th District’s representative, Steve Weir (R), voted against SB397. The 55th District (covering Andover, Bolton, Hebron, Marlborough, and portions of Glastonbury) needs a representative who strikes the right balance, and that is why I will be voting for Ellen Paul for the 55th District in November. I hope you will too.

letters.headline: Weir at Your Disservice
letters.note: Sauyet is co-chair of the Andover Democratic Town Committee and a member of the RHAM Board of Education, but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: Every so often Hartford dreams up a scheme so radical that only a true conservative can stop it. This spring it was House Bill 5467: a plan to help small businesses cut through state red tape by giving them a single person to call at the economicdevelopment office. A concierge, essentially, for the shop owner drowning in permits and paperwork.
The House passed it 143 to 4.

You will not be surprised to learn who supplied one of those four votes. Our representative, Steve Weir, looked at a bill designed to make state government less of a nuisance for small business and decided this was the hill. Forty-five of his fellow Republicans voted ‘yes.’ Every Democrat voted ‘yes.’ Steve voted no. Four members of the entire chamber stood against it, and he was one of them.

I have tried, as I always do, to reconstruct the principle. This is a man whose own biography calls him a small-business owner, recent chair of the CT River Valley Chamber of Commerce, and a “staunch supporter of free markets” and “limiting government intrusion.” If you drew a Venn diagram of the people who should have sprinted to the microphone to vote ‘yes,’ Steve Weir would be the overlap. He is the concierge’s ideal customer.

And yet. Perhaps he found the state being too helpful. Perhaps a man who has navigated the permits himself resents the thought of anyone else getting a guide. Perhaps “limiting government intrusion” turns out to include the parts of government that intrude by helping.
Whatever the reason, he has not shared it, and the vote is on the record either way.

When 143 of your colleagues, from both parties, agree that the small businesses of Connecticut deserve a phone number to call, and you are one of four who says no, the explaining is not their job. It is yours.

So I would like to hear it. Not a slogan about free markets; those he has in abundance. An actual reason the businesses of the 55th District should not have gotten this small, unglamorous help. Fortyfive Republicans managed to vote for it. Our representative couldn’t.
bills: HB 5467 (2026): small-business single point of contact

letters.headline: Ellen Paul for Women’s Rights
paragraphs: There are decisions that belong to government, and decisions that belong to people. Most of us, whatever our politics, would put a woman’s private medical care in the second category.

In 2025, the Connecticut House voted on House Bill 7213, protecting access to reproductive health care. This was not a party-line cliff. On final passage, a majority of the Republican caucus, 25 to 23, voted to protect that access. Our representative, Steve Weir, voted ‘no,’ joining the 23.

You can hold deep personal convictions on this subject and still believe that the choice itself belongs to the woman and her doctor, not to a legislator in Hartford. A growing number of Rep. Weir’s own colleagues seem to have arrived there. He has not, not on this bill, and not on any contested bill of its kind in the record.

The 55th District is home to people of every view on this question. What we should be able to share is the principle that some decisions are simply not the state’s to make. On the day the House affirmed that, our representative did not.

letters.headline: Weir Listens and Answers
paragraphs: The political silly season is here, and it wouldn’t be politics without partisan, out-ofcontext criticism. If we’re going to have a conversation about Steve’s performance, let’s make it an honest one. You can count on Steve for an honest conversation.
I’ll again be supporting our state Rep. Steve Weir for reelection. In my observation, he has lived up to the promises he made along the campaign trail over the past four years.

I’m thankful that Steve reads the bills, is wellinformed, and votes not with the majority or the minority, but rather based on how he interprets a piece of legislation will affect the 55th District. I appreciate Steve’s discretion and judgment more than a party-line vote. We didn’t put Steve in office to vote robotically on a party line.
On occasion, I’ve called him on his cell phone, texted him or emailed with legislative questions, including about his votes. And that’s the thing about Steve – he responds.

He’s active both in the district and at the Capitol to understand the impact of proposed legislation. He shows up at events. He volunteers. He donates and supports local organizations. He listens to all sides of an argument. He publishes a regular e-newsletter that anyone can sign up to receive. In that newsletter, readers are informed not just about district events and legislation that has passed, but also legislation that is up for consideration.

letters.headline: Weir is Working for All
letters.note: Beaulieu is a member of the RHAM Board of Education but is speaking as an individual.
paragraphs: I wanted to take a moment to share my thoughts about Steve Weir as he seeks reelection as state representative for Connecticut’s 55th District. We’re both longtime Hebron residents, and I’ve known Steve and his family for years and have always been impressed by his intelligence, integrity, and work ethic. Steve and his wife, Allegra, have volunteered quite a bit around the community, including helping the Lions at the annual Harvest Fair for the past few years. As a successful business owner, he understands the challenges facing working families and small businesses, and he brings practical, real-world experience to Hartford.

Steve is thoughtful and thorough. He doesn’t make decisions based on political pressure or catchy headlines. He takes the time to understand the details of every issue and carefully considers the long-term impact of the legislation before him. Whether you agree with every vote or not, you can trust that Steve has done his homework.

I’ve read several recent letters criticizing Steve’s record. While everyone is entitled to their opinion, many seemed to repeat partisan talking points rather than acknowledge the thoughtful approach Steve brings to public service. Legislators don’t vote on bill titles – they vote on the entire bill. Sometimes that means opposing legislation because of provisions unrelated to its stated purpose, including unnecessary government spending or other concerns that deserve careful scrutiny. As one of the few Republican voices in a legislature with a Democratic supermajority, Steve plays an important role by asking tough questions, offering a different perspective, and ensuring that legislation receives the careful review it deserves.

Whether Republican, Democrat, or Independent, we all benefit when our elected officials think independently rather than simply follow the crowd. Steve is honest, approachable, and deeply committed to serving the people of the 55th District. I encourage my fellow residents to look beyond the political rhetoric, consider Steve’s record, and support his reelection.

letters.headline: Question
paragraphs: One vote, and one question, from 2023.

That year the Connecticut House passed House Bill 6569, which raised the marriage age to 18 with no exceptions and ended child marriage in our state. The state Senate had already passed it unanimously: every Democrat and every Republican. Connecticut became the ninth state to close the loophole.
Our representative, Steve Weir, voted no.

Here is the question. The entire state Senate, of both parties, agreed that children should not be married in Connecticut. What did Rep. Weir know, or believe, that every one of those senators did not?

I am not asking rhetorically. There may be some explanation. But on a bill to end child marriage, one so broadly accepted that the Senate passed it without a single dissenting vote, the people of this district deserve to hear, in his own words, why their representative said no.

letters.headline: A Vote Worth Missing
letters.note: Sauyet is co-chair of the Andover Democratic Town Committee and is a member of the RHAM Board of Education, but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: State Rep. Steve Weir shared some news on Facebook this month: in his four years at the Capitol, he has never missed a vote. All 650 recorded votes of the term, and he was present for every one. That is true, and it deserves credit. It is also true of Speaker Ritter, of our neighbor Rep. Tim Ackert, and of 35 other members of the House, none of whom made a graphic about it. Showing up is the job, and roughly a quarter of the chamber does it perfectly. But grant him this: he shows up.

Which is just the trouble with a perfect attendance record. It means every vote is a choice. No gaps, no sick days, no “I missed that one.” When our representative tells us he has never missed a vote, he is telling us that everything on his roll call was done on purpose.
Including June of 2023.

That month the House took up House Bill 6569, raising Connecticut’s minimum marriage age to 18, with no exceptions. It ended child marriage in this state and made us the ninth state in the nation to do so. The Senate had passed it unanimously: every Democrat, every Republican, not a single dissent. The House passed it 98 to 45, and the governor signed it into law.
Steve Weir voted ‘no.’

The bill did one thing. It said that children cannot marry in Connecticut. Senators of both parties found it an easy yes, all of them. Our representative read the same page and found his way to ‘no,’ and thanks to his diligence we know it was not an accident. He was there. He heard
Members of the public are invited to the debate. He chose.
Perfect attendance is an honor we mostly give to schoolchildren. Protecting them would have been the better one to claim.

letters.headline: Reelect Steve Weir!
paragraphs: What are your values as a resident of the State of Connecticut? Who would you want to represent those values and what you so firmly believe? For us, we want Steve to be that person. We have no doubts and we have no questions . We support Steve Weir!
Jack and Sandy Hooker
Hebron Residents for Over Half a Century

letters.headline: Leave Weir Alone
paragraphs: Last week, a couple of letters addressed CT House Bill 6569, which raised the minimum age for marriage to 18 in CT. Presumably, the bill protects individuals under the age of 18 from potential victimization or abuse due in part to a child’s lack of maturity, life experience, and decision making ability. Or, as the letter writers suggest, the bill was designed to protect children. Maybe I missed it, but I don’t recall much of an argument or debate about this topic. Certainly the authors of the aforementioned letters didn’t need to make a compelling case for a bill that is self-evident. But they did anyway.

Aside from espousing the protection of children, the authors also reference the voting record of state Rep. Steve Weir (R-55), who voted no for the passage of Bill 6569…in 2023. Three years ago. Apparently 44 other state representatives also voted no…in 2023. Three years ago. Why are we talking about this now? Bill 6569 is old news. And why is Rep. Weir being singled out for his vote? Is the News Bulletin going to print the other 44 names? It seems that the virtue of Bill 6569 is being used to bring negative attention to Rep. Weir. My cynical side wonders if this has anything to do with Rep. Weir’s (R) designation.

And remember, even though multiple states have a minimum marriage age of 18 due in part to a child’s lack of maturity, life experience, and decision-making ability, Nancy Pelosi wants 16 year-olds to vote in presidential elections. Can I get me a ballot, dude?

Instead of impugning Rep. Weir over an already enacted bill, we should be more concerned about Chris Murphy’s unscrupulous proposal to increase the minimum wage to $25/hour by 2031. What we really need is a bill to protect us from Chris Murphy.

letters.headline: To the Right of His Own Party
paragraphs: In 2025, the Connecticut House cast a final vote on House Bill 7213, which protects access to reproductive health care. It was a high-profile vote, and a revealing one.
On final passage, the Republican caucus voted 25 to 23 in favor of the bill. A majority of his own party backed it.
Steve Weir was one of the 23 voting ‘no,’ to the right of his own caucus on one of the most closely watched issues of the session.

This was not Weir holding a Republican line. The line had moved, and his own colleagues, narrowly, had crossed it. He stayed behind. And it was not a one-time stand: across every contested reproductive-rights bill in the recent record, our representative has voted ‘no,’ every time.

The people of this district hold a range of views on this issue, as they should. But they are entitled to know that on reproductive health care, their representative sits not in the middle, and not even with most of his own party, but at the far edge of it. The 2025 vote made that plain.

letters.headline: We’re Better for Weir
paragraphs: In today’s world, it’s easy to focus on titles or political affiliations. I believe the people who leave the greatest impact are often those who quietly show up and invest in their communities without expecting recognition. That’s why I wanted to share a few words about Steve Weir, not simply as a state representative, but as someone I’ve had the privilege of knowing for most of my life.

I’ve known Steve since childhood. I grew up alongside his middle daughter, Juliana, and we spent years together on countless swim teams. Like many parents, Steve devoted countless hours to supporting his children, but he always seemed to go a step further. Multiple nights a week, he drove us to practices, waited through long evenings, cheered us on at meets, and made sure everyone got home safely. Looking back, I realize those moments reflected the same dependable character I’ve continued to witness throughout the years.

As I grew older, I continued seeing Steve involved throughout our community. Whether it was volunteering, supporting local organizations, or simply showing up to help wherever he was needed, he consistently demonstrated that community service isn’t about publicity. I’ve had the opportunity to work alongside Steve at many community events. I’ve seen him volunteer at the

Glastonbury Apple Harvest & Music Festival, including helping with the annual 5K, assisting with parking at the Hebron Harvest Fair, and volunteering at Marlborough Day. I’ve also watched him attend and celebrate multiple local business grand openings, encouraging entrepreneurs and welcoming new businesses into our town. Time after time, he chooses to be present because he believes in strengthening the community.

I’ve also seen Steve volunteer in the kitchen at The Brick Cantina, a local restaurant, during one of its busiest times. As someone who now handles the restaurant’s marketing, I’ve come to appreciate just how demanding restaurant work can be. Steve didn’t stop in for a handshake or photo. He put on an apron, worked alongside the staff, and helped wherever he was needed.

While many people know Steve because of public office, I’ve always known him first as a father, neighbor, volunteer, and friend. Regardless of political beliefs, it’s important to recognize people who consistently give back. Steve Weir has spent years doing exactly that, and our community is undoubtedly better because of his steady commitment, humble leadership, generous spirit, and unwavering willingness to serve others every single day.

letters.headline: We Need Steve Weir
paragraphs: I find myself so fed up with all of the political commercials on television every night. I usually end up muting most of them. I remember when those commercials were about the person that wanted to be elected, not who could tear their opponent apart.

I want to talk about Steve Weir. I worked with Steve at the Glastonbury Police Department for several years. It was such a pleasure working with Steve as his demeanor spoke volumes about who he is. I never once heard him raise his voice. He is one of the most compassionate people I know. The life of Steve Weir revolves around helping others. I will never truly understand how he fits so many varied interests into a normal day.
Steve is always accessible. I have reached out to him to produce proclamations from the House for fellow workers who were about to retire and had made a significant impact on the Town of Glastonbury.

Steve always came through for me. It was so uplifting when Steve would present the proclamations to the employees. In most cases Jill Barry, from the 31st District, would accompany Steve. Steve Weir is a hard-working man. We need him in the 55th District. His 100% voting record in the House for all 4 of his years in the Legislature is commendable. Steve will listen to anyone and is willing to have a conversation with them regardless of party affiliation. Steve always gives back to the community. Steve is a people person. Steve is a wonderful person. Steve is a leader. We need Steve Weir.

letters.headline: No Better Choice Than Weir
letters.note: Retired Glastonbury Police Officer
paragraphs: I am writing in strong support of Steve Weir’s re-election to the Connecticut House of Representatives for the 55th District. I have known Steve for nearly 30 years and cannot think of anyone who has worked harder for the people he represents.

As a retired Glastonbury police officer, I worked with Steve directly and later took over his role as Crime Prevention and Community Outreach Officer. His impact on Glastonbury’s seniors and the Riverfront Community Center was lasting. For more than a year, people still accidentally called me “Steve” because of the impression he had made. He cared deeply about people, brought forward-thinking ideas to the department, and got things done.

One of Steve’s greatest strengths is his ability to listen. At the Glastonbury Apple Fest, he always remembered my wife’s and daughters’ names and took a real interest in our conversations. He listens to Democrats and Republicans alike, and when a concern is valid, he fights for that person regardless of party affiliation. That is exactly the kind of representative we need.

I have watched Steve serve this community as a small business owner, police officer, realtor, and founder of American Integrity Restoration. His career reflects a consistent commitment to service, and his deep Glastonbury roots make him well suited to represent us.

Steve is also a devoted family man and a familiar presence far beyond his district. Years ago, at a lake gathering in Columbia, a small helicopter flew overhead and people immediately said, “There goes Steve Weir.” He knew we were there and flew by to say hello. That moment captured how connected he is to the people around him.

I am not usually active in politics, but after knowing Steve for so long, I am confident he is the right person for the job. His 100% voting record shows that he shows up, stays informed, and takes his responsibilities seriously.

To me, there is no better choice. I would rather be represented by someone with deep hometown roots and a real understanding of our community. I urge everyone to vote for Steve Weir. He is an impressive person and a good friend.

letters.headline: Weir Is a Nice Guy; That’s Not Enough
letters.note: Sauyet is co-chair of the Andover Democratic Town Committee and is a member of the RHAM Board of Education, but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: Recent letters have praised Steve Weir as a kind, accessible, hard-working man. I believe every word. If we were choosing a neighbor of the year, he would get my vote.

But we are choosing a legislator, and a legislator’s job is not proclamations and ribbon cuttings. It is votes. His admirers point to his perfect attendance. Perfect attendance is fine, but only if those votes support our community. Consider what four years of showing up has produced.

This May the House passed the budget adjustment, SB 1, by 127-21. It carries roughly $630,000 in new aid for the five towns of the 55th: about $98,000 for Andover, $270,000 for Hebron, $149,000 for Marlborough, plus more for Bolton and eastern Glastonbury. Of the 49 Republicans voting, 28 said ‘yes.’ Weir voted ‘no,’ on money for his own towns.

After the Concierge Apartments disaster in Rocky Hill, where an out-of-state owner let a complex rot until thousands of tenants had to be relocated and the Attorney General had to extract over $5 million, the legislature answered with SB 274. It passed the Senate and cleared committee unanimously. On the session’s last night, Weir and a few allies threatened to run out the clock, and the bill died without a vote. Weir sits on the board of the Connecticut Apartment Association, whose president testified against the bill. Whose side was he on that night?

The pattern runs deeper. He voted no on requiring safety fences around swimming pools; it passed 102-45. He voted ‘no’ on ending child marriage in Connecticut; it passed 98-45. He was one of five ‘no’ votes on approving the State Police union contract, one of four against giving small businesses a single point of contact in state government, one of three against reappointing Judge Elizabeth Bozzuto, and the lone Republican ‘no’ on enforcing our boating laws.
This is not moderate versus conservative. When a bill passes 143-5 and your representative is one of the five, again and again, that is not independence. It is reflex.
A thousand ribbon cuttings do not make up for a no vote on your own towns’ aid. A hundred proclamations will not shelter a tenant or fence a pool. Steve Weir is a nice guy. That is not enough.
bills: HB 5467 (2026): small-business single point of contact

letters.headline: We Can’t Afford A Third Weir Term
letters.note: Wilkinson is a member of the Marlborough Democratic Town Committee, but said she is speaking as an individual. on first service or next service
paragraphs: I went looking for evidence that Steve Weir has delivered results for the 55th District. I visited his own campaign website, steveweirforct. com, expecting to find a bill he authored, a dollar figure he brought back to our towns, or a law that eased the cost of living here. I found none. What’s there is attendance, community involvement, and general values language — no legislative accomplishments, no funding secured, no results claimed.

Then I looked at Ellen Paul’s site, ellenforstaterep.com, which lays out Weir’s actual voting record with bill numbers attached. According to her published account: he voted ‘no’ on early-childhood education funding, ‘no’ on property tax relief tied to modernizing the state’s school funding formula, ‘no’ on renewable energy and community solar projects that could lower our electric bills, and ‘no’ on paid sick days and paid family leave — this despite serving as Ranking Member of the Labor Committee. Her site also states he voted the Republican party line 96% of the time on contested bills.

Meanwhile, our bills keep climbing. Property taxes are up. Gas, groceries, heating oil, and electricity cost more every month. Health insurance premiums have gotten so high that families are dropping coverage they can’t afford. This is precisely the moment a state representative should be delivering relief — not compiling a perfect attendance record while voting no on the bills meant to address it.

Ellen Paul is a librarian, nonprofit leader, and mother who has spent her career building coalitions and getting things done. Her platform speaks directly to what’s hurting us: property tax relief, affordable housing, and accountable energy policy that puts ratepayers first.
This November, or during early voting Oct. 19th through Nov. 1st, I’ll be voting for Ellen Paul.

letters.headline: Time for a Change
letters.note: Howell is a member of the Hebron Democratic Town Committee but said he is writing as a concerned citizen.
paragraphs: Over the past few weeks, I have seen several letters commenting about Steve Weir, both positive and negative. I applaud these letters as this is what our constitution guarantees: freedom of political choice and voice.

At the start of this political season, I reviewed Steve Weir’s record and was truly surprised. His voting record, which is available to all and has been discussed in depth in several letters, shows a complete lack of support for our district. One of his supporters stated that Steve has a 100% voting record (as does about 40% of our elected representatives), that he always listens and studies what is in front of him, so he understands what he is voting on. My thought was this position statement is unfinished as it should have ended with “and then he votes ‘no’ anyway.”

But what astounded me is the absolute lack of any bills sponsored by Steve Weir. Our district is facing several significant challenges: lack of housing for our young people resulting in many having to move out of state; rising educational costs, especially when it comes to our special needs students; bonding issues for upkeep of our infrastructure; funding to help the less fortunate in our society who are being thrown off food and medical support by the current national administration.
And Steve’s reaction: nothing but crickets.
Join me in voting for Ellen Paul this November, a candidate who has the experience and network in Hartford to help our district navigate our growing challenges.

letters.headline: Why I’m Seeking Reelection
paragraphs: I am seeking another two-year term as state representative of the 55th District because I believe experience, preparation, integrity and a deep understanding of the communities you represent matter.

My connection to this area goes back a lifetime. I grew up in Glastonbury, have lived in Hebron with my family for 26 years, and have spent more than three decades working, volunteering and serving in our communities. Before entering the legislature, I have served as a police officer, business owner, employer, volunteer and community leader. Those experiences shape how I approach this job every day.
Serving effectively requires much more than showing up, although I am proud to have maintained 100% attendance for every House and committee vote during my four years in office.

It requires doing the work before the vote. It also requires building relationships with legislators on both sides of the aisle, listening to different perspectives and finding common ground whenever possible.

Legislation is rarely as simple as a title or a political talking point. Bills can contain hundreds or thousands of lines, and good ideas are sometimes accompanied by provisions with unintended consequences. I take seriously my responsibility to read legislation, research the issues, ask questions and listen to people on all sides before deciding how to vote.

I don’t believe one party has all the right answers all of the time. I have supported good ideas regardless of where they originated and opposed proposals when I believed the details would hurt the people I represent. My obligation isn’t to a political party. It is to the residents of Andover, Bolton, Glastonbury, Hebron and Marlborough.

I also believe balance matters in government. Connecticut’s legislature is currently controlled by the Democratic Party by roughly a two-toone margin, with veto-proof majorities. Regardless of which party holds power, government benefits from strong voices asking questions, challenging assumptions and ensuring that different perspectives are represented.
Over four years, I’ve worked to earn your trust by being accessible, listening, showing up and treating people respectfully whether they agree with me or not.
I know these communities. I’ve raised my family here, built businesses here, volunteered here and served here for decades.
I’m asking for the opportunity to continue that service – with the same preparation, independence, integrity and commitment I’ve brought to the job every day.
State Rep. Steve Weir
R-55th District
Proudly Serving Andover, Bolton,
Glastonbury, Hebron and Marlborough

letters.headline: Kind, Accessible, Committed
paragraphs: Four years ago, I became friends with Steve Weir, and over those four years, I’ve gotten to know not just the State Representative, but the person behind the title.
Our daughters went to RHAM High School together and are now roommates at FGCU. Along the way, our families have become family, our home is their daughter’s home, and theirs is our daughter’s home.

Steve is level-headed, kind, accessible, and genuinely committed to serving the people of Connecticut. One thing I appreciate most is that he does his homework. He reads the bills before voting, asks questions, and uses common sense to think about what legislation actually means for Connecticut families, businesses, and communities.

When I hear constituents raising concerns about an upcoming bill, I’ll often read it myself and then call Steve and ask, “What do I need to know? Is there something I should be concerned about?” He is always willing to make the time to explain the details and help me understand what’s really in the legislation.

Steve doesn’t vote blindly or simply follow a party line. He has had to make difficult decisions and vote ‘no’ on bills when he believes they are not right for Connecticut. He looks beyond the headline, pays attention to the details, and works to make sure the “hidden stuff ” doesn’t slip through.
He has shown up for every vote during his four years in the legislature, and to me, that says a lot about his commitment.

I’m proud to call Steve a friend, and I’m grateful our families have become so close. Most importantly, I know that when Steve says he is working for the people of Connecticut, he takes that responsibility seriously.

letters.headline: Two Stacks of Mail
paragraphs: Since the middle of July, eight letters have appeared in these pages telling us good things about state Rep. Steve Weir. I went back and read them all, and I believe every word. He remembers your children’s names at the Apple Fest. He volunteers at the Harvest Fair and once worked a shift at a busy local restaurant, apron and all. He answers his cell phone. Four of the eight points to his 100 percent voting record, which, as one letter honestly puts it, shows that he shows up.

Then I noticed something odd. In eight letters of praise, not one defends a single vote he has cast. One brings up his vote against ending child marriage but argues only that it is three years old and that other legislators voted the same way. Two more explain, in general terms, that a legislator sometimes opposes a good bill because of hidden or unrelated provisions, but never name a bill or a provision.

Last week, Mr. Weir joined in with a letter of his own. He tells us he reads every bill and votes ‘no’ when the details would hurt us. Which details? Which bills? Go back and read it: in his own case for reelection, the man present for every vote of his four years does not name, let alone defend, one of them. The letters questioning his record read differently. Since May, more than 20 of them have discussed at least 15 specific votes, with bill numbers and tallies anyone can check: the budget carrying $630,000 for our five towns, help for small businesses, safety fences around pools, ending child marriage, and more.

So we have two stacks of mail. One tells us who Steve Weir is: a kind, hard-working, and decent community member. The other shows us what he does with the vote we lend him every two years. Neither stack disputes a word of the other. Both can be true at once. However, only one of them is about the job. If anyone, including Mr. Weir, believes those votes were the right ones for the 55th, the page is open: pick one and make the case. Until someone does, I am with Ellen Paul, who talks about the votes because she is not afraid of them: ellenforstaterep.com.
bills: HB 5467 (2026): small-business single point of contact

letters.headline: Weir Works for All
paragraphs: I am writing to endorse Steve Weir for another term as our state representative for the 55th district. He has been working hard for all of us and will continue to do so. He hasn’t missed a single vote and showing up is half the battle. It’s also evidence that he takes his job seriously. He gets involved with many things that are happening in the towns he covers. He’s ready to listen to all of us and do what he can to effect change where needed. We are clearly ruled by the Democratic Party in this state, and it’s getting harder to make ends meet.

There have been several letters claiming that Steve has voted against some bills with very desirable names. Most people are aware that these bills have many other parts that are tucked into them that are not so desirable. Steve reads the entire bill and sees unintended consequences. When he votes ‘no’ it is because of other things in the bill that the letter writers don’t tell you. Don’t be fooled by these letters. You can go and read these bills yourself or contact Steve and he will tell you why he voted ‘no.’

Citizens need all our support, and we need more Republicans elected to strike a proper balance in governing. Steve Weir is a great example of a Representative with honesty and integrity, working for all the people, and not just “playing politics”. We need him to be re-elected. Please vote for Steve Weir.

letters.headline: Long Overdue
letters.note: Sauyet is co-chair of the Andover Democratic Town Committee and a member of the RHAM Board of Education, but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: Let me tell you about librarians.

Mrs. Hatch, who ran my elementary school library, taught us to read stories aloud and had a gift for putting the right book in the right hands at the right moment. Some of you have heard me tell of her before. I make no apologies. She earned it.

A junior town librarian of my childhood broke a rule for me. Adult cards began at 13, and then only with parents’ permission; I was 10 and had read my way through the children’s room. She glanced around to see that no one was looking, then issued the card. In gratitude I tried to teach her to juggle. I was probably a terrible teacher at 10. I hope she kept practicing. I am ashamed to say I no longer remember her name. I have never forgotten the card.

In high school, Miss K taught me what research actually is: not finding an answer but testing one. Where did this come from? Who wrote it, and what did they want me to believe? What would it take to prove it wrong? I have leaned on those questions my entire adult life.

So when I learned a librarian was running for state representative in the 55th District, I was delighted even before I read a word of her platform. Then I read the record. Ellen Paul leads the Connecticut Library Consortium, helping more than a thousand libraries of every kind pool their buying power. And in 2025 she helped pass two state laws: the e-book pricing law, Public Act 25-9, four years of coalition work with a Republican senator among its lead champions, and the freedom-to-read law, Public Act 25-168, which protects a library’s ability to carry the Bible as surely as any book someone else would remove.
Our current representative voted against the e-book bill, and against the budget act carrying the freedom-to-read provisions.

Ellen Paul is a candidate who has never held office but spent years on Congressman Joe Courtney’s staff, who ran the East Hampton library when it won a statewide excellence award, and who, as a legislative outsider, helped deliver two state laws. A librarian on the ballot! I can’t stop asking myself, “How did we get so lucky?”
I have spent a lifetime being handed the right book at the right moment. On November 3, I get the chance to hand something back. (ellenforstaterep.com)
bills: PA 25-168 (2025): state budget incl. freedom to read

letters.headline: Voting for Weir
paragraphs: I had the pleasure of meeting Steve Weir many years ago while I served as voluntary Senior Coordinator for Andover seniors. During those years I watched him become more and more involved with the town, including our seniors. He has served the town of Andover in a knowledgeable and caring way. Steve is not the type of man that brags about what he has accomplished but just goes about doing what he believes is in the best interest of the towns he represents. Steve always comes to the events held in town whatever the cause, talks with many people to get their ideas and opinions on various subjects. For years when the seniors needed money to hold weekly lunches and there was no money in the budget, Steve appeared and supported us with whatever needed to be done. He attends meetings and voting days in Hartford and does not quickly vote ‘yes’ or ‘no’ on any issue. Steve reads everything and gives the best answer that will help all residents.
I will be casting my vote for Steve Weir in November and urge all of you to do so. Thank you.

letters.headline: Votes Against Protecting CT Vulnerable Citizens
paragraphs: In their August letters, Mr. Sauyet and Ms. Wilkinson pointed us to Rep. Weir’s actual record for District 55. Woefully, Rep. Weir voted against Senate Bill 397 and House Bill 8004, too, which all together were passed to protect Connecticut citizens against ongoing federal law enforcement abuses: banning masks, limiting courthouse arrests, empowering civil lawsuits against abusive force, and limiting private data dissemination.

After reaching out when the federal government first began militarizing law enforcement in early 2025, I have had multiple pleasant but pointed conversations with our representative; still, he did not vote for these protections. Our community deserves vision, discretion, and courage in defending our Hebron freedoms.
bills: SB 397 (2026): limits on federal immigration enforcement

letters.headline: Who Is Ellen Paul?
letters.note: Dunn is co-chair of the Marlborough Democratic Town Committee, but said she is speaking as an individual.
paragraphs: Who is Ellen Paul? Why is she running to unseat a conservative Republican State House incumbent whose voting record demonstrates ineffectiveness? Why is she gaining momentum in the 55th District? And what has she done to enrich the lives of people in Connecticut?

Ellen Paul is the Democratic candidate for state representative in the 55th District, which includes Hebron, Andover, Marlborough, and parts of Glastonbury and Bolton. She is a librarian by profession, a mother of two elementaryschool children who attend public schools, and a Glastonbury resident.

Ellen Paul is no newcomer to Hartford or to the legislative process. For more than 30 years, the voice of the 55th District has been compromised when its representative has not been part of the majority party. Ellen believes the district deserves a representative who will be heard in Hartford and who can help ensure that the concerns and priorities of the 55th District are part of a successful legislative process.

She has already demonstrated that she knows how to turn ideas into action. Ellen has shepherded legislation through the legislative process – from transforming policy ideas into legislation, to understanding the critical importance of committee work, educating decision-makers and stakeholders, and ultimately celebrating the passage of laws that benefit Connecticut’s libraries.

Ellen is a librarian who brings people together. As executive director of the Connecticut Library Consortium, she has worked with more than 1,000 libraries across Connecticut – including public, school, and college libraries – to enhance services and save taxpayers money.

And Ellen is not simply talking about representing the 55th District—she is already out listening to its residents. Look for her at community events. As of September 1, she has knocked on more than 2,000 doors, meeting residents and hearing their concerns, ideas, and hopes for the future.

She is preparing to bring those voices to Hartford and turn the concerns and visions of people in the district into action and, where appropriate, legislation. Ellen wants to meet and hear from as many residents of the 55th District as possible. Her website, ellenforstaterep.com, provides more information about her background, priorities and positions on the issues.
A vote for Democrat Ellen Paul is a vote for the voice of the 55th to be heard in Hartford!

letters.headline: Real-World Experience
paragraphs: As a UConn student entering my third year of school, it’s now time to start thinking about getting possible internships. When looking for internships, I know it is vital to connect and talk with as much people as possible. A few months ago, state Rep. Steve Weir had approached me about a connection that could possibly lead to landing an internship. He had already known that I had aspirations of becoming a pilot and understood I have a passion for aviation. After a few texts and phone calls back and forth, I got connected to one of his connections at Bombardier.

All of this ultimately led to a tour at Bombardier’s facility at Bradley International Airport in Windsor Locks. While at the facility, I gained insight about the company’s history, values, and future plans for Bombardier as a whole. I experienced first-hand Bombardier’s Hartford maintenance hangars and learned about their procedures and processes when repairing business aircraft. Now I will be connected with someone internally at bombardier and I am one step closer to landing a position that I am passionate about.

One thing I appreciate with elected officials is experience outside of government and I believe that Rep. Weir embodies this well. Steve had his own lawn care business, worked in real estate and has many other experiences from outside of politics. Real-world experience matters to me in politics because having it shows that he was just like you or I. In my case he was once 20 years old and trying to see what he wanted to do with his life, and it ultimately worked out, which is encouraging for me. I believe without those experiences he wouldn’t have built the connection network that he has today, and I wouldn’t have been able to begin my journey in working in the aviation industry.
I would like to personally thank Mr. Weir for this opportunity and his commitment to helping his constituents.

letters.headline: Weir for Entire Community
paragraphs: I first met Steve Weir shortly after moving to Marlborough in May of 2024. My first interaction with Steve was entering my driveway on a scooter. He was informing district members and handing out pamphlets regarding the upcoming election. Through friends I was formally introduced to Steve. He treated me like his own neighbor – friendly, honest and straightforward. Since 2024 I have met with Steve many times. We both share the same passion of aviation, which allowed me to get to know him further.

During the Hurricane Helene disaster, he and I flew from Connecticut in a Hughes 500A to provide lifesaving airlift capabilities. That eighthour flight from Connecticut to just north of Asheville, N.C., allowed me time which many of his voters will never have access to. Throughout the trip we flew approximately 25 hours; just him, myself and the mission. I got to know about him, his past, his family and his aspirations and why he continues public service.

I can say without a doubt regardless of which political affiliation you vote for, Mr. Weir is for our entire community. I have watched him fight for our district and state in Hartford firsthand. He reads each bill to ensure our word is reflected in legislation. He cares deeply for our community, and is putting in long hours each day, every night taking work home with him to ensure our voices are heard. I have many other examples of why I trust Steve. If you see me around town just say hello; I would be happy to share.

letters.headline: Weir’s the Way
letters.note: Hjulstrom is a member of the Marlborough Board of Finance, but said he is speaking as an individual.
paragraphs: We need to return Steve Weir to Hartford as our state representative for the 55th District. Steve has proven himself to be a tireless advocate for the towns of Marlborough, Andover, Hebron and parts of Bolton and Glastonbury. Our small towns need a strong voice speaking out for our interests. Steve is that person.

Steve Weir is a former police officer and is currently a small business owner. Steve knows how critical it is to create an environment that promotes a Connecticut where people can thrive and feel safe. In times when so many young people and retirees are leaving Connecticut, we need to address the issues that will encourage people to stay here rather than fleeing to other states with lower taxes and a lower cost of living.

Steve has the energy and dedication needed to take our message to the State House and is committed to fighting for us. But first, Steve needs us to fight for him. Steve needs your vote in November to reelect him as our state representative for the 55th House District. I will be supporting Steve. I am asking you to do the same.
PS: If you see a really tall guy going door to door while riding a scooter, say hello. You’ll be glad you took the time to chat with him.

letters.headline: Votes with Integrity!
paragraphs: Steve Weir votes with integrity! When presented with the budget document, hundreds of pages long, after midnight, for a vote the next day, he found that special interest bills were added into the document. Many of these bills were completely unrelated to budget issues (the legislation at hand), hadn’t had proper discussion, and were things that should have been heard on the house floor. Because there was not proper time to look at the impacts of all of the bills that were added into the budget legislation, and these additions didn’t go through proper democratic routes, he voted ‘no.’

It was not that he voted against our towns getting the money that was included in the budget, he was in favor of that. It was that there were too many special interests and unknowns, many of which might not have been in the best interest of his constituents, that legislators were just trying to push through without due diligence. (The system and process are broken!)

Steve’s personal experiences, being a former police officer, building his own small business from scratch, and family experiences as public school teachers, give him a very well-rounded perspective. Before you make your decision on how to vote in the next election, please look at where Steve stands on issues, and if you don’t agree with a vote, don’t jump to conclusions; take a few minutes to reach out to him and ask him about it.

letters.headline: Supports Weir
paragraphs: I am writing to express my support for Steve Weir in his reelection bid for state representative.

My first contact with Steve came when I reached out to him about an issue affecting the customers of a nonprofit organization that I run. Since then, I have had the opportunity to see firsthand his willingness to listen to everyone he meets and his genuine interest in understanding people’s concerns.

Steve has always been open about his voting record and willing to explain the reasons behind his votes. I appreciate that transparency and his willingness to engage in thoughtful conversation, even on issues where people may have different perspectives.
I also see how hard Steve works on behalf of the people he represents, and I am impressed by his dedication and commitment to serving his community.
For these reasons, I am pleased to offer my support for Steve Weir in his reelection bid.

letters.headline: I’m Supporting Weir
paragraphs: I have known Steve Weir for more than 25 years. We have been neighbors and family friends since Steve and his family moved to Hebron in 2000, and over those years I have gotten to know Steve not just as our state representative, but as a neighbor, friend and someone I know I can count on.

I have operated a dairy farm for almost my entire life, and farming comes with its share of challenges. Steve understands many of the issues farmers face, from the cost of doing business and finding reliable labor to protecting farmland and keeping farms viable for the next generation. He has helped me personally on the farm (once or twice rather memorably when he helped me corral some cows that escaped to the road), and I know he has been a strong advocate in Hartford for farmers, agriculture and farmland preservation.

More importantly, Steve is accessible. When I have a question or problem, I can call, text or email him and know he will respond. Recently, I had concerns about an invasive weed affecting my crops. Steve got involved and worked with both the Department of Agriculture and DEEP to help me get answers. That’s the kind of representation I appreciate.

Our relationship goes well beyond politics. Steve and I have attended the same church and served together on the Board of Trustees and Building Committee. I’ve seen firsthand his willingness to volunteer, help others and follow through on his commitments.

After more than 25 years as his neighbor and friend, I know Steve to be reliable, hardworking, accessible and trustworthy. He has always been there when I needed a hand, and I am proud to support Steve Weir for another term as our state representative.

letters.headline: Steve Shows Up
letters.note: U.S. Army Recon, Hebron
paragraphs: I am writing this letter to recognize Steve Weir and the impact he has had on my life. Throughout my time in the Army, Steve has been someone I have been able to look up to, learn from, and rely on for guidance. He has helped me become a better soldier, but more importantly, he has helped me become a better man.

Steve has been there for me during some of the hardest moments of my life. After losing my father, I was going through a difficult time and needed someone to help guide me. Steve stepped in when he didn’t have to. He had no obligation to be there for me, but he chose to be. He gave me advice, support, and guidance when I needed it most. He became someone I could turn to for direction and someone who genuinely cared about how I was doing.

Steve has also given me opportunities to see what true public service looks like. He invited me to the Connecticut State Capitol, where I was able to see firsthand the work that goes into serving the people of the state. Being able to experience that with him gave me a different perspective on leadership and public service.

From serving as a police officer to serving as a state representative, Steve has consistently dedicated himself to helping others. He leads by example and has taught me the importance of integrity, hard work, responsibility, and doing the right thing even when nobody is watching.

My Army career has come with challenges, but Steve has always encouraged me to keep pushing forward and hold myself to a higher standard. The lessons he has taught me are things I will carry with me throughout my military career and the rest of my life.

I am extremely grateful for everything Steve has done for me. He stepped up during a time when I needed someone, and I will never forget that. His guidance, support, and example have helped shape the person I am today. I truly believe I am a better man because of him.

letters.headline: Seniors, Be Aware!
paragraphs: I have been living in Marlborough for more than 50 years. Being a retiree on a fixed income, I worry about the future as our taxes continue to rise significantly every year. In reviewing the outcomes from the most recent government sessions I was alarmed to see that our state representative from the 55th district, Steve Weir, voted to reject $630,000 in state aid to our district. I do not understand why Steve would have rejected any funds which would help our town. He may not be concerned about cost but most seniors are. Thankfully, he failed to prevent this economic aid from returning to the taxpayers of our towns but I am concerned that we will not be so fortunate in the future,

As we continue to watch difficult municipal budgets force small towns, in particular, to struggle with rising property taxes and an increasing population of retired seniors, we need to ensure that our representatives in Hartford are fighting to bring tax dollars back to our district. Seniors, in particular, should insist that our interests are being represented as taxes rise and towns are forced to bear the burden.

For this reason I am asking that people vote for Ellen Paul! We need a change and we need it now! Ellen Paul is young, enthusiastic and she has the energy and commitment to make sure that the needs of retired people are not forgotten. She is new to public service and is willing to run because she knows we need a change and she knows we need it now! In her platform, she states, “Elected office should be public service, not a lifetime job or an opportunity for personal profit. I support reasonable term limits, banning elected officials from trading individual stocks while in office, and requiring legislators to hold regular public town halls in the communities they represent.”
