I don’t know how anyone could not agree with Ellen’s position! We seniors have more than paid our share in taxes over our lifetimes and now is not the time to bypass any monies which will help to reduce our taxes. Please support seniors by voting for Ellen Paul.

letters.headline: Steve Weir for State Rep
paragraphs: It is my distinct pleasure to endorse Steve Weir for another term as our state representative for the 55th district, which includes Andover, Hebron, Marlborough, and portions of Glastonbury and Bolton.

I have known Steve since he moved to my town of Hebron 26 years ago, coming from adjacent Glastonbury. In those ensuing years, he and his family have become embedded in our town’s daily lives, embracing the best that our community has to offer. He has been involved in town government, serving as a member of the Zoning Board of Appeals. He also served as chairman of Gilead Congregational Church’s Board of Trustees.

In the greater picture, he has created several businesses, including one, a successful restoration company, that created over 50 jobs for its employees when it was sold in 2022. In 2011, he was named the Business Person of the Year for the Connecticut River Valley Chamber of Commerce. Also, he has been a police officer in the past, a profession woefully underappreciated.

To those who would criticize Steve’s vote on some certain topic, I understand completely, because I’ve been there. As my town’s first selectman, I sometimes had to make decisions that were necessary, but not universally popular. He does his homework in order to cast an informed vote. Steve has a remarkable 100% attendance rate in Hartford over his four years in office, showing his commitment to his constituents.

For years I was the recipient of his daughter Meredith’s venture in growing food items; she would deliver to my doorstep each week wholesome fresh vegetables, eggs, and blueberries. That’s Steve at his best, rearing his children to be productive members of our society, embracing the work ethic. He even formalized the arrangement by incorporating it as Gilead Hill Farm, LLC to show his daughter the business end.

In January of this year, being a veteran, I attended the Connecticut Veterans Hall of Fame induction in Rocky Hill. Each year, only 10 to 14 veterans are chosen for this honor. To my surprise and delight, Steve was there to witness the ceremony, important to our state’s veterans.
Steve Weir has shown all of us that he has been dedicated to serving our communities with diligence, integrity, and thoughtfulness. Please vote for him on Nov. 3.

letters.headline: The Leadership Our Community Deserves
letters.note: Wilkinson is a member of the Marlborough Democratic Town Committee but said she is speaking as an individual.
paragraphs: A recent letter from an Andover resident brought back a vivid memory from when I was a single mom raising my son.

My mother and I introduced him to the wonder of stories almost as soon as he could sit. The library became our weekly oasis. We would leave with an armful of books – far more than the “one or two” books I heard other parents allowing their children. We knew we’d be back the following week for more. And when we exhausted our local library’s shelves, our library card opened the doors to neighboring towns.
That experience taught me something I never forgot: libraries are investments in people.
That is why I am so enthusiastic about Ellen Paul for state representative in the 55th District.

As executive director of the Connecticut Library Consortium, Ellen has spent her career helping libraries serve their communities better – connecting people with information and resources, strengthening programs, supporting lifelong learning, and responding to the changing needs of the people they serve.
Those are not just library skills. They are leadership skills.

Ellen knows how to listen, bring people together, stretch resources, solve problems and turn community needs into action. Most importantly, she understands that government should work for the people it represents – not the other way around.
We need that kind of leadership in Hartford.

I urge voters in Andover, Bolton, Glastonbury, Hebron and Marlborough to take a serious look at Ellen Paul. Visit ellenforstaterep.com, and don’t just take my word for it – email Ellen at ellen.a.paul@gmail.com. Ask questions. Hear what she believes and what she will fight for.
I believe Ellen Paul has the experience, values and leadership our district needs, and I strongly urge you to support her for state representative.

letters.headline: Who’s Defending Weir’s Voting Record?
letters.note: Golfin is co-vice chair of the Marlborough Democratic Town Committee and a member of the RHAM Board of Education, but is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: Many letters have appeared supporting Steve Weir for 55th District Representative. Most of these have focused on Weir’s personal qualities and his attendance at votes. But none that I can recall defend Weir’s voting record. Where is the substance on his term in office?

Several letters critical of Weir’s performance have specifically detailed his votes that are difficult to understand. I, and I’m sure many other voters, would like to know why he voted against money for our towns, voted ‘no’ to banning child marriage, and the rationale for other problematic votes that have been questioned in prior letters to the editor. On the troublesome voting record that has been raised in these pages, the only response we see is that Steve is a hardworking family man who reads the bills in their entirety and shows up for every vote. But why does he vote the way he does?

In his own letter to the editor asking to continue his tenure in the House, he states that he believes that listening to different perspectives and finding common ground are important legislative qualities, but then why run out the clock on a session to prevent action on a bill? That doesn’t sound like common ground.

Some might say that Weir won’t vote for a bill that he has thoroughly researched and has provisions he can’t support. If that results in no vote after no vote and no productive legislation to his name, then that’s not how representative government works. We all must compromise and so it is with legislation. If every bill had to have unanimous support, with every member agreeing with every detail of the legislation, nothing would get done and it seems clear that Weir hasn’t done much.
So, in future letters to this paper supporting Weir, I’d like to see some specific explanation of his voting record and how it supports the communities of the 55th.

letters.headline: Weir Is My Choice
paragraphs: I’ve noticed an interesting pattern in the recent letters to the editor supporting and opposing candidates for the 55th State House District.

The letters supporting Steve Weir seem to come largely from everyday residents – neighbors, community members and voters who aren’t typically involved in party politics. Meanwhile, many of the letters attacking him have come from people closely involved with one political party or its local town committees.
That distinction matters.

There’s nothing wrong with being active in a political party. But when the political insiders are lining up on one side and ordinary residents are speaking up on the other, I think it tells us something about the choice before us.
Do we want someone who represents a political organization, or someone willing to represent the people who actually live here?
For me, that choice is pretty clear.
If you want an independent voice for our communities at the State Capitol, vote for Steve Weir.

letters.headline: Steve Weir: A Personal Perspective
letters.note: Corentin is a member of the Hebron Republican Town Committee but said she is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: As a fellow Hebron resident, I’ve gotten to know Steve Weir as more than just our state representative. He’s someone who has put down roots here, raised his family here, built businesses here, and continues to be involved in our community.

What I appreciate about Steve is that he shows up. He listens, he makes himself available, and he’s willing to have conversations with people – even when they don’t agree with him. That matters to me.

Steve brings a lot of real-world experience to his work in Hartford. He’s been a police officer, a small-business owner, an employer, a farmer, and a community volunteer. He understands what it means to work hard, meet a payroll, raise a family, and deal with the challenges that come with running a business.

I also think it’s important to look at what someone actually does rather than what people say about them. Steve has a record of being present, doing the work, and staying connected to the people he represents. The Connecticut General Assembly currently lists him as the 55th District representative and Ranking Member of the Labor and Public Employees Committee.
For me, that’s what matters most. I don’t expect to agree with anyone on every issue. But I do value someone who works hard, listens, and stands behind his decisions.
I’m proud to support Steve Weir, and I’m glad he’s representing our community.

letters.headline: Vote for Elle Paul
paragraphs: As I considered voting for the General Assembly’s 55th district Representative, Steve Weir or Ellen Paul, I did my assessment. What does the character of each candidate reveal, the vital component for anyone seeking to be public servants? There are letters praising Weir as a nice guy and dedicated. I have enough life experience to know that “nice” and “dedicated” tell me nothing about character.

I have voted for Republicans and Democrats based on character alone. Do I trust them? Are their values aligning with mine? Trustworthy? Committed to the people, especially the least of them, as Jesus said in the Sermon on the Mount. And a record of effective service.

Ellen Paul has a life of service, from serving on US Representative Joe Courtney’s staff to managing a public library to directing a nonprofit for libraries, accomplishing non-partisan legislative victories in this latter role for the libraries.
Transparency. Ellen’s organization must be transparent to receive financial support.
Steve can talk about being hard-working and independent. So what. That’s a cliché line. Our district doesn’t need a Lone Ranger. Our towns need bi-partisan and broadly collaborative representation.
I choose Ellen Paul. Effective public service. Working for the least of us. Bipartisan. Transparent.
Vote for Ellen Paul.

letters.headline: Weir Shows Up
paragraphs: I have known Steve Weir for more that 25 years, going back to 1999 when Steve and his wife Allegra bought property in Hebron and my company poured the foundation for their new home.

Over the years, I have gotten to know Steve not just through business, but simply by being involved in the same community. I have been a longtime member of the Hebron Lions Club, and if you spend enough time volunteering and attending events around Hebron, you get to know the people who consistently show up. Steve is one of those people.

Our families have crossed paths in many ways over the years. My wife Mary works at RHAM and works at the RHAM girls’ volleyball games where Steve and his family have been staples. Steve also has volunteered at RHAM career days, talking with students about careers and sharing his experiences as a local business man. That may seem like small things, but I think it says alot about a person.
Hebron has been my home for a long time. I care about this town and I believe there is value in having a state representative who genuinely knows the community and has been part of it for decades.
Steve doesn’t just represent our towns in Hartford, he’s part of our community. He shows up, he listens, and hasn’t forgotten the people and organizations he represents.
After knowing Steve for more than two decades, I am pleased to support him for another term as our state representative.

letters.headline: Weir is Focused
letters.note: Hjulstrom is a member of the Marlborough Board of Finance, but said he is speaking as an individual.
paragraphs: During Steve Weir’s time as our state representative, he has remained intently focused on the issues that impact Connecticut’s taxpayers and businesses.

You will likely hear other candidates, including Steve’s challenger, saying that they will go on the offensive to address issues with Washington and even matters that are driven by foreign affairs. However, our state representatives and state senators are limited on what they can do on a national level. So, when you hear a candidate for state office bemoaning what’s going on in Washington, it tells you that those candidates are coming forward with a personal agenda that is simply not focused on us, right here in Connecticut.

So, on Nov. 3rd, I ask you to support the candidates who will be laser focused on issues that affect us right here in Connecticut. Trust me when I say there is plenty to deal with right here at home, without getting distracted by national issues.
I am voting for Steve Weir on Election Day. Please join me and let’s keep Steve on the job in Hartford.

letters.headline: Support Ellen Paul
paragraphs: This letter is in support of Ellen Paul for the 55th House District. Ellen is bright, energetic, and serious in her quest for the 55th District. Ellen is currently the executive director of the Connecticut Library Consortium. The CLC serves a variety of libraries across the state combining library resources that help your local library continue to provide services that the community wants. The agency has saved the taxpayers around $7 million annually.

When Ellen is knocking on doors, she genuinely listens to what the people are concerned about across the district. She takes her time to interact with them. This has been a huge task for Ellen (she started in March) and she is diligent about it. She has personally knocked on over 2,000 doors. There are common themes when Ellen is speaking with and listening to voters. One of the chief themes is to find common ground between the parties. In her work at the CLC she works with countless people to resolve challenges and find the common ground for the benefit of all. She will bring this talent to the House.

Ellen’s ideas are noteworthy: energy policies that make sense and help beleaguered ratepayers, affordable housing for the middle class – firefighters, and young families, keeping Eastern Connecticut green, modernizing the Education Cost Sharing Formula so it delivers tax relief to the taxpayers, and responsible technology with appropriate guardrails.

Ellen has lived in eastern Connecticut all her life. She is aware of the needs our region has. Ellen lives in our district with her husband and two wonderful daughters. She will fight for you in the House when she wins in November.
Please vote for Ellen on Nov. 3rd.

letters.headline: Seven Letters, One Vote
letters.note: Sauyet is co-chair of the Andover Democratic Town Committee and a member of the RHAM Board of Education, but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: Last week’s Rivereast carried seven letters for Steve Weir, five from Hebron and two from Marlborough. They describe a man who answers his phone, helps a neighbor corral loose cows, and stepped in for a young soldier after his father died. I do not doubt a word of it.
Six of the seven do not name a single vote he has cast.

The seventh does, and I want to thank Cheryl Lage of Amston for it. She is the first Weir supporter I have seen take up an actual vote and make a case for it. Her account is that the budget landed after midnight, hundreds of pages long, carrying items that had never been properly debated, so he voted no. She adds that he was not voting against our towns getting the money, that he was in favor of it.

That last part is where it comes apart. A legislator has one way to be in favor of something, and it is the vote. Take her account as given: 48 Republicans faced the same stack of paper under the same clock, and 27 voted ‘yes.’ The bill passed 127 to 21 and carried $630,000 in new aid to the five 55th district towns. It came home because they voted ‘yes.’

Reasons explain a vote. They do not stand in for it. Nearly every bill is a package, and every member weighs the parts they dislike against the rest. That weighing is not a technicality that gets a vote out from under him. It is the vote. On this one he decided his objections outweighed $630,000 for his own towns.

Ms. Lage also suggests that anyone troubled by a vote should call and ask. Fair, and people have. David Olio of Amston wrote here two weeks ago that he had several pleasant conversations with our representative. The votes came out no, all the same.
A correction of my own: in August I wrote that 28 of 49 Republicans backed that budget. One member sat in the wrong caucus in my data. The right count is 27 of 48. I apologize.
One letter noted that several Weir critics are active in town committees. True, the paper prints that under my name every time; party work is why I have the roll calls at hand.
More letters are welcome. Pick a vote and make the case for it.

letters.headline: Answer Us, Steve
letters.note: Terezakis is a member of the Marlborough Democratic Town Committee, but said she is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: Recent letters endorsing state Rep. Steve Weir have repeated some comments that concern me greatly. One is his often stated 100% attendance, and the writer says, “…showing up is half the battle.” What about the other half? What about substance! What about studying both the content and the constituents he represents, their needs and preference, regardless of party?

We have seen that Steve Weir has voted no, even in opposition to his own party let alone on bills with strong bipartisan support. The letter writer says there are “other things” in the bills and you can “contact Steve and he will tell you why he voted no.” It does not appear that the writer knows why – only that she likes Steve and trusts he must have a good reason.
So, I am asking Steve Weir for specifics, now, in this public forum, so we can all understand.

Why specifically did Steve fail to allow a vote on SB274, effectively siding with property owners and not tenants? Why specifically was he in the significant minority to vote against SB1 which would and did bring much needed $630,000 into our district? Exactly what did he have against early childhood education funding? We know by now how important it is to children’s growth and development. The old and inequitable school funding formula has needed to be upgraded for years and bring relief to homeowners-why did he vote no? Why did he vote no on renewable energy? Why would he vote ‘no’ on enforcing boating laws, or on having safety fences around swimming pools? And one that I find overwhelming – why on earth did Steve Weir vote no on ending child marriage in Connecticut? The list goes on.

But the folks endorsing Steve believe he has good reasons, and somehow none of them have made it into print. So I am asking Steve. I want to see specific responses, and Rivereast is a good place to see them.
Being friendly, shaking hands, platitudes are not enough. Answer the questions, please, we all deserve to know.
Please read Ellen Paul’s platform, as I did. You will see her experience, her values, and her clearly stated positions. Go to ellenforstaterep. com, and see for yourself why the 55th needs a change.
bills: HB 5003 (2025): early childhood care and education
ECS formula modernization (no bill number cited)

letters.headline: A Voice That Makes Us Matter
letters.note: Salvador is a member of the Marlborough Democratic Town Committee, but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: What is the role of a representative? To be the voice of the people, and to support legislation that meets their needs. Steve Weir, our representative in the 55th District, has done neither. It’s time for a change!
Our voices matter and Ellen Paul cares a lot about that. She strongly believes in defending

Connecticut’s values. Ellen will bring problem-solving skills and common sense to Hartford. Ellen is concerned about homeowners bearing the costs of education and local services. She wants the state to support these costs. Her goal is to modernize the outdated formula used by the state to share in education costs, providing relief for property owners. Currently, Connecticut ranks 46th in state support for education. As a retired teacher, I’ve seen the drastic cuts in programming, increased class sizes, and lack of materials because local residents cannot shoulder the load of providing quality education to our children. Ellen Paul wants Connecticut to provide greater assistance. Weir voted against giving over $600,000 to our district. We sure can’t count on Weir’s help.

Ellen’s concern for our shrinking wallets goes beyond our property taxes. Connecticut’s utility costs are outrageous. Our rates are soaring, and the utility companies post record profits. Ellen Paul wants an energy policy that puts us first. She wants stronger oversight holding the utility companies accountable. Ellen knows energy is a necessity for people, not a luxury. What do utility costs mean to someone like Weir, who flies his own helicopter?

Reduced tax burdens and lower utility costs for homeowners would be a tremendous relief. We need a voice that will fight for this. Ellen Paul is that voice. She cares about the future for children. It’s what got her into this race in the first place. Her compassion, common sense, and drive will be a refreshing change. Her desire to collaborate lends itself well to bipartisanship.

Ellen Paul is a dynamic candidate that will finally give the 55th District a voice in Hartford. I haven’t been actively involved in politics during my lifetime. When I met Ellen and learned about her reasons for running, ability to collaborate, and desire for a better future, it motivated me to get involved in a campaign for the first time in 50 years! We need Ellen Paul.
Learn more about Ellen at www.ellenforstaterep.com and you’ll be inspired to Vote Ellen Paul in November!

letters.headline: Weir is Good for CT
paragraphs: I have known Steve Weir now for several years and find him to be hardworking, honest and dedicated to his family and his community.

I don’t have much respect for most politicians but I have to say Steve Weir is the exception. Steve is personable, hardworking and listens to everyone. He doesn’t care what your political affiliation is he wants to hear your concerns, your view on the issues that affect your life.

Steve has a strong business background so he understands the pitfalls of doing business in Connecticut. He reads every line of every bill to make sure that in its entirety it is good for the people of his district as well as for all the people/ businesses of Connecticut.
Steve Weir is good for Connecticut. Steve Weir has my whole hearted support for reelection, so he can continue to serve the people of this district and the state of Connecticut.

letters.headline: We Need Weir
paragraphs: I am writing to endorse Steve Weir for another term as our state representative for the 55th District. He has proven himself to be an outstanding resident his entire life. He was born and raised in Glastonbury and has lived in Hebron with his wife, Allegra, where they raised three daughters. He’s a former Glastonbury Police officer, a small business owner and employer and farmer, volunteer, coach husband, father and neighbor. He knows the communities he represents. He’s always willing to listen and share ideas. He has served on several boards and volunteered in many ways. Now he has gained experience as our representative.

I can’t imagine anyone more qualified to represent us again. He has a 100% attendance for House and committee votes. He reads the bills and sometimes finds unintended consequences so votes ‘no.’ If you want to know the reasons for the ‘no’ votes, you can ask him directly and he will communicate with you.

I’m sure his Democratic opponent is a fine person, in a noble profession, but being a librarian doesn’t measure up to the qualities and experience of Steve Weir. We need him to stay on the job of representing all of us in the 55th District. Please reelect him.

letters.headline: Paul Over Weir
paragraphs: I have examined the internet websites for Steve Weir and Ellen Paul, both of whom are running for Connecticut State Representative to represent Marlborough. A Steve Weir website lists his many civic volunteer activities which I think are admirable. However, one item missing on his site is the legislation he voted for as my representative in the legislature. To see what Steve had voted for, I had to turn to Ellen Paul’s website. Steve not only voted against Democratic bills but he also seems to have often voted against some proposed by his own Republican colleagues.

Rep. Weir has voted against bills that would help Marlborough, even voting against a grant to his district that would have given monies to help reduce the mill rate increases that the towns he represents experienced this last budget cycle. Ellen on her website states she would have voted differently.

Steve has indicated that one reason he didn’t vote for such bills is they contained other provisions that would have increased the state budget, a point he disagreed with. This prompts the question: why wasn’t Steve able to convince his fellow legislators to remove such provisions so he could vote for them? Ellen will have the ability to speak to her fellow majority party members to discuss any amendments she wants to make in proposed bills.

Ellen will also be a partner to my state senator, Cathy Osten, who provides some help to Marlborough such as a $30,000 grant to the fire department that Cathy was able to secure. Having Ellen as our state rep would be advantageous for Marlborough as she could work with Cathy to benefit Marlborough.

letters.headline: Paul: Self-Evident Values
letters.note: Sauyet is co-chair of the Andover Democratic Town Committee and a member of the RHAM Board of Education, but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: There are plenty of reasons to vote for Ellen Paul. Mine is simple: she shares my values. Everyone says that about their candidate, so let me be specific.

I think a fence around a backyard pool is a small price for a child not drowning. I think a decision about a pregnancy belongs to a woman and her doctor, not to the legislature. I think that when an out-of-state owner lets an apartment complex decay until thousands of tenants have to be moved out, the town where it sits should at least have known who owned it. And I think that when the state budget carries about $630,000 in new aid for Andover, Bolton, Glastonbury, Hebron, and Marlborough, you vote yes.

None of that is radical. When those questions reached the House, most of it agreed with me: 102 to 45 on pool fences, 117 to 27 on reproductive care, 127 to 21 on the budget. The tenant bill, which had passed the Senate and cleared committee without a single no vote, never got a House vote at all.

Ellen has said plainly where she stands. Decisions about reproductive health care belong to women and their doctors. Protecting children and keeping seniors safe should be the easiest votes a legislator ever casts. Our teachers, nurses, and young families need homes they can afford, and the state’s school funding formula, untouched since 2013, needs fixing so our property taxes stop covering the gap.

And she is a librarian, for heaven’s sake. Librarians belong in the same company as schoolteachers and nurses: the people who hold a town together, for modest pay, because they believe in the work. Ellen’s values turned the East Hampton library into an award-winner, then took her to the nonprofit whose contracts libraries in every Connecticut town use to purchase together, and through four years of coalition work with a Republican senator to pass the state’s 2025 library e-book law. Of the second law she helped pass that year, on the freedom to read, she said it protects a library’s ability to carry the Bible as much as books about gender identity. That is the temperament I want in Hartford.
I said she shares my values. I don’t think they are only mine. They are not Democratic values or Republican values; in these five towns they are simply ours. Vote for Ellen Paul on Nov. 3.
bills: PA 25-168 (2025): state budget incl. freedom to read

letters.headline: Seniors Need a Change
paragraphs: I am going to keep this short and to the point. We seniors deserve continued attention and a strong voice in our state government. Too often, after candidates “get elected” and “get “settled in” they forget about who elected them and the longer they are in the worse it gets! In my opinion, this is what has happened to Steve Weir. We all agree that he is a nice, very visible guy who appears at all events but we need more than that! Seniors have concerns about many things such as escalating property taxes which is at the top of the list but so too are the rising costs of living, programs that insure older adults can remain in their houses if they so choose, threats to Medicare and drug costs and a host of other issues affecting vulnerable seniors.

I believe the needs of senior citizens were not a concern for Steve Weir when he did not vote for $630,000 which would have gone to citizens in our district. Why? I guess we need to hear from him on that issue. I wonder why he voted against the majority of the Representives, Republicans and Democrats, regarding fences around pools and child marriage. Are these issues he really believes he cannot support or was he not paying attention?

Being our representative at the state level requires being more than a “nice guy!” We need someone who takes an active role in knowing what the issues are and voting appropriately even if he has been in office for a long time!

I have a lot of concerns about our future and after meeting with Ellen Paul and hearing what she hopes to accomplish when she gets into office I decided to volunteer as a driver for her as she campaigns door to door. I can assure you that I have never done this before but I feel, after having talked with her, it was time to “step up to the plate.” Totally committed to representing all the constituents in the 55th, she sincerely seeks dialogue with Republicans, Democrats, and Unaffiliates alike. She has specifics in how to reduce energy costs, and property taxes, and offers practical solutions and strong community values to all.

I am writing to express my support for Ellen Paul’s candidacy for state representative in the 55th District. I sincerely hope that you will give her a chance and join me by voting for her on Nov. 3rd!

letters.headline: I’m For Weir
paragraphs: Ive known Steve Weir for more than a dozen years now. I met Steve and his wife Allegra when our children attended the RHAM Middle School together. When I think of who I want representing our community, I honestly feel we are very fortunate to have someone like Steve. Steve has spent nearly his entire life in Glastonbury and Hebron, and understands the makeup of our district. His broad background as a Glastonbury Police officer, a volunteer on numerous community & industry boards and also a self-employed small business owner gives him unique insight into both the public and private sectors. He also has an outstanding work ethic, which is evidenced by his consistently attending community events and listening to his constituents.

I can tell you firsthand that I have seen voters on both sides show appreciation for the work Steve has done. In 2025 I ran for the Board of Selectmen and Steve and I were spending a Sunday afternoon going door to door in Hebron talking to voters. While going door to door, Steve made sure to bring me to doors of all political affiliations. I can attest that Steve enjoys broad support from Republican, Democratic and unaffiliated voters because he is willing to listen to everyone. During our walk around the neighborhood, we passed by one yard that clearly had several Democratic candidate signs. The owner called out to Steve, introduced herself and very seriously said: “We don’t always align politically, but it’s apparent from your work around the district that you listen to all and work across the aisle. We need more of that, and I appreciate your hard work.”
Steve works hard and listens to all sides, and to me that says it all. That’s why I’m voting for Steve Weir, and urging everyone I know to continue to support him in November.

letters.headline: Reelect Steve Weir
paragraphs: Have you met Steve Weir, incumbent state representative for the 55th District, yet? Most of us have, but if not, let me tell you about my friend, who you may see on his scooter, as he travels the district to meet you.

Over the years, I have knocked on hundreds of doors in Marlborough with Steve as he set out to meet his future and now current constituents. Steve wants to hear from us, learn what our important issues are, and hear your thoughts on how to make state government more efficient. He genuinely looks to connect with us all, without regard to political affiliation, Steve looks to engage and he genuinely wants to hear your concerns. So, when you see him on his scooter, he is working to be efficient and get to more of the community. This is who Steve is.

Steve and his wife have raised their family in Hebron. He was a Glastonbury Police Officer until he decided to become a small business owner and navigated the many hurdles required to do so in Connecticut for small businesses to become successful. In 2020, he helped his youngest daughter open a small farm at their home which has grown considerably to even include poultry and operating year-round. What began as a school project with his daughter evolved into helping her learn how to build, grow and diversify a business. He brings this experience and practical know how to Hartford. This is who Steve is.

Steve is ever-present in our community frequenting local businesses who know him by name. You will see him at Eagle Scout ceremonies (he was one himself), MVFD Annual Chicken BBQ, Marlborough Day, and the Hebron Fair, to name just a few. He is always talking to someone. Steve is accessible to you because he knows representing his constituents is his responsibility. This is who Steve is.

Over the past four years, Steve has represented us well in Hartford. He is respected by his colleagues, on both sides of the aisle, as someone who is fair, hardworking and smart. If you have not met Steve, I encourage you to reach out or just look for the guy on the scooter – engage with him. See the experience he brings to this seat as our State Representative for the 55th District and send him back to Hartford for another term to serve us well.

letters.headline: Vote for Steve Weir
paragraphs: Please join me in voting for Steve Weir. I have known Steve personally for decades. Steve weighs decisions based on what is right for all the people in the district. Steve will listen first, do his ‘homework,’ then clearly articulate his position and reasoning. A solid businessman, father, husband, philanthropist, and good person, Steve is also our state representative -- let’s keep it that way.
Vote for Steve Weir.

letters.headline: Proud to Support Weir
paragraphs: Do you have that one person who comes to mind when you think about integrity and someone who truly holds themselves accountable? I certainly do, and that person is Steve Weir.

I have known Steve for just over 10 years. We first met at a conference in the multifamily housing industry and, shortly afterward, at a church event where I was a new member. Steve and I quickly became friends, and it was through that friendship that I began to realize what an impactful individual he is.

Over the years, we have both volunteered our time on the Board of Directors of the Connecticut Apartment Association, one of the many ways Steve has served through local and state organizations. What has always impressed me most about Steve is his dedication to his fellow neighbors and his commitment to giving back to the community. Somehow, he always finds the time to make it happen because I believe service is simply part of who he is. He devotes himself to making life better for the people around him.

When Steve reached out to me in 2022 and told me he would be running for state representative in the 55th District, I immediately thought, “Who could be better for this job?” To me, the answer was simple: Steve.

That is why I was proud to join him in knocking on our neighbors’ doors and talking with residents about his campaign. Four years later, Steve remains just as committed to representing the people of the 55th District. I still see him pounding the pavement, knocking on doors and speaking directly with his constituents.

What stands out to me is that Steve genuinely listens. It doesn’t matter what your political affiliation is – he takes the time to hear people’s concerns and values their opinions on the important issues facing our community. That willingness to listen, combined with his years of service to others, is something I believe is essential in a public servant.

I am writing to the Rivereast News Bulletin to express my full support for Steve Weir. He is someone I respect and look up to in many ways, and I have had the privilege of seeing firsthand the kind of person he is when no one is asking him to be.

I began this letter by talking about integrity, and I want to close by returning to that word. Steve’s integrity and character are not just qualities he talks about – they are qualities he demonstrates through his actions and his commitment to the people around him.
For these reasons, I am proud to support Steve Weir and believe he would continue to serve the people of the 55th District with the honesty, accountability and dedication they deserve.

letters.headline: Please Support Weir
paragraphs: I have known Steve Weir for over 15 years, first as a customer of his restoration business, then as my constituent and now as my representative.
During the eight years that I served as a state representative from Glastonbury, I was impressed with Steve’s passion to help small businesses.

Having served in elected office myself, I know that representing a community requires much more than holding a title. It requires listening, working hard, understanding the people who you serve and being willing to support them.
All of this, Steve has demonstrated in his four years of service and now as he is seeking his third term, I request you to support him.

As an elected official, Steve is hard working and deeply committed to the community that he represents. He understands the challenges facing families and small businesses through his own personal experiences. Steve is not someone who views public service through the lens of politics. He understands what it means to run a business, employ people, raise a family and be an active member of the community.

What has always impressed me most about Steve, however, is the person behind the public role. He is family-oriented, approachable and genuinely cares about the people around him. Over more than 15 years, I have seen that commitment remain constant.
I am proud to call Steve Weir my friend and I have utmost confidence in him that he is a strong candidate to serve our community. Please support Steve this November in his election.
Prasad Srinivasan, MD
State Representative of
Glastonbury - 2010-2018
Candidate for Governor of
the State of Connecticut – 2018

letters.headline: Why I’m Running
letters.note: Candidate for State Representative. Paul is running for the 55th House District, which covers Andover, Hebron, Marlborough and parts of Bolton and Glastonbury.
paragraphs: I never expected to run for office.

I love the work I do, and I’ve been fortunate to build a career around public service. I’m a librarian, a nonprofit executive, and a former staff member for Congressman Joe Courtney. Today, as executive director of the Connecticut Library Consortium, I work with more than 1,000 libraries across our state to strengthen public services, reduce costs for taxpayers, and expand access to information.

That work has also brought me to the State Capitol, where I’ve worked with Republicans and Democrats on legislation addressing issues facing Connecticut libraries. I’ve learned firsthand that good government is still possible when people listen to one another, build consensus, and stay focused on solving problems rather than scoring political points.
But to me public service has never been only about a job.

I grew up in Mansfield and have spent my life in eastern Connecticut. Today, my husband, Steve, and I are raising our two daughters in public school. I was raised to believe that citizenship means more than voting. It means contributing to your community and that when you are in a position to make a difference, you have a responsibility to step forward.
That is why I decided to run for state representative.

I believe deeply in the values that have guided both my life and my career: respect for one another, opportunity, strong public schools, responsible government, trust in facts and expertise, and equal rights under the law.

I didn’t enter this race because I always wanted to be an elected official. I entered it because I believe public service matters, that government can still accomplish good things, and that each of us has an obligation to contribute when we can.
For me, this is my moment to step forward. I invite you to learn more about me on my website: EllenForStateRep.com

letters.headline: Reelect Steve Weir
letters.note: DeDonato is a member of the Hebron Board of Finance, but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: We have been incredibly fortunate to have Steve Weir representing the 55th District. For four years now, he has been fully dedicated to this district. From long nights in Hartford to early mornings at local events, and from supporting local fundraisers to simply being present when neighbors need a hand, Steve is constantly giving back to the towns he represents.

We need leaders who can relate to the people they serve. Leaders who understand what it is like to raise a family, pay a mortgage, buy groceries. Steve isn’t a career politician. He’s a husband and father. He’s a small business owner who built something of his own from the ground up, right here in our community. He knows what it takes to meet a payroll, and he understands the strain that rising costs and inflation have put on families and businesses. It’s part of why he’s so focused on making sure Connecticut stays affordable for all of us.

On policy, Steve keeps his priorities straight. He pushes for fiscal responsibility and transparency, has our first responders’ backs, fights for our schools and kids, and stands up for local businesses. He’s easy to find and easy to talk to — showing up around our towns and listening when people, regardless of political affiliation, bring him their concerns. With so many politicians these days stoking partisan divides, it is refreshing that we have someone who cares about all of us. That’s not biased rhetoric. He’s voted with the majority 77% of the time, which is hardly the record of someone who only shows up for his own side. It’s the record of someone reading each bill and doing what’s right for all of us, not just those who voted for him.

I have known Steve and his family for 15 years — our children grew up together — and I can tell you firsthand that his commitment to this community isn’t a campaign talking point, it’s just who he is. Connecticut needs more people like Steve fighting for our jobs, our families, and our future. Let’s send him back to Hartford and keep him working for us. Reelect Steve Weir as our state representative for the 55th District.

letters.headline: Weir the Best Choice
paragraphs: I’m writing this letter in support of Steve Weir for his reelection to the Connecticut House of Representatives for the 55th District. I’ve known Steve for almost 30 years, and I have witnessed his genuine care and concern for people throughout our community.

Steve has a wonderful ability to really listen to people and care about their concerns. While he was at GPD, we regularly saw Steve at the Apple Fest in Glastonbury each year, and he would always know my name and my daughter’s’ names and was interested to know what we were doing and how he could help. Steve listens to all sides of a matter, whether you are a Democrat or Republican, and he will support the commonsense approach, regardless of party affiliation. We need this kind of thinking in our representatives!

I’ve witnessed Steve grow from a small business owner to a police officer, a realtor, owner/ president of American Integrity Restoration, and now to running his own farm with his daughter, Gilead Hill Farm, LLC. As a small business owner myself, I’m happy to have Steve on my side. Small businesses are generally treated poorly in the State of Connecticut, but Steve advocates for policies that will support business owners – not punish them!

Steve’s family has many roots in the education of children. He supports our local schools and school choice, believing that a school system should work for the family and the child. He’s also brought his helicopter to local schools, wanting to share his love and passion for flying with the next generation.
Steve is also a great family man. He participates in projects with his children and he is always there for them. He’s involved in his local church and is a volunteer and servant for local charities.

I normally don’t get involved in politics but knowing Steve for so long I feel confident that he is the best choice for the job. And I’ve never heard of a state representative that has a 100% voting record for all four of his years in the legislature! Steve shows up and he is well informed. I urge everyone to get out to the polls and vote for Steve Weir.

letters.headline: Where Are the Answers?
paragraphs: In the Sept. 18th edition of the Rivereast , Ann Terezakis asked pointed questions of Steve Weir to explain his voting record. We all know Steve is there 100% of the time to vote, but how he votes is concerning to the taxpayers in his district. I was expecting answers to her questions from Steve this week. Instead, one of the support letters for Steve asked people to, “ask Steve himself and he will tell you the answers.” Seriously?

Steve should be able to articulate his answers to these questions in a written response to the Rivereast . Everyone says that Steve is a great guy with integrity. If so, why would we as voters have to track him down for the answers? That doesn’t seem to be right.
As a man who is purportedly a “good listener,” why is he not answering the question?

letters.headline: No Guessing with Paul
letters.note: Lawrence is vice chair of the Hebron Town Council, but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: When looking at the choices for our representative in Hartford on Nov. 3, Ellen Paul has already made her case clear. Her website goes issue by issue through the bills that have reached the House, on schools, housing, energy, and reproductive care, and says how she will vote when they come back. As she says, “you won’t have to guess.” That is the representative I want.

Contrast this clear platform with the case for Steve Weir as his supporters have made it in these pages: He shows up. He listens. He works hard. He cares. He’s honest. He reads every bill. He listens to everyone. He shows up. That is a great deal of praise, but something is missing.

On Sept. 4, Chesney McOmber of Andover counted eight letters praising Mr. Weir since mid-July and found that not one defended a single vote he had cast. That seemed like an invitation his supporters would take up, so I counted what came next. From that issue through last week, 23 letters praised him. One names a vote and defends it: Cheryl Lage’s, on this spring’s budget adjustment. The other 22 do not mention a vote at all.

Over the same four weeks, 10 letters critical of him named Weir’s specific votes: the budget (against), safety fences around pools (against), ending child marriage (against), early childhood funding (against), renewable energy (against). The letters for him named his family, his farm, his church, his business, his scooter, his helicopter. Nothing in the second list is wrong. It’s just not what we send a representative to Hartford to do.

It is telling that the only people discussing his voting record are his critics. His supporters certainly aren’t shy; they have filled endless pages defending him. Yet, on this issue, they are completely silent. The closest thing to a record in all 23 letters is a supporter writing that Mr. Weir votes with the majority 77 percent of the time to prove he works across the aisle. It sounds reassuring until you realize that over his term, only seven of the 154 people who served in the House voted with the majority less often.
Ms. McOmber’s invitation still stands: pick a vote and make the case for it. But because Ellen Paul has already laid out her positions openly, I will vote for Ellen Paul on Nov. 3.
bills: HB 5003 (2025): early childhood care and education

letters.headline: We Need More Like Weir
paragraphs: As a longtime Glastonbury resident, I am extremely concerned by dramatic changes in the political landscape in Connecticut over several decades. As a registered Democrat, one might think I would celebrate the control the Democratic party has over Connecticut politics and therefore over Connecticut public policy. The truth is quite the contrary, as any government so heavily weighted as to act as an autocracy is a threat to all citizens due to the loss of honest debate and, most egregiously, the arrogance that comes from a legislative body that feels no obligation to answer to constituents.

In recent years, several bills before the legislature have deeply affected me personally and professionally. I reached out to my representatives repeatedly, as did friends and colleagues in their own communities. The only elected official who consistently responded to us was Rep Steve Weir. Other legislators failed to make even a feeble effort to comprehend the details in these bills, while Steve listened, asking questions until he had a working knowledge of the issues. Despite being just as busy as every other legislator, Steve always responded and made time to understand how proposed legislation impacted real people and businesses.

In the case of legislation affecting my profession, Steve met with our delegation and arranged for his colleagues to meet with us as well. I have no doubt that had the Democrats who ignored us entirely, including my own Senator, made the same effort, the very poor legislation we rallied against would have been defeated. Rather than dialogue, however, we were met with refusal to respond to phone calls, emails or public testimony. Elected officials who simply vote as directed by party leaders are not acting in good faith, nor are they respecting their oath to protect the Constitution of the State of CT.

Steve Weir is that very rare elected official who behaves like a representative of the people, rather than a politician. Whether guided by his own roots in the community, his experience as a successful businessperson or simply his commitment to his own family, Steve hasn’t lost sight of his responsibility to serve both the people of this community and Connecticut. We don’t need greater imbalance in the legislature; we need more representatives like Steve who are committed to service and whose obligation is to the people, rather than to a party.

letters.headline: Support Steve Weir
paragraphs: I have known Steve and his wife for over 10 years and see him often at our volleyball games. I enthusiastically endorse his re-election to the 55th District where he has served for a number of years.

I support him for a number of reasons. First and foremost, he is one of us. He has lived his life in our district, raised his family here, had a small business here and volunteered for a number of local community service endeavors. He puts our small-town values first and supports local control, which was recently threatened by House Bill 8002, which eroded local “home rule” in favor of shifting zoning to state oversight.

As a seasoned legislator he has consistently worked to increase transparency and accountability in our state government. He has been a proponent of eliminating waste, fraud and abuse as evidenced by his support of legislative reforms which included funding of an independent inspector general and stronger audits of agencies funded by the state.

He has worked consistently to reduce our electric rates which are among the highest in the nation. He has supported small business and was awarded the Connecticut Business and Industry Association (CBIA) Award for supporting business-friendly legislation.

In addition to all of the above, Steve is a friendly person, easily approachable and interested in our concerns. If you are on his mailing list, he sends a Capitol News Update which summarizes recent issues and actions and helps to keep us informed of what is occurring at our Capitol.
Please support him in November.

letters.headline: Seniors, Be Aware!
paragraphs: When evaluating Steve Weir’s job as our representative for the 55th district I decided to look beyond the “Letters to the Editor” that say what a wonderful person he is and what a great job he has done and … this is some of what I found out!

In 2023 the legislature’s Aging Committee sent a bill to the house that would have required nursing homes to report their costs honestly and to disclose when a private equity firm owns them. Not to ban anything. Just to say who owns the building where our family member is sleeping. It passed 128 to 10. Every Democrat voted ‘yes’ and 41 Republicans said ‘yes!’ Steve was one of 10 who said ‘no.’
I have to ask…Steve, “why did you vote against legislation that would help to protect senior citizens?”
The more I talk with Ellen as I drive her around knocking on doors the better I have gotten to know her, and I know she would not have voted ‘no!’
I hope you will join me by voting for Ellen Paul for the 55th District on Nov. 3rd!

letters.headline: Safer with Ellen Paul
paragraphs: I have seen too many stories lately about young children drowning in a family swimming pool. Drowning is among the leading causes of death for young children, and a fence or barrier is one of the few things that reliably stops it.
In 2024 the Connecticut House voted on exactly that: requiring safety barriers around swimming pools. It passed 102 to 45. Our representative, Steve Weir, voted ‘no’ (HB-5169, 2024).

I went looking for the principle behind that vote and instead found a pattern. He voted NO on ending child marriage in Connecticut, a bill the Senate passed without a single dissent (HB6569, 2023). He voted ‘no’ on letting the public see how nursing homes care for our parents, though his fellow Republicans supported it 4 to 1 (HB-6678, 2023). On numerous bills whose entire purpose was keeping somebody’s child or somebody’s parent safe, he found his way to vote ‘no.’

Ellen Paul, who is running for this seat, has a refreshingly ordinary way of thinking about such bills. Not every vote is a battle of ideologies, she says. Some just ask whether we protect children and keep seniors safe, and those should be the easiest votes a legislator ever casts. Her whole career, in libraries and nonprofits and coalition work, has been the patient business of making shared spaces safer and better for everyone in them.

What I need from my representative is simple: vote ‘’yes’ for bills that will keep your constituents safe. This November, the 55th can elect Ellen Paul, check out her website for more info on the difference she will make: ellenforstaterep.com .

letters.headline: Support Steve Weir
paragraphs: I’ve known Steve Weir for 32 years and he is an outstanding individual, from starting and developing and succeeding with several businesses. He served as a Glastonbury police officer, living and working with us in our community. He knows and understands how to support people. He has balanced budgets and makes common sense decisions. He has served the community in many ways; just to name a few, I have witnessed him as a volunteer basketball coach, served on the Hebron Zoning Board of Appeals, was former chairman of the CT River Valley Chamber of Commerce.
There is no better hard-working, honest, committed, reliable person than Steve Weir to represent our community. Regardless of your party, vote for Steve Weir for Connecticut House of Representatives.

letters.headline: A Decade of Trust
paragraphs: I don’t normally get involved publicly in politics. My wife and I tend to vote for the person rather than the party, and I have friends and family with a wide range of political views. But I’ve known Steve Weir and his family for more than 10 years, and I believe character still matters when deciding who we trust to represent us.

We first met the Weirs through our children’s swim activities. Over the years, that connection grew into a close friendship between our families. Steve’s daughters have babysat, coached and helped care for our son and daughter. His middle daughter has been trusted not only to watch our children, but to drive them to activities. Our beagle came to us through the dog rescue where Steve’s oldest daughter, worked, and when we’ve traveled, we’ve trusted Steve and his family to care for her.

Those may not sound like political qualifications, but they tell you something important about a person and a family. You don’t entrust your children and pets to people unless you trust their judgment, responsibility, and character.

I’ve seen those same qualities in Steve as our state representative. I have reached out to him for guidance involving a nonprofit I’m associated with, and whenever I’ve called or texted with a question, Steve has responded. He doesn’t suddenly become accessible at election time. That’s simply who I’ve known him to be. I’ve heard people describe Steve as a “nice guy,” sometimes even while disagreeing with his votes. He is a nice guy, but I think that description sells him short. He’s thoughtful, prepared, and willing to ask difficult questions. He’s not someone who follows the crowd simply because it’s easier.

I don’t expect my representative to agree with me on every issue. I expect him to listen, use good judgment, and think independently. Steve wasn’t elected to be a rubber stamp for anyone. He was elected to represent his neighbors throughout the 55th District, and sometimes that means challenging the status quo. Steve is also very aware if something in Hartford goes south I will call him out on it but that will not change our families’ strong relationship we have forged over the years.

Writing a political letter is outside my comfort zone. I’m doing it because after knowing Steve and his family for more than a decade, I’m comfortable putting my name behind what I know about him personally: his character, integrity, judgment, and commitment to the people he represents.

letters.headline: Ellen Paul for All
letters.note: Keener is a member and former chair of the Andover Democratic Town Committee, but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: I’m supporting Ellen Paul, Democratic candidate for state representative from the 55th District. The 55th District is made up of Andover, Bolton, Hebron, Marlborough, and part of Glastonbury and we have not had a Democrat representing us for as long as I can remember.

We have a great candidate in Ellen Paul. She is a librarian and the executive director of the CT Library Consortium. She has worked with the CT General Assembly to advance bipartisan legislation to protect library access to digital books and to safeguard intellectual freedom. She knows how to get things done in Hartford from the outside, and soon she can get things done from the inside as a member of the legislature.

From reading her website (ellenforstaterep. com), I find it easy to agree with her commonsense approach to the issues that face our small towns. She takes each issue and discusses what needs to be done in Hartford to help us right here in the 55th. She supports updating the Education Cost Sharing system to bring more state money to our schools that will bring our property taxes down. She supports investing in energy infrastructure that will bring our energy costs down. She wants to address affordability for young families by providing child care assistance and by making it easier to build smaller more cost-efficient housing. She wants to keep eastern Connecticut green by allowing sensible development without spoiling our beautiful landscape. Ellen has published well thought out stances on many other issues on her website.

With the Democrats being the majority party in the CT State Legislature, it can be easier to get both power and consensus on issues from a member of the Democratic party. The 55th has not had a representative from the majority party for many years. This is the year we turn the 55th blue!

letters.headline: Weir Is a Better Choice
paragraphs: Who we choose to represent us in House District 55, Glastonbury, Marlborough, Andover, Bolton and Hebron, seems to come down to two different philosophies. One recognizes laws, once enacted, have long lives, and unintended consequences. The income tax and the bottle bill are two, but there are others. The other says let’s pass laws that look good for the party in power in return for a vote to get money from the state for projects – even un-needed ones. Our town and others just got substantial grants for transportation projects. You’re thinking light rail, bus-ways, a new road, an added lane – nope, it’s going to fund...culverts.
One could fill every page of this paper with a list of the taxes, mostly hidden, Connecticut residents are forced to pay. Working great for us, aren’t they?
Steve Weir represents a better choice for us, I think.

letters.headline: Taxes and Education
paragraphs: After knocking on more than 2,500 doors across our district, one concern comes up again and again: property taxes.

People want excellent schools. They also want to be able to afford to stay in their homes. Those two things should not be in conflict, but the way Connecticut funds public education too often puts them there.

Education is one of the largest expenses in our municipal budgets. In communities like ours, much of that burden ultimately falls on individual homeowners. When education costs rise and state support does not keep pace, towns face difficult choices: raise property taxes, cut school programs, or reduce other municipal services.
Connecticut needs to make funding local education a much higher priority within the state budget.

I am not talking about raising state taxes. I am talking about how we prioritize the money the state already spends. I cannot think of a more impactful investment Connecticut could make than sending more education funding back to our communities. It strengthens our schools while relieving pressure on local property taxpayers.

One place to start is the Education Cost Sharing formula. Its foundation amount, intended to represent the cost of educating a student before other factors are considered, has remained $11,525 since 2013. The actual cost of educating our children has not.

Making the state’s investment in local education a priority would be my first, second and third priority in Hartford. We should update our funding system to reflect what education actually costs today and make sure the state is carrying its fair share.

But we should also be willing to ask a bigger question. Connecticut relies heavily on local property taxes to pay for public education. We may be the Land of Steady Habits, but sometimes a longstanding habit deserves another look.
At the doors, I hear both sides of this equation. People deeply value our schools, and they are worried about whether they can continue to afford their property taxes.
We should not have to choose between strong schools and affordable communities. If the state makes education the priority it should be, we can work toward both.

letters.headline: Protecting Your Right to Vote
letters.note: Vrooman is a member of the Marlborough Democratic Town Committee, but she said she is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: Voting is not only a right; it is a privilege and a responsibility! Therefore, why does Steve Weir want to hinder our access to voting?

Early Voting passed the House 107-35 after voters had approved the constitutional amendment. In essence, Weir voted against what your neighbors already voted for at the ballot box. He is supposed to fight for what his constituents want. That is the job of an elected representative and Ellen Paul has taken a clear position on this.

“When Connecticut voters amended our constitution to allow early voting. They gave the legislature a job: carry it out. That’s the basic promise of self-government. When the people decide, their representatives follow through. I trust the voters of this district. I’ll work to make voting secure, accessible, and convenient for every eligible voter, and I will never vote to make participating harder.”
(Quote by candidate Ellen Paul)

letters.headline: Ellen’s Credentials Check Out
letters.note: Sauyet is co-chair of the Andover Democratic Town Committee and a member of the RHAM Board of Education, but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: I keep seeing one question about Ellen Paul, the Democratic candidate for state representative in the 55th District: what qualifies a librarian to serve in Hartford?

The honest answer is that no job qualifies anyone. Connecticut has a citizen legislature. Its members serve part-time and come from ordinary working lives on purpose, so the people writing our laws also live under them. There is no credential for the job, and there shouldn’t be.

Our current representative runs a restoration company, owns commercial real estate, and flies helicopters. That is honest work, and I don’t doubt he is good at it. But none of it is more training for writing state law than a library degree. The real question is what each person brings.

A good librarian brings a method: find the best information, check it, organize it so others can use it, and listen closely enough to learn what people actually need. She also brings the habit of stretching a thin budget. The Connecticut Library Consortium, which Ellen has led since 2022, gets a state grant of $124,402 a year, down from $350,000 a decade earlier, and estimates that its contracts save libraries and taxpayers over $7 million a year.

And then there is this librarian. Ellen spent four years working with Republican Sen. Tony Hwang, on a library e-book bill, testifying and building a coalition until it passed the Senate 35 to 1 in 2025. Steve Weir voted ‘no.’ That same year she helped write the freedom-to-read protections that became law in the state budget.

In fairness, individual members’ bills rarely pass in Hartford, in either party. Laws get made the way Ellen made hers, through years of work across the aisle. Weir has filed 41 bills of his own in four years, and none reached a floor vote. The clearest case I can find of him steering an outcome came on the last night of the 2026 session, when he and a few allies threatened to run out the clock on SB 274, a tenant-safety bill that had already passed the Senate. It died. He sits on the board of the Connecticut Apartment Association, whose president testified against it.

So what qualifies a librarian to serve in Hartford? She’s already done the job’s hardest part from outside the building. Weir is kind and hard-working. Ellen is too, and she has two laws to show for it.

letters.headline: Ellen Paul for Families

letters.headline: Weir Brings Balance
paragraphs: I am writing to support Steve Weir’s reelection, as representative of the 55th District, to the Connecticut House of Representatives. Our needs and interests deserve Steve’s representation. Steve is very happy to engage with anyone, to explain issues, and to explain his voting record.
Vote the entire Republican ballot, to bring common sense to Hartford and to all of Connecticut!!

letters.headline: A Real Voice for Change
paragraphs: It wasn’t that long ago that the division in Washington was far removed from our Connecticut towns. It didn’t matter much what party our local politicians were from. We voted for the quality of the person – Republican, Democrat or Independent. Sadly, times have changed. The state’s Republican politicians are now beholden to those controlling Washington.

Steve Weir is by all accounts a nice guy – but is that enough to reward Republicans by sending him back to Hartford? Republicans have represented the 55th since 1981. How has that loyalty been repaid?
Steve’s voting record tells us where his priorities lie:
• Voted ‘no’ to help seniors stay in their homes (SB-1, 2026).
• Voted ‘no’ to increase housing options (HB5288, 2026).
• Voted ‘no’ to keep medical debt private (SB395, 2024).
• Voted ‘no’ to improve sick leave (HB-5005, 2024).
• Voted ‘no’ to expand early-childhood education (HB-5003, 2025).
• Voted ‘no’ to diversify energy production (HB-5340, 2026).
• Voted ‘no’ to end childhood marriage (HB6569, 2023).
Here’s the good news: This November we have a real voice for change on the ballot.
Ellen Paul is an experienced, sensible, independently-minded candidate who actually wants to put working families first.
Paul supports affordable housing without hurting the rural landscapes that make our towns beautiful. She also supports property tax relief for older homeowners and help for renters .
Paul supports oversight, accountability, and a diversified energy portfolio to help combat surging fuel prices.
Paul supports our workers, including paid sick days, family leave and labor rights.

Elections have consequences, and you can see those consequences right now, every time you get your electric bill or pay for groceries. The Republican Party in Connecticut must be sent a clear message that we want them serving us, not Washington. That includes Steve Weir.
Please vote this November, and if you are independently-minded and want to support someone who will represent you – not a political party – vote Ellen Paul.

letters.headline: Future of Local Education
letters.note: Marlborough Resident & Educator
paragraphs: As a Marlborough resident and mother to a young son who will start school in just a couple of years, I care deeply about the future of local education. While I teach in a neighboring district, my professional experience and my personal stake as a parent remind me daily that strong public schools are the backbone of our town. You do not need a child in the classroom to share that stake, either. Top-notch schools protect local home values, attract young families, and keep our community economically healthy for every resident.

Keeping our schools strong requires leaders in Hartford who will actually vote to support them. In my classroom, if a student brings home a 52%, that is an F on any grading scale. Yet that is the exact score state Rep. Steve Weir earned on the Connecticut Education Association scorecard after repeatedly voting against key education measures and state budget adjustments (SB 1) that directed vital aid to our area. While voting against state spending is often framed as fiscal conservatism, for small towns like ours, rejecting state aid does not save taxpayers a dime. When Hartford turns away education funding, local operating costs do not magically disappear; the financial burden is simply passed directly to local property taxpayers, or our schools are forced to make tough cuts. You can review his full documented voting record for yourself at cea.org/legislator-reportcard.

Our community deserves representation that reflects our shared investment in local public education, which is why I am supporting Ellen Paul for state representative. Ellen understands that securing our fair share of state funding is a direct investment in our town’s financial health that protects both our schools and local homeowners.

From our children’s education to our home values, every single resident benefits when our public schools succeed. Based on his recorded votes, Steve Weir simply hasn’t earned a passing grade. I urge my neighbors across the 55th District to join me in voting for Ellen Paul.

letters.headline: Weir Is What We Need
paragraphs: When I think about who I want to represent our community, I want someone who lives in and understands our community. Steve Weir is a strong example of that person. He has lived and worked in our community his entire life. His life experiences run the gamut. From being a police officer to starting two successful small businesses, Steve has the vision and perseverance to grow an idea into reality. I have never seen Steve back down from a challenge. This is a testament of his problem-solving skills, a skill that he learned and honed while building and running his small businesses. He is exactly what we need to represent our thoughts, ideas and voices in Hartford.
I hope that you, the reader, strongly consider voting for Steve Weir this November.

letters.headline: I’m Voting for Ellen
paragraphs: There have been a lot of letters recently saying what a great guy Steve Weir is. I have met him and yup, he is nice, friendly; I am sure he is a great guy. But a great guy doesn’t necessarily get things done.

Steve turns up and votes, but does he vote in the interest of our small town of Hebron? During this year’s legislative session, Steve voted against substantial aid in the form of $630,000 to help our budget. Why on earth would he turn down the money we need? Steve voted consistently to protect landlords from being regulated so they couldn’t abuse tenants’ rights. Really? Steve voted ‘no’ to protect the rights of citizens to file lawsuits against abuse by federal agents within our state. He voted against a digital privacy bill aimed at protecting children when using online platforms. Why would he not want to protect children? He voted against a healthcare regulation addressing emergency medical services and specific standards of care for pregnant women. Are you kidding me?

Ellen Paul is advocating for modernizing Connecticut’s Education Cost Sharing formula, aiming to fix the disparities where a child’s quality of education is strongly related to their zip code. She is looking to lower energy and electric bills – we all need that – as well as help senior citizens on fixed incomes lower overall cost-ofliving burdens. She supports expanding affordable housing – maybe our young people could actually afford to stay in town if more reasonably priced housing was available. She supports strengthening protections for workers and fair labor practices.

In these turbulent times, where we see our First Amendment rights under threat, Ellen stands for protecting those rights, expanding voting access and having guardrails to protect us from advanced technologies. With all the open space and great trails Hebron is blessed with, she also supports protecting our green spaces and environment.
So though Steve may be a nice guy, I will be voting for Ellen and I urge you to vote for her too.

letters.headline: The Librarian vs. The Naysayer
paragraphs: Thinking about my experiences with libraries I realize I could write an essay. From toddler to senior, I doubt a week has gone by without library time. I love and respect libraries, and I love and respect my local Richmond Memorial Library.

As we enter Banned Books Week (I cannot believe I have had to write that phrase in my America!), I am reflecting on librarians and what they do. From my own experience, the short version: old and new books, movies, digital books; help with my iPhone, iPad, and computer; library of games indoor and outdoor, to borrow; arts and crafts for all ages; space to study, read, write, research; educational lectures; cookbook club in conjunction with senior center; book clubs offering both friendship and close reading; grants for programs such as Books for Babies; pajama time to nurture little ones love of reading; lessons in on-line safety and recognizing scams; partnering with local businesses-currently Zina’s Cucina; community outreach; creating a place of acceptance and safety for everyone. Librarians do it all and more, often with limited funds and little public awareness.

Ellen Paul is a librarian and more. She is the executive director of the Connecticut Library Consortium. Consider what a consortium is, an alliance that pools resources, to achieve common goals too large for a single member to handle alone. Ellen leads that alliance of more than 1,000 (yes that is thousand) libraries of different kinds, helping them to pool buying power, share ideas, provide better services, by working together. Recently we have faced serious threats to our freedom to read. Her work with the General Assembly helped pass two laws, one protecting the freedom to read and a bipartisan one protecting library access to e-books. She is a defender of intellectual freedom, a consensus builder, a voice for all five towns in the 55th.

Steve Weir voted ‘no’ on both: the e-book bill, which passed the House 106 to 38, and the state budget that carried the freedom to read protections. He also voted against the 2025 bill increasing resources for students, schools, and special education; he was one of only 10 House members to oppose early childhood care and education.
Go to her website, Ellenforstaterep.com, and see the differences between Weir the naysayer and Ellen Paul, the problem-solver.

letters.headline: Weir Reads the Bills
letters.note: Barton is chair of the Andover Republican Town Committee.
paragraphs: The 55th Representative District had two very good representatives before Steve Weir. Pam Sawyer and Robin Green. Both of these ladies learned that you had to read the whole bill to see and understand what was being voted on. letters.headline: Weir’s Enduring Commitment

Steve’s broad community involvement over the years has given him the necessary experience to build on his political success. From his years as a Glastonbury police officer, involvement as former chairman of the Connecticut River Valley Chamber of Commerce, and many hours volunteering in schools and for charities, Steve’s service is laudable.

Voting is among our most vital processes in a democracy, and sometimes, it’s difficult to know what differentiates candidates. I feel confident that Steve Weir is the most capable, qualified candidate to represent Connecticut’s 55th District, and that’s why he deserves your vote.

letters.headline: Reelect Weir

letters.headline: Voting for Paul

From this point, it is part of life that any detailed matter which may come along can be learned, but it will be dealt with in a trustworthy and ethical manner and for the greater good. letters.headline: Why Not Steve Weir?!
