letters.headline: Ellen Protects the Shelves
letters.note: Sauyet is co-chair of the Andover Democratic Town Committee and a member of the RHAM Board of Education, but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: This is Banned Books Week, a good time to ask a simple question about the 55th District: whose freedoms does our representative protect?

Ellen Paul’s answer is on the public record. In 2025 she helped write and pass Connecticut’s freedom-to-read law, which bars libraries from removing a book because of the origin or views of its author, gives anyone who objects to a title a fair and consistent process, and protects librarians who act in good faith. In her words, it “protects a library’s ability to carry books like the Bible as much as it protects books about gender identity.” That same year she helped pass the library e-book law, with a Republican senator, Tony Hwang, among its lead champions. It cleared the Senate 35 to 1.

State Rep. Steve Weir voted against the ebook bill. He also voted against the 2025 budget act that carried the freedom-to-read provisions. In fairness, that was a vote on the whole budget, and he would say it was about spending. So look at his votes where spending was not the question.

This spring he voted against oversight of private-equity ownership of hospitals, though most of his own caucus voted ‘yes.’ He voted against stronger wage-theft enforcement, and against limits on warehouse productivity quotas. He voted against nursing-home transparency that his fellow Republicans favored 41 to 10. And when a bill to hold out-of-state apartment owners accountable after the Rocky Hill apartment disaster came up on the session’s last night, having passed the Senate and cleared committee without a single ‘no’ vote, he and a few allies threatened to run out the clock until leadership pulled it. He sits on the board of the Connecticut Apartment Association, the landlord trade group whose president testified against it.

Hospital investors, employers who shortchange paychecks, absentee landlords. Weir is a hard-working man, but that is where his votes land. Ellen has spent her career protecting the right of our children to walk into a library and find the book they need.
On Nov. 3, I know which kind of protector I want in Hartford.

letters.headline: Keep It Positive With Weir
paragraphs: I’ve known Steve Weir since we attended Glastonbury High School together. We weren’t close friends then, but years later our families reconnected through our daughters. From the beginning, Steve, his wife, and their family welcomed us as family. Our daughters became best friends and are now attending college together, and over the years I’ve had the opportunity to know Steve not as a politician, but as a husband, father, friend, and member of our community.
That is why I was disappointed to receive a recent political mailer portraying Steve as an extremist and attempting to connect virtually every vote he has taken in Hartford to national politics.

Steve’s opponent moved into our district only about a year ago. I would much rather learn about her ideas, experience, and what she hopes to accomplish for our five towns than see a campaign focused on attacking the character of someone who has spent most of his life living, working, volunteering, and serving here.

The Steve Weir I know grew up here, served as a Glastonbury police officer, built businesses that employed people and supported families, raised his family here, and has spent decades giving back to his community. Through our friendship with the Weir family, I have also become more involved in community service myself. I now volunteer with the Lions and hope to become a member, another connection that has reminded me how much strong communities depend on people willing to show up and contribute.

I’ve also learned that Steve asks questions, lots of them. He reads legislation, looks beyond the title of a bill, considers the cost, and asks about unintended consequences. We should want our representatives to do that.

A bill can have a wonderful-sounding title and still contain provisions that deserve scrutiny. Reducing a complicated legislative vote to an inflammatory sentence on a political mailer may be effective campaigning, but it doesn’t give voters the whole story.

Steve and I won’t agree on everything, and I don’t expect to agree with any elected official on every issue. But I know Steve Weir. I know his family, his character, and his commitment to the communities he represents.
Our five towns deserve a thoughtful conversation about Connecticut’s future, not another campaign built around national political division. I hope you’ll join me in supporting Steve Weir.

letters.headline: Proven Service to Our Community
letters.note: O’Reilly is a member of the Hebron Board of Finance, but said he is speaking as an individual.
paragraphs: I have known Steve Weir for many years, and I believe his background and character speak volumes about the way he approaches public service.

Steve is an outstanding individual who has worked hard his entire life. He has started, developed and successfully operated several businesses in Connecticut, and earlier in his career served as a Glastonbury police officer. He has lived in Hebron since 2000, raised his family here and has spent years living, working and volunteering in our community.
Steve understands what it means to run a business, meet a payroll, manage expenses and make practical decisions when resources are limited. Those are qualities I believe are important in government.

His commitment to Hebron began long before he became a state representative. I have personally seen Steve give his time as a volunteer basketball coach. He has also served on the Hebron Zoning Board of Appeals and as chairman of the Connecticut River Valley Chamber of Commerce.
In Hartford, Steve has focused on issues affecting working families, seniors and businesses, including taxes, government spending and the cost of living.

What stands out most to me is Steve as a person. In my experience, he is hard-working, honest, committed and reliable. He understands our community because this is his community too. He listens to people and brings a commonsense approach to the decisions he makes.

Regardless of political party, I encourage residents of the 55th District to look closely at Steve Weir’s background, community service and record representing us in Hartford when making their decision this November.

letters.headline: Enough Said Ned!!!
paragraphs: Eight years of our tax-and-spend Democratic governor Ned Lamont is enough!!!

There shouldn’t be a single senior or working people over 50 voting for him. Connecticut is one of 11 states that continue to tax Social Security benefits monies that have already been taxes at least once if not more. The Lamont Administration also taxes the hospitality industry – restaurants, nightclubs, food trucks – at 7.35% instead of the 6.35% for every other business. Connecticut also has a list of unfunded mandates dumped on the small business community – mandatory sick leave, family medical leave, up to two months of maternity leave for both the birth mother and the spouse. These employee perks used to be for high-performing and longtime tenured key employees. These mandates put a huge strain on all businesses and most get passed onto the consumer. Connecticut also has one of the highest minimum wages in the country and is forcing small business owners to reduce their staffing.

There’s more: public benefits brought to us taxpayers by Ned Lamont. This unfunded mandate forces working people, a.k.a. taxpayers, to “chip in” to Connecticut Natural Gas and Eversource bill and pay those who don’t pay their bills. The state is acting as the collection agency for these conglomerates who are making billions and billions in profits. Add to this the HUSKY health insurance, which is provided free to all or most of the people who are on the SNAP card program. The list goes on and on with the giveaways.

People who work and seniors have been tortured for the last eight years under Ned Lamont’s collection of “free” social programs. Connecticut is the third-highest-taxed state in the country. Now that’s something to be proud of.

Ryan Fazio has promised to eliminate “public benefits” and cap property taxes for seniors and cut utility costs. What a concept! Connecticut has been under Democratic rule for decades and look what they’ve done. Our cost of living forces many of fixed incomes to make terrible choices of paying their mortgage, buying food and/or paying their utility bills – never mind having some “peaceful down time.”

Do you want to continue with this high cost of living in this very blue state? I hope not. It’s time for a change; we need new leadership at the capitol! Ryan Fazio and his team will make our state a better place to live; so will Steve Weir!!

letters.headline: Holding Elected Officials Accountable
paragraphs: Since March, I have knocked on more than 2,500 doors across our district.

I have walked down country roads, through neighborhoods and cul-de-sacs, past farms, fields and woods, and up more long driveways than I can count. I have talked with Democrats, Republicans, independents and people who would rather not talk about politics at all.
I do it because this race matters deeply to me. But I also do it because I believe this is what representative government is supposed to look like.

If you are going to represent a community in Hartford, you should know the people who live there. You should understand what they are worried about, what they value and what they expect from their government. And you cannot learn that only by talking to people who already agree with you.

I love eastern Connecticut. I love its farms, fields and woods, but I also love something less tangible about this place: a basic expectation of decency, civility and respect for our neighbors, even when we disagree.
Those values shape the kind of representative I want to be.

I believe elected officials should be accessible and accountable to the people they serve. That means holding regular public town halls and listening throughout a term in office, not just during campaign season. I also support reasonable term limits and prohibiting elected officials from trading individual stocks while in office. Public office should be public service, not a lifetime job or an opportunity for personal profit.
After 2,500 doors, I certainly have not met everyone. But every conversation has reinforced my belief that good government begins with listening.
I will keep knocking. And if I have the privilege of representing this district, I will keep showing up, listening and making sure the voices of eastern Connecticut are heard in our State Capitol.

letters.headline: Why Not Steve Weir?!
paragraphs: I continue to ask myself “Why won’t Steve reply” to any of the requests for more information from people who have taken the time to write letters to the editor of the Rivereast ? Could it be that he has no defense? Maybe he just doesn’t care enough about the job anymore of being our representative in the 55th!
He cared enough to vote no on the following issues:
to require nursing homes to report their costs honestly and to disclose when a private equity firm owns them;
to expand early childhood education;
to help seniors stay in their homes;
to keep medical debt private.
I know why I will not be voting for Steve Weir! It’s because he has shown he does not care about seniors, childhood education, renters or working families.
If you belong to one of these groups I hope you will join me in voting for Ellen Paul on Nov. 3rd.

letters.headline: Steve Has Earned My Trust
paragraphs: You shouldn’t judge a book by its cover, and you can’t judge a bill by the catchy name it has been given, or by the one thing that some groups highlight in order to make their opponent look bad. What needs to be judged, is the bill as a whole, and what is actually written in the legislation. That is what Steve Weir does; he looks at the whole bill, not just the title, not just one part, not just at what seems obvious.

If you judge a bill by the catchy title or by one part that is being highlighted, you are judging a book by its cover. When you read beyond the title and carefully crafted highlights that are put out in mailers and by some people, and dig deeper into what is written, many times there are lines buried that can have unintended consequences for our local communities and families. Steve understands that, and his diligence is important to the people in our district and Connecticut. The campaign rhetoric comes and goes, but Steve’s thoughtful approach and commitment to the people in our district and CT are unwavering.
Steve has earned my trust, and I am proud to support him and his bid for continued service in the Connecticut House of Representatives!

letters.headline: Paul for Property Tax Relief
letters.note: Ockman is a member of the Hebron Board of Finance, but said he is speaking as an individual.
paragraphs: I will be voting for Ellen Paul in the 55th District this November. I respect that there are many reasons to vote for or against someone, but I’m going to focus on one reason in particular: how we pay for education.

Connecticut’s state and local taxes are regressive when considered together – meaning that the highest-earning people pay the smallest share of their income, and low- and middle-income people pay a higher effective tax rate. It’s not the state income tax that causes this problem – it’s our reliance on town property taxes. This is laid out in the state’s 2025 “Connecticut Tax Incidence Study” (you can Google for that report!).

For most towns in our part of Connecticut, education is the largest expense, and we saw substantial increases in costs this year. So it’s no wonder that this year’s budget referendums were so contentious. Especially when this burden is unfairly placed on middle-income families and retirees.

The state already provides aid to towns for education. But the formula hasn’t been updated for inflation since 2013, as the Connecticut Council of Municipalities recommends. This has resulted in the increasing burden being felt directly in the property tax. The solution is clear: we need to fix the formula and increase the state’s commitment.

Ellen Paul understands that funding our schools shouldn’t place a disproportionate burden on homeowners and renters. She’ll work to modernize state aid, ease the pressure on property taxes, and keep us from having to choose between adequate school funding and affordability. Our country deserves well-funded schools that will prepare our children for the challenges of the future.
Please come out to vote, either early or on Nov 3.
Have a great weekend!

letters.headline: Vote for Steve Weir

Best regards,

letters.headline: Supports Weir
paragraphs: I am writing in support of Steve Weir of Hebron, who is seeking reelection to the state House of Representatives to continue to represent the 55th House District and citizens of Andover, Hebron and Marlborough and parts of Bolton and Glastonbury.

I have worked with Steve on behalf of clients in his role as a lawmaker and ranking member of the General Assembly’s Labor Committee. He also serves on the Higher Education and Housing committees. Steve is accessible, thoughtful and listens carefully. He studies policies thoroughly and he advocates vigorously on behalf of his constituents and issues that he supports. Steve is honest and forthright whether he agrees with a policy or not.

Steve supports his local community. He served as chairman of CT River Valley Chamber of Commerce. We volunteered together through the Chamber as judges on a panel evaluating student presentations of business concepts. Steve was thoughtful, fair-minded and offered insightful, constructive criticism to help students refine their ideas.

As a business owner, Steve has brought his knowledge and experience to the legislature to help shape legislation and the state budget. As an employer, he knows what it is like to lead, collaborate, make ends meet and, if necessary, compromise – essential skills in adopting a budget and setting policy. As a devoted husband and father, he understands the challenges of raising a family in Connecticut.
I respectfully ask citizens in the 55th District, when they go to the polls on Nov. 3, or if they vote early or via absentee ballot, to support Steve Weir.

letters.headline: Read Between the Signs
paragraphs: It’s that time of the year again. When the lovely landscape of eastern Connecticut gets littered with roadside political signs. The chief offender, of course, is Steve Weir. His sign is everywhere, it seems. You’d think he was running for seven or eight offices. The point is, he’s better at putting up signs than at being a legislator. Personally, I’d rather it were the other way around, which is why I’m voting for Ellen Paul. Sure, she’s put up some signs here and there, but what she offers goes well beyond signs. It’s the promise of hard work, intelligence, empathy, and a talent for paying close attention to constituents.
This November read between the signs. Vote for Ellen Paul.

letters.headline: Librarians Vital to Towns
letters.note: Larson is an alternate member of the Marlborough Zoning Board of Appeals, but said he is writing this as an individual.
paragraphs: Librarians are vital to the life of a community. In addition to providing books, CDs, DVDs, magazines, and other means of communication to people of the town, they also serve as computer, printer and fax consultants for individuals who are unfamiliar with modern technologies In some cases they serve as a social service provider for individuals who have need help in navigating modern society. They also prepare budget and advocate for said budget, deal with library employees issues and the maintenance of the library building on behalf of the community. They also plan and implement various programs to provide education and entertainment at the library that benefit the community. And they are the front line of supporting the first amendment so that all members of the town can access diverse views that other people or outside agitators may not want distributed.

I may be biased as I am a brother, a cousin and a grandson of librarians and have worked in a library to help pay for my graduate studies. Some letter-writers who dismiss librarians as individuals who are of little consequence are unaware of the amount of work they do and support they receive from the public. Not only do they need to keep up with the many rules governing libraries and the constantly changing technology that supports library science, they interface with all ages of library clientele.

Ellen Paul is rightly proud of her profession and the work she has done as librarian. In addition to her work as the head of a library, she is also the head of a consortiums of libraries which enable small town libraries to offer a wider variety of books they would otherwise. And as such executive she helped to successfully shepherded two bills through the legislature which is apparently two more than her opponent successfully got passed. Having met Ellen, I’m sure that she would not run away from the votes she makes as Steve Weir does by refusing to defend or even explain the votes he has made.

Furthermore, Sen. Cathy Osten needs a partner in the house of representative to help bring grants and other state resources to the 55th. I plan on voting for Ellen and Cathy for our legislators and urge you to do the same.

letters.headline: Weir Can Read
letters.note: Hjulstrom is a member of the Marlborough Board of Finance, but I am speaking as an individual.
paragraphs: I have read letters complaining about Steve Weir voting no on certain legislation. Are those people saying that they want their Representative to blindly approve everything?
Unfortunately, some good legislation has garbage attached in order to try to sneak by frivolous, wasteful or downright destructive things.
Steve Weir takes the time to read the bills that are placed before him so he can make an informed decision on what he is being asked to support.
Do you really want your legislators to simply vote yes on everything? I didn’t think so.
So, if you want a representative who works for you and watches out for your interests, please join me in voting for Steve Weir on Nov. 3rd.

letters.headline: Vote for Ellen Paul
paragraphs: Did you know that in the four years Steve Weir has been in office, no bill he ever filed has even received a floor vote in either chamber of the General Assembly? No bill he has ever filed has become law. You should ask yourself why this is.

Of the 24 he filed, 11 were for bills he had filed before in prior sessions of the General Assembly; meaning no new thought or effort was needed to draft them. Subtracting out the 11 filings of previously submitted bills results in an actual number of bills he drafted as only being 13 in his four-year tenure. And even these few failed to advance. The full analysis of his record can be found at andoverct.info/reports/55th/weir-far-right.
Shouldn’t we expect more from our representative?

I do and you should too. My vote, therefore, is going to Ellen Paul. She is campaigning precisely because she knows we deserve better. Ellen is in touch with the interests and needs of the district. In her professional career, she has a history of being able to advance bills and to keep parties with divergent interests at the table until a consensus is reached. She has an important talent for creating coalitions and working well with everyone. She knows that while it is important to show up for every vote, it is essential to think for herself, listen, and vote according to what is best for the district. For more information, please go to ellenforstaterep.com.
Vote for Ellen Paul! Thank you.

letters.headline: A Champion for Eastern CT
paragraphs: I attended the candidates’ forum in Glastonbury last week. Ellen Paul clearly demonstrated that her focus is on items that benefit the common people in the 55th District.

As a retired school business manager, I know that in the mid-1990s, Connecticut’s target for funding public education was that Connecticut would fund an average of 60% of the local cost. Over the years that percentage has decreased to where today Hebron is receiving an Educational Cost Sharing grant of $5,997,693 or 39.36% of our local education budget.

At last week’s forum, Ellen stated she supports increasing state dollars for Education. Her opponent, Steve Weir, voted ‘no’ for a bill that provided an additional $400,000 in school and municipal aid for Hebron. In spite of his negative vote the bill passed. Those funds saved the tax payer who owns a house with an assessed value of $350,000 over $200 in annual property tax.

On July 17, Rep. Weir is quoted as saying on the GOP website (www.cthousegop.com/weir/repweir-receives-100-voting-record-for-2026-legislative-session) “Representing you and your family in Hartford is something that I take very seriously. This session, I am proud to have achieved a 100% record for all 316 votes taken on the House floor.”
That may be true however many of his votes were against items that either supported or protected the people of the 55th District. For example, he voted ‘no’ on bills:

That would have helped seniors afford to remain in their homes. All bills that addressed women’s health and reproductive healthcare. Housing bills that would convert empty commercial buildings to living spaces keeping homeless people off the streets.
Most interesting to me is why Ellen Paul is running for office.

She wrote a letter to Steve expressing her concern that ICE agents in Connecticut were taking children and adults with no criminal record into custody and sending them to detention facilities without due process.
He chose not to respond to Ellen. Much the same way he has chosen not to respond to many of you on other items the past several weeks.
Is that the type or person you want representing you in Hartford? I don’t!!!

I’m voting for Ellen Paul. Ellen has many years of experience as a former legislative aid to Representative Joe Courtney. Ellen is a great listener and open to new ideas and most importantly represents my values!!

letters.headline: Steve Weir Lacks Independence
paragraphs: Over four years in Hartford, state Rep. Steve Weir has voted the Republican party line 97 percent of the time on contested bills. In 1,351 roll calls, he cast three genuinely bipartisan crossover votes. Three.

When he does break from his caucus, it is almost always to the right. On 95 occasions he voted to the right of his own caucus, opposing bills most Connecticut Republicans supported. He has voted ‘no’ on every clean-energy or climate bill of consequence.

Weir casts the most reliably partisan votes in our corner of the state. His record shows a consistent instinct: the party line first, the district after. A full analysis can be found at andoverct.info/ reports/55th/weir-far-right.

Ellen Paul has built her career on coalition and consensus, and she has pledged to be a voice for the district’s five towns rather than a reliable vote for anyone. On Nov. 3, I urge you to vote for her.

letters.headline: Questions for Weir
letters.note: Sauyet is co-chair of the Andover Democratic Town Committee and a member of the RHAM Board of Education, but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: I went to the Oct. 7 candidates’ forum in Glastonbury expecting a town hall. It wasn’t one; eight candidates spoke, including Ellen Paul and Steve Weir, but the audience didn’t get to ask questions. It was a good event anyway, and I’m grateful to its organizers. But I came with questions for Rep. Weir, so I’ll put them to him here.

1. What is the bill you’re proudest of? Not constituent help, which everyone agrees you do well, and not one you cosponsored alongside dozens of colleagues, but a bill you wrote and shepherded through yourself, or one you fought hard to defeat.

2. Your campaign website offers your biography, your community service, and principles like “Protect taxpayers.” It doesn’t name a single bill, position, or plan. What are two specific things you’ll do next term, and how will you get them passed?

3. In 1,351 roll calls over four years, I count 95 times you voted to the right of your own caucus, but only three times you crossed party lines on a vote where the parties actually divided. Did I miss any crossovers?

4. Senate Bill 274 was written after the Concierge Apartments disaster in Rocky Hill, where an out-of-state owner let a complex decay until thousands of tenants had to be relocated. The bill raised penalties for repeat fire and building-code violations and required out-of-state owners to register with the towns where their buildings sit. It passed the Senate and cleared committee without a single no vote. On the session’s last night, you and a few allies threatened to run out the clock, and it died without a vote. Why that bill? And if you opposed it, why not simply vote no?

5. In May you voted against a budget adjustment carrying about $630,000 in new aid to our five towns, a bill that 27 of the 48 Republicans voting supported. What would you tell taxpayers about that vote?

There is one more question I would have liked to ask, but this page keeps letters to state and local matters. I sent it to Rep. Weir by email on Sept. 10 and have not had a reply. Any answer he gives will be published in full at andoverct.info/reports/ ahm/disavowal.
Ellen Paul answers questions like these on her website. I’d like to hear Rep. Weir’s answers too.

letters.headline: Paul is the Right Choice
paragraphs: I was shown Steve Weir’s latest mailer. It was amazing to me that he had small-town advocate as his heading. Steve Weirs’ voting record brings his small-town advocacy into question. Why?

Steve has voted ‘no’ in helping to defray energy costs. He voted ‘no’ for solar projects and community solar (HB-7087, 2025). Has he seen the electricity bills most people are currently paying? How does that help the people of our district?
Ellen Paul believes we need energy policies that put ratepayers first with accountability and investment in alternate forms of energy to bolster Connecticut’s ability to produce power.

Steve is a Ranking Member of the Labor Committee. According to the AFL-CIO’s scorecard Steve agreed with workers on 2 of 14 bills (7%). He voted ‘no’ on expanding sick leave (HB -5005, 2024) and voted no to Family and Medical Leave improvements.

Ellen Paul believes in workers and their right to make a living. No one should have to decide between taking care of a sick child or an aging parent. Paid sick leave, family leave, and basic decency for our struggling workers are key for our families.

Steve also voted no to early voting after Connecticut voters approved it by constitutional amendment (HB- 5004-2023) and on absentee voting reforms (HB-5001, 2026). Why is he so concerned that the people in our district have access to a variety of ways to vote? Happily, people can vote by absentee ballot, and during the early voting window. (This year it is from Oct. 19 to Nov. 1.)
Ellen believes that voting should be secure, accessible and convenient for every eligible voter. She will never vote to make this process more difficult for the people of the 55th district.
Steve has a caption on the mailer that states, “You can count on me to do the right thing.” My question is when is this going to happen?
Ellen Paul has a plan to address issues that residents of the 55th District are looking for. Please join me in voting for Ellen Paul whenever it’s most convenient for you before Nov. 3, 2026.
bills: Paid family and medical leave (no bill number cited)

letters.headline: Paul vs. Weir
paragraphs: Dan Malloy, Democratic Party Governor 2011- 2019 = 8 years.

letters.headline: The Man I Married
paragraphs: As Steve’s wife, I see the side of him that doesn’t make it into the headlines: the long days, late nights, and the countless times he makes room for someone who needs his help. His commitment to serving others extends to his work, countless volunteer endeavors, boards and commissions, his state Representative duties, our children and our family. It is simply part of who he is.

Steve cares deeply about our families, businesses and our communities. He listens, shows up, and puts in the work because he believes people deserve a representative who takes their concerns seriously. I have watched him giving his time and energy to helping others – quietly and without expecting anything in return. That is the man I know and love.

Public service requires sacrifice, and I see firsthand how much Steve gives of himself to this responsibility. He does it because he believes in our towns and the people who call them home. Yes, he reads every bill, sometimes very early in the morning or late at night. Anyone who has reached out to him knows he’s accessible. His cell phone number is published on almost all of his state rep material.

When I first met him he was already a young man of great character, hard-working, smart and kind. He and I were a relatively new young love story when both my parents passed away my senior year of high school (my father lost a short battle to ALS and nine weeks later my mom was murdered). Steve as a young man could’ve run for the hills, but instead he stuck by my side and became my rock, with his quiet, caring and steadfast nature. He is the reason my once nightmare of circumstances turned into the beautiful life we worked hard to build for our three daughters.

I knew when I married an Eagle Scout that I was marrying a man of true integrity, grit, who is committed to helping others. There are many members of our community who can and have attested to Steve’s commitment to helping and to serving others. Then, as now, my husband – and your state representative – is a good man and dedicated servant.
So, take it from someone who knows him best: Steve Weir cares deeply about our communities. It is why he serves, and why I want him to continue. He has my vote, and I hope he earns yours.

letters.headline: Steve Weir Gets It
paragraphs: I am writing to enthusiastically endorse Steve Weir for reelection as our Connecticut State Representative for the 55th District. I know what it takes to be a successful House member. Having watched his dedication to our community, it is clear that he remains the right choice to represent our values and ensure our voices are heard in Hartford.

Steve has consistently demonstrated that he values the input of his constituents above all else. He makes a deliberate effort to share with constituents the details of active bills, and speak up on the issues that affect their daily lives. In an era where politics can feel distant, Steve’s open-door approach and emphasis on community feedback are deeply refreshing. Whether advocating for sensible fiscal policies, addressing critical housing issues, or ensuring our towns receive state support, Steve approaches every challenge with practical, common-sense solutions. He recognizes the immense pressure that working families and local businesses are under, and he fights tirelessly to make Connecticut a more affordable and accessible place to live, work, and raise a family.

We need a representative who is accessible, transparent, and focused on results who reaches across the aisle. Steve Weir has proven himself to be exactly that kind of leader. Please join me in voting to send Steve Weir back to Hartford. Steve Weir gets it.

letters.headline: Paul Will Honor Our Vote
letters.note: Wilkinson is a member of the Marlborough Democratic Town Committee but said she is speaking as an individual.
paragraphs: Do you remember voting to amend the Connecticut constitution to allow early voting? It passed statewide in 2022 with a clear majority.
So how did our representative respond when the legislature took up the law to carry out what we had decided? State Rep. Steve Weir voted no. It passed the House 107 to 35 without him.

That was not the only time. When the legislature voted to let you decide whether Connecticut should allow no-excuse absentee voting, he voted no on even asking the question, though 16 of his fellow Republicans said yes. When absentee-voting reforms came up this spring, he voted no again.

When the people of Connecticut speak clearly through a referendum majority, they expect their representative, of whatever party, to honor that voice. Each of these votes tested that expectation: does our representative carry out what we decide, or second-guess it?

Ellen Paul starts from the opposite premise. She trusts the voters of this district. She has pledged to make voting secure, accessible, and convenient for every eligible voter, and never to make participating harder. Carrying out what the people decide is, in her view, the first duty of the job.
The 55th does not need a representative who audits our decisions. It needs one who respects them. On Nov. 3, you get the deciding vote: ellenforstaterep.com.

letters.headline: Paul an Excellent Candidate
paragraphs: The Rivereast does a great service for our community in publishing each week what are often well thought out letters to the editor. It is an important contribution at election time, and as a reader, I especially welcome the letters of support for candidates that come from citizens, rather than friends, family members, or business associates. This is that kind of letter. I am inspired to write in support of the Ellen Paul, the excellent Democratic candidate for the 55th.

In this time of political divisiveness, we need legislative leaders who can do more than follow a party line like sheep – we need politicians with solid common sense, a strong commitment to social responsibility and fairness, and a willingness to collaborate to pass the kind of legislation that will support a safe environment, for us today and for our children tomorrow. It takes courage to choose an independent perspective – but truly it is the way to really see our democracy at work. The incumbent, Steve Weir has voted along his party lines 95+ percent of the time, and often falls to the right of even his own party caucus. I want my representative to be able to work across the aisle to create and pass legislation that we all can benefit from. Ellen Paul is ready for that.

One of the most important reasons I’m motivated to support Ellen Paul is because she recognizes the need to prioritize support of the middle class - the working people who keep this country going. A critical issue is fair housing and the support of opportunities for families to be able to afford to buy reasonable homes. It is part of the American dream that so many of our children find out of reach. While there have been lots of bills that would support this effort to increase availability of lower cost homes, Steve Weir has consistently voted against them. Ellen would not.

Ellen’s priorities include work to support the most vulnerable members of our communities, our children and our seniors. She is an advocate for fair taxation and she supports a science-based perspective having to do with energy. She feels a duty to protect our beautiful environment. Steve Weir has voted against virtually all bills that mention green energy, including recent solar bills.
From my perspective, the choice is a clear one. I hope you’ll vote for Ellen Paul.

letters.headline: Implied Moral Equivalence
paragraphs: I’ve endeavored to understand what the Democratic Party actually stands for. John Barnowski and Scott Sauyet have provided glimpses of what is important to them and their party. Barnowski claims voting Democratic will save democracy whereas voting Republican threatens to “extend ultra-conservative trends” into his town.

Barnowski’s previous letters typically consist of hit-and-run attacks on Republicans, and issues surrounding both ends of life where he is an ardent supporter of abortion and a proponent of legal euthanasia. Scott Sauyet shows that his and Ellen Paul’s most important issue involves utilizing school libraries to circumvent parental authority and guidance regarding matters related to the development of minor children.

The fact that Sauyet and Paul brood over what they call “Banned Books Week” is both telling and bizarre. Reviewing what books are age-appropriate for minor-aged students is very similar to what the Motion Picture Association’s rating system does for movies. Sauyet’s approvingly repeating Paul’s statement about her legislation “protecting a library’s ability to carry books like the Bible as much as it protects books about gender identity” is both outrageous and alarming. The ridiculouslyimplied moral equivalence is shocking.

Why are Democrats so obsessed and focused on the sexual orientations and potential gender dysphoria in minor children who are not their own? I find that very peculiar and warranting greater scrutiny. Their recent proposals to start early education at six months of age shows their objective of controlling our children from the very start of their lives.

I find it revealing that in recent weeks Sauyet and Paul have contradicted themselves by first championing an increase in the age of consent for girls to get married, while at the same time indignantly calling for no age restrictions on minor children to view materials they aren’t emotionally stable or mature enough to process safely.

Democrats think people who are struggling should be made more comfortable in their deprivations. Republicans think people need opportunities to change their lives and to substantially improve their situations. Rather than foolishly increasing the minimum wage, which only devalues the currency causing a recalibration and increase in other prices, Republicans encourage people to develop new higher-value skills to obtain higher pay.
Democrats have demoralized generations of children to have fear and dread regarding their futures. Fewer and fewer are marrying and having children. We need more children and fewer Democrats.
bills: HB 5003 (2025): early childhood care and education

letters.headline: I Call Baloney
paragraphs: I have been asking for specific information from Steve Weir. I have read every article and endorsement letter for Steve Weir, hoping to see legitimate responses.

Last week, I carefully read Weir endorsement letters. His supporters believe he is willing to listen, has energy, does the right thing, has a 100% voting record, and defends the rights of all families. The belief that appears to drive his supporters is that Steve reads bills carefully, probably finds additions “tucked into them” (Sept. 4), or worse, “unintended consequences,” (Weir Aug. 28) hence votes no even if his own party strongly supported the bill. People endorsing him, trusting souls who want to believe his best intentions and careful work, assume he found something so negative for his constituents that he went against a bill his party or even his state supported. I call baloney. Pay attention to issues, not personality.

What unintended consequences would keep a caring father of daughters from voting to end child marriage? Does it really give families greater independence? Or does it open the door to predatory practices with underage girls? The Connecticut House passed it 98 to 45, the Senate passed it unanimously. An explanation would really help.

What addition was “tucked in” to make him vote no on early childhood education and care? There can be no doubt that early childhood sets the stage for health, well-being and successful learning. He was one of only 10 “no” votes in the entire House. An explanation would really help.

Given the horror stories coming out of nursing homes, what “unintended consequences” were in that bill on nursing home transparency that caused Weir to vote no? His fellow Republicans supported it 41 to 10. An explanation would really help.

Writers said that Weir is “focused on issues affecting working families.” (Oct. 9) Really? The Connecticut Working Families Party endorsed Ellen Paul. It is an independent political organization. It prioritizes affordable communities, workers’ rights, and strong public schools. They are clearly not impressed with Weir’s stand on issues affecting working families.
The Connecticut Education Association endorsed Ellen Paul. Clearly they respect her focus on strong public schools.
Go to EllenforStateRep.com; pay attention to her focus on real, practical issues. Consider whether her stand on issues outweighs a 100% voting record that says ‘no’ on issues important to you.
bills: HB 5003 (2025): early childhood care and education

letters.headline: A Scout’s Values in Hartford
paragraphs: I am writing to support state Rep. Steve Weir’s reelection in the 55th District.

As a former scoutmaster of Troop 28 in Hebron, I have seen firsthand how much Steve invests in our young people. He has attended every one of our Eagle Scout ceremonies, and at each one he presents a proclamation from the House of Representatives marking this milestone in a scout’s life. He also takes time to speak to the troop about his own scouting years in Glastonbury and his journey on the Trail to Eagle. For a young scout, hearing that from someone who walked the same path means a great deal.

Steve’s support goes beyond ceremonies. Every year he joins our Scouting for Food drive, which stocks the community food bank at AHM in Hebron. He does not come for a photo. He comes to connect with the young male and female scouts and share the impact that scouting had on shaping his own character and values.

I have known Steve (and his wife Allegra) for more than 30 years, as a fellow communicant at Gilead Hill Church, as parents raising children in our own community, and as a business leader and friend. I can personally attest to his character and integrity.

Some letters have asked how Steve decides his votes. From what I’ve seen over three decades, he decides by the same principles every Scout promises to live by: be trustworthy, do your duty, and help other people. When he votes no, it is because he believes the bill is not right for the people he represents, not because it is the easy thing to do.
As a small business owner, Steve also understands what our rural farming community needs to grow, and how to balance that growth with the character that makes Hebron special.
Please join me in voting for Steve Weir on Nov. 3.

letters.headline: Support Ellen Paul
paragraphs: I recently had the pleasure of meeting Ellen Paul and was impressed with her plan for a better Connecticut. I support Ellen as our next state representative because she supports quality public education for our state. She plans to achieve this by revisiting Connecticut’s Education Cost Sharing formula so the burden of funding public education does not just rest on the property taxes of the town.

The high cost of electricity is another issue Ellen is concerned about. I feel she will work hard to make Connecticut’s electricity affordable. Finally, as a senior, something very important to me is making Connecticut affordable for seniors. I see her focusing on property tax relief, promoting affordable health care and keeping energy costs in check. Please join me in voting for Ellen Paul as our next state representative. Thank you

letters.headline: Why I’m Supporting Weir
paragraphs: I’m supporting Steve Weir for reelection because I believe he is fighting for what is best for Connecticut residents. We need representatives who listen to the people who live here and make government work for us, instead of giving in to pressure from Hartford insiders and special interests.

I appreciate Steve’s commitment to reducing state spending and questioning spending that seems wasteful or frivolous. Our money should be used responsibly and focused on real issues that affect Connecticut families, including the extra tax on prepared meals and the high cost of electricity, gas, and everyday living.

Steve introduced legislation to eliminate the extra 1% tax on prepared meals, and he has spoken up about the effect energy costs can have on electric ratepayers. Those issues matter to families like mine. I want to see him keep pushing for relief and for a future where Connecticut residents can afford to live, work, and thrive here.

His commitment also shows in the time he puts into the job. In the 2026 legislative session, he was present for all 316 House floor votes and every committee vote. That kind of commitment matters. I’m grateful to have a representative who shows up, takes the work seriously, and keeps fighting for our district and for Connecticut residents.

letters.headline: Paul for More Homegrown Power
letters.note: Wilson is a member of the Marlborough Zoning Board of Appeals, but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: Open your last electric bill. Now consider a few facts alongside it.

Connecticut households pay some of the highest electricity rates in the continental United States. The utilities delivering that power have been posting healthy profits and returning for rate increases anyway. And the state’s supply of homegrown power has not kept pace with what we use, which leaves every ratepayer exposed when prices spike.

Ellen Paul, candidate for State Representative in the 55th, has put this at the center of her platform. In her words: “Connecticut families pay some of the highest electric bills in the country, while utility companies keep posting massive profits and asking working families to pay more.” Her answer has three parts: stronger oversight of the utilities, real accountability when they fail the people paying the bills, and long-term investment in a diverse, reliable energy supply so Connecticut is producing more of its own power rather than importing its price shocks.
More supply, more competition, less exposure. It is the least ideological plan you will read this year, which is rather the point. As she puts it: “Affordable energy isn’t a luxury. It’s essential.”

There are many reasons to choose a legislator. The number at the bottom of your electric bill is as good as any. Read her plan at ellenforstaterep. com, and remember the name on November 3: Ellen Paul.

letters.headline: No on Steve Weir
letters.note: Howell is a member of the Hebron Democratic Town Committee but said he is writing as a concerned citizen.
paragraphs: The towns in the 55th District, like all towns in Connecticut, are facing another difficult budget season. The loss of financial support from the federal level, past and pending health care premiums increases caused by the big beautiful bill, escalating diesel and gas prices and the accelerating rise in inflation are combining for a perfect financial storm.
We need state representatives who understand these problems, support what the voters want and make effective policy changes.

Steve Weir does none of these things. Every flyer I see, every letter to the editor, all say the same thing: Steve is a great guy, a nice neighbor, easy to talk to, reads all the bills he votes on to make sure he understands them and never missed a vote yet. And then he voted ‘no’ on over 90% of the bills. He voted ‘no’ on helping reduce our local tax burden, voted ‘no’ on ending childhood marriage, voted ‘no’ on early childhood learning and his ‘no’ vote list goes on. He states he reads the bills to understand all of the add-on legislation put in place which he says he determined to be detrimental. So he votes ‘no.’ Think about that. He is saying, with his ‘no’ voting record, that over 90% of the bills are detrimental. I think he always sees the cup as halfempty.
Ellen Paul has advanced bills, crossed the aisle to get support and gotten them passed. Steve Weir has passed exactly none.

We have the opportunity to put a positive, forward-thinking legislator in office who understands the problems we face and will pass effective legislation to address them. Join me in voting for the cup is half-full candidate Ellen Paul.
bills: HB 5003 (2025): early childhood care and education

letters.headline: We Need Steve Weir
paragraphs: I’ve been reading all the letters regarding the 55th district and noticed several things in common. Most of the letters written by Democrats are very negative, while most of the letters written by Republicans and supporters of Steve Weir are positive. I also noticed that many call for more money from the State for education and other things, to keep property taxes down. Where does the state get the money? Some will reply, “from the federal government!” Okay, where does the federal government get the money? Governments, be they local, state or federal, have no money except for the money we all pay in taxes.

Steve Weir is the one trying to keep expenses down, encourage small business creation, and is in favor of students learning skills that are needed, especially working with their hands. We need carpenters, electricians, plumbers, mechanics, etc., to replace those that have retired. New small businesses bring more income, thus increasing the tax base. Every new government job does not increase the tax base, since the cost of it is paid from our taxes.

Why does the Democratic Party keep thinking they can fix something by spending more money on it. Republicans try to reduce spending by reducing the size of government and excessive regulations. When Steve Weir reads an entire bill and finds unnecessary or unintended consequences, he votes ‘no,’ so don’t let the title of the bill fool you. We need Steve Weir to stay on the job of representing all of us in the 55th District. Please re-elect him.

letters.headline: Landlord Accountability
paragraphs: I invite anyone voting for Connecticut State Representative for the 55th District (Andover, Bolton, Hebron, Marlborough and eastern Glastonbury) to view the CT Mirror article of May 6, 2026 titled “House kills bill to hold nonresident landlords accountable.” Senate Bill 274 sought to increase penalties for repeated building and fire code violations by landlords and require out-of-state landlords to register additional personal contact information with the Connecticut town in which their rental properties exist. Common-sense stuff, right?

The bill was a response to a crisis in Rocky Hill, at the Concierge Apartments, owned by a California private equity firm. Thousands of tenants were displaced in February due to flooding and lack of heat.

Although having passed in the Senate, the bill was killed on the last day of the legislative session. State Rep. Steve Weir of the 55th District and other Republican legislators had threatened to run the clock out on debate until midnight, according to the Majority House leader.

While Rep. Weir has accumulated an impressive public service record in our towns, it isn’t mentioned on his campaign website that he is an Associate Director of the Connecticut Apartment Association, a landlord and property management advocacy group.

This concerns me, as does the 52% out of 100% score given him this year by the Connecticut Education Association on education advocacy and policy issues. Is it time for a change? Weir’s challenger, Democrat Ellen Paul, is the director of a consortium of libraries in Connecticut. She served as an intern for U.S. Rep. Joe Courtney, and supports the rights of tenants, quality public education, property tax reform and other issues that make sense to me.
Please consider voting for Ellen Paul. She is a common-sense candidate who better reflects our values.

letters.headline: Ellen Paul for Libraries
paragraphs: Hello! I have never written a letter to the editor before, but this time I am compelled to write to support our local libraries. As you know, libraries are critically important centers of our communities. Libraries provide books, research, education, book clubs, hundreds of programs, and connection for citizens of all ages! They support people in our communities of all income levels. These materials and programs need to be available to everyone, but libraries are operated as non-profits and typically underfunded.

We all need to support our local libraries. You can support by getting a library card, taking out books and materials, and joining programs of interest. But these efforts are not enough. To make the most impact, we need to support library boards, school boards, finance boards, town councils, state representatives, and people in congress that have the power to make major decisions for our libraries.

It has never been more important than today in our country to support libraries, which are centers for learning and essential to support education, sharing of ideas, free speech and critical thinking.

That is why I support Ellen Paul for state representative in the 55th district in this election. She has deep experience with libraries. She is currently the executive director of the CT Library Consortium (2021 to present). She personally drove two 2025 Connecticut laws, the library e-book licensing law (Public Act 25-9) and the freedom-to-read library-policy law (within Public Act 25-168), and was named a national Library Journal “Mover & Shaker” for her work in 2026. The organization she leads saves Connecticut taxpayers millions a year through cooperative purchasing.

She has also been a hands-on librarian for over 15 years, most recently serving as the director of the East Hampton public library. Under her leadership, the library was awarded the Excellence in Public Library Service Award by the Connecticut Library Association for innovative projects. Additionally, her advocacy and improvements led to the library breaking records in annual borrowing, program attendance, and summer reading participation.
She cares deeply to ensure that all of our citizens have access to critical library services.
Thank you for your time and consideration.
bills: PA 25-168 (2025): state budget incl. freedom to read

letters.headline: Same Person = Same Results
letters.note: Riley is a member of the Hebron Board of Selectmen, but is speaking as an individual.
paragraphs: There’s an expression that goes like this: “Insanity is the doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results.”

State Rep. Steve Weir is now running for his third term representing the 55th District. My question is what tangible results has he brought to the district? How has he assisted in actively addressing pressing issues such as affordability? The burden of taxes on our families and senior citizens? Addressing the severe lack of affordable housing in the district?
Since January of 2023, Rep. Weir put his name on 41 bills as an introducer and not one of them became law.

For example, he introduced a bill in 2023 that would have barred minimum wage class action lawsuits where hourly workers band together to sue an employer for systemic pay violations. Thankfully, this bill died in committee.

On Nov. 3rd, I will be casting my vote for Ellen Paul for the 55th. We need a state representative that will advocate for practical solutions for our towns’ real problems: public education & property tax relief, affordable housing, reducing our energy cost burdens and supporting our seniors.
I ask you: don’t we want to see real change for the 55th instead of the same representation that has yielded little results?
Now is the time — voters can enact fresh, new leadership in Hartford. And that is Ellen Paul.
