letters.headline: Cost of Electricity
paragraphs: After knocking on more than 3,000 doors across our district, few issues generate as much frustration as electricity.
People show me their bills. They ask why electricity has been so expensive in Connecticut and why a bill for something as basic as keeping the lights on is so difficult to understand.
I share their frustration.

Electricity is different from most things we buy. If I don’t like the price or service at one grocery store, I can go somewhere else. But most of us cannot choose the company that delivers electricity to our homes.
When consumers don’t have the power of choice, government regulation has to provide the power of accountability.

That means utility companies should not simply be guaranteed the opportunity to earn more regardless of their performance. Their financial incentives should be tied to measurable results: reliability, affordability, customer service and controlling costs. Connecticut has begun developing this kind of performance-based regulation. I believe we should follow through and make it meaningful.
We also need to look carefully at what we put on people’s electric bills.

I support helping neighbors who cannot afford to keep their homes warm. I support investments that make our energy system more efficient and reliable. But if the legislature decides that something serves a broad statewide public purpose, we should ask whether an electric bill has become a substitute for taxation. Does that program truly belong on your electric bill, or should it compete with every other priority in the state budget?

Finally, people deserve transparency. An ordinary person should be able to look at an electric bill and understand where their money is going, what each major charge pays for, and who is responsible for it.
Electric rates have come down this year, and that is welcome news. But Connecticut families need more than temporary relief. They need an energy system they can understand and trust.
If a company has a monopoly, accountability should come with it. And if government puts a charge on your bill, government should be able to explain why it is there.

letters.headline: Let’s Embrace Change
paragraphs: We’re so lucky to live in our small Connecticut towns. As the leaves turn and nights cool, we are reminded of the beauty of New England’s everchanging seasons. No matter how much we might enjoy summer, Autumn always comes. We can’t stay stuck in the past. We know how to embrace change.

This November, we can make another change. For most of our lives, Andover, Bolton, Glastonbury, Hebron and Marlborough have been represented by the Republican Party. I can’t help but feel that they take our district for granted and have grown complacent. We’re a sure thing. They have no incentive to work hard and deliver for the people in our towns.
With all the challenges we face, we need more than just a seat warmer in Hartford. We need someone focused on advocating for our district at the capitol. It’s time for a change.

This November, we have a special opportunity to send someone to the legislature who is ready to be that powerful advocate. Ellen Paul knows that good government is still possible when people are willing to listen, build consensus, and stay focused on solving problems instead of scoring political points.

Paul wants to reform property taxes to ensure the state pays their share of education funding. Aren’t we all sick of fighting over school budgets? She has a plan to provide for our schools without hiking mill rates.
Ellen wants to ensure our seniors aren’t priced out of their homes, giving them tax relief so they can stay in the towns they spent their lives improving.

Ellen isn’t afraid to tackle the big problems of energy policy or technology. She wants to hold Eversource accountable for rate increases. She knows part of the solution is diversifying how we make power so we can cope with price spikes. She also knows the billionaires running AI companies need guardrails and will work to build them for Connecticut.

Ellen Paul has experience in public policy and leadership. She is energized and wants to hear everyone out, not just the people who vote for her. As many have seen, she been knocking on doors for months, talking to thousands of us. She wants to earn your vote, not expect it.
Let’s embrace change and send someone to Hartford willing to put in the work. Vote Ellen Paul this November.

letters.headline: Vote for Ellen Paul
paragraphs: You have read all the letters supporting Ellen Paul to be our representative in the General Assembly. The information has been factually correct, the evaluation of her character and dedication has been spot on, and the opinions of her skills and outstanding character are not overstated.
Ellen has stepped up to the plate to represent us. Now it is time for you to step up to the plate and vote for her!
We cannot do better than electing Ellen Paul to be our representative. Please make it so! Thank you.

letters.headline: Supports Weir
paragraphs: I am writing to endorse and strongly encourage voters who live in CT District 55 to support Steve Weir with their vote in November 2024. Knowing Steve personally and professionally through his support of veteran and other organizations in Connecticut, I have witnessed firsthand how his hard-working, common-sense voice is exactly what we need advocating on our behalf in the Hartford Legislature.

Nationally and locally, and regardless of political affiliation, the economy overwhelmingly tops the list of what is important to voters this election year. Steve’s experience as an entrepreneur and small business owner, common sense approach to problem solving and experience representing the 55th District in Hartford make him the right choice for the challenges facing Connecticut today. His 100% voting record clearly shows his commitment to represent all constituents. As a state representative Steve earned the reputation of working hard to understand all sides of complicated issues, and then reaching across the aisle for collaboration without compromising his core values.

Rounding out his lifelong dedication to serving others, Steve also worked as a police officer, and on many local boards and community organizations spanning local business, athletics and youth services.

A lifelong resident of the district, he values and prioritizes family, hard work and service to his neighbors. Another important trait of Steve is that he listens. During one-on-one interactions, or in a sea of people at an event, Steve actively takes note of what all people have to say and uses their input to inform his decisions.

If you already know Steve Weir and his work for the 55th District, you have likely observed firsthand the attributes I describe. If you have yet to have the pleasure to meet him, I suggest you take the time to learn more and consider supporting him with your vote in November.

letters.headline: Same Shelf, Same Rules
letters.note: Sauyet is co-chair of the Andover Democratic Town Committee and a member of the RHAM Board of Education, but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: Sam Prentice says he has tried to understand what Democrats stand for. John Barnowski can speak for himself; I’ll explain what Ellen Paul and I said.

Our most important issue, he said? This fall I’ve written about town aid, pool fences, tenant safety, nursing homes and wage theft. My Banned Books Week letter turned halfway to hospital investors and absentee landlords.

He calls it outrageous that Ellen’s law “protects a library’s ability to carry books like the Bible as much as it protects books about gender identity.” That is not moral equivalence. It just means the same rules apply to both. The law bars removing a book because of its author’s views. That guards his shelf against those who dislike his views exactly as it guards other shelves against him.

In 2023 a Utah school district, acting on one person’s challenge, pulled the Bible from school shelves for vulgarity and violence. Anyone who has read Genesis 19, 2 Samuel 11, or Judges 19 knows what the reviewers found. Those chapters don’t make the Bible unfit for a library. They show why no single objector should decide what is on the shelf for everyone else’s child.

He compares book review to movie ratings. But ratings don’t pull a film from every theater because one patron objects. They inform parents, and families decide. Connecticut’s law works the same way: every library needs a written collection policy, and anyone objecting to a title gets a fair, consistent process.

Nor is raising the marriage age a contradiction. Marriage binds a child to an adult by contract. A library book binds no one, and a parent can return it. The Senate passed that law unanimously, the House 98 to 45, and Connecticut became the ninth state to end child marriage. Rep. Steve Weir voted no.
I’ve repeatedly debunked his minimum wage theory; no need to do so again.

Why do Democrats care about children not their own? Caring for other people’s children is the whole premise of public schools and libraries. As for education at six months, whatever he means, the 2025 early childhood bill passed the House 133 to 10. Weir was one of the ten.

He closes by wishing for more children and fewer Democrats. I’d settle for more children in well-funded schools, choosing from shelves filled by parents and librarians, not the loudest objector. On Nov. 3, that means Ellen Paul.
bills: HB 5003 (2025): early childhood care and education

letters.headline: Why Not Ellen Paul?
letters.note: Petit is a member of the Hebron Town Council but said he is writing this letter as an individual.
paragraphs: Our political system often leaves us choosing between a Republican and a Democrat. Both parties seem increasingly focused on appealing to the extremes rather than the voters in the middle. Too often, we’re left feeling like we’re choosing the lesser of two evils. Here’s why I’m voting for anyone but Ellen Paul.

First, the negativity. I’ve lived in the 55th District for 15 years, and one thing I’ve learned is that we don’t appreciate negative campaigning. If she can’t explain why she’s the better candidate without tearing down her opponent, what does that say about her ability to lead? We’re being asked to trade someone we know for someone whose approach we are being given a preview of. Her campaign manager believed negativity would work, and she chose that path rather than standing on her own merits. If she can’t push back against her own campaign team, how will she stand up to her party in Hartford when the 55th’s interests are on the line?

Second, the campaign promises. Her mailers promise to protect local control, deliver property tax relief, hold Eversource accountable, and declare that “it’s our turn to drive.” Look beyond the slogans. The Democrats she would join in Hartford have held power for decades, and the policies she promises to fight for are products of that same leadership. Everything she is “fighting” for was put in place by them. My first point proves that she can’t stand up to them. Where has the meaningful property tax relief been? While the state directs millions in taxpayer dollars toward Eversource-related rate relief, Connecticut families continue to shoulder the costs. We deserve more than recycled promises and political talking points.

Third, the constant references to Donald Trump. Again, she can’t run on her own merits, so she just keeps invoking his name. As an educated voter in the 55th, I am voting to send someone to Hartford, not Washington. We need a representative with a plan to address Connecticut’s problems, not someone whose primary strategy is blaming the feds. Frankly, few things are putting more pressure on my wallet than the decisions of Connecticut’s unchecked Democratic majority.

Ultimately, this election should be about leadership, accountability, and results – not attack mailers, party loyalty, or slogans. For these reasons, and plenty more reinforced by what keeps arriving in my mailbox, I’m voting for anyone but Ellen Paul.

letters.headline: Weir Asks for Reelection Support
paragraphs: Thank you for the honor of serving as your state representative for the past four years. The opportunity to represent the families, businesses, and communities of Andover, Bolton, Glastonbury, Hebron, and Marlborough is both a privilege and a responsibility I take very seriously.

Politics is the arena in which ideas are debated, common ground is found, and support is built to move those ideas forward. I have earned the endorsements of both the Republican and Independent Parties, validation that I have worked with colleagues on both sides of the aisle. Part of the job also requires building relationships and being an honest broker.

It’s easy for some to criticize without offering an alternative, but being a good representative requires one to sometimes compromise. Washington-type mudslinging is thankfully not how I’ve observed the inner workings at the Capitol. Representatives should also not go to Hartford to be a rubber stamp for a particular party. Good ideas come from many places, and reaching solutions requires listening and considering different perspectives.

I am also honored to have the support of the Glastonbury Police Officers Association, Connecticut Realtors, and the Connecticut Fraternal Order of Police, and to have received awards from several small business organizations, as small businesses are the drivers of our economy.

My perspective has been shaped by experiences beyond the State Capitol. As a nearly lifelong resident of the district, I’ve built businesses, created jobs, made payroll, and seen firsthand the pressures facing small employers and working families. My years in law enforcement taught me the importance of listening, exercising judgment, and helping people through difficult circumstances. Coaching youth basketball, supporting local charities, and volunteering in our communities have reinforced the responsibility we share to look out for one another.

The decisions made under the Golden Dome in Hartford are not abstract political exercises. I take the time to read the bills before me, listen to people with differing perspectives, ask questions, and carefully consider the consequences before deciding how to vote. The record shows that I voted with the House majority 77% of the time this past session. Nobody is going to agree 100% of the time.

I believe our district deserves a representative who listens, does the homework, considers the consequences, and approaches every decision with care and a strong sense of responsibility. I respectfully ask for your vote and the opportunity to continue serving as your State Representative.
State Rep. Steve Weir
R-55th District
Note: The 55th House District serves Andover, Hebron and Marlborough and parts of Bolton and Glastonbury.

letters.headline: Support of Steve Weir
paragraphs: I first met Steve Weir when our daughters played on the same high school volleyball team. We spent many evenings sitting on the bleachers, watching the girls play and talking about life, family, and our community. Through those conversations, I came to understand who Steve is at his core: a devoted husband and father of three daughters, and someone who shows up for the people around him.

Steve and his family are deeply engaged in our community. Their shared commitment to service is a cornerstone of their family life, reflecting values that inspire Steve’s work and dedication to the community. Whether volunteering with the Hebron Lions at the Hebron Fair or supporting dog rescue efforts, their family’s involvement is a living example of the care and responsibility they feel toward making this community better for everyone.

One evening, during a gathering of volleyball parents, Steve shared his background with me. I learned that he served as a police officer in Glastonbury before becoming a small business owner. A few days later, he texted me, recalling details from our conversation. That small gesture stood out to me. It showed how attentively he listens and how much he values the people he interacts with.

When Steve learned that my wife was exploring new career opportunities, he immediately offered guidance and support. He didn’t have to do that. But he did, because that’s who he is. He cares about the people in this community and wants to help where he can.

I am a father of two daughters, and Steve and I share common values rooted in family and community. This connection is evident in how attentively he listened to me and the support he offered my wife when she was exploring new career opportunities. His family reflects that same generosity and commitment through their volunteer work and community involvement. Getting to know Steve has shown me that he is thoughtful, engaged, and dedicated to serving the people of Hebron, Marlborough, Andover, Bolton, and Glastonbury.
I am proud to support Steve Weir for State Representative for Connecticut’s 55th District.

letters.headline: Osten & Paul for Progress
letters.note: Thiele is the chairwoman of the Hebron Town Council but is writing this letter as an individual.
paragraphs: Municipalities across Connecticut are struggling with the same problem: How to properly fund town services and schools without burdening taxpayers. That’s why we need active representation at the State Capitol – someone who understands these issues and is willing to fight for us. That’s why I support state Sen. Cathy Osten.

Cathy is a champion for small towns in eastern Connecticut. She understands the unique challenges we face and has fought for Hebron, Marlborough, and all towns represented by the 19th District. She has brought money back – money that helps us move important projects forward, or, simply cover the rising costs of doing basic town business. Last year alone, she voted to send more than $250K in extra money to Hebron to help with our schools’ budgets.

Cathy is a fighter. She advocates for fully funding excess cost, which would be a significant boost to our school budget. I know she will continue this fight in the next state budget. She supports labor – not just the right to organize, but the right to earn good wages and provide for a family. She is also present at nearly every significant event in Hebron. It matters when you can see your state senator on a regular basis and know she is fighting for you.

Cathy needs a reliable partner in Hartford to continue these efforts, and that’s why I’m voting for Ellen Paul for state representative. As a librarian, Ellen understands the importance of access to education and the need for funding. She will work with others to fix our outdated Education Cost Sharing grant funding, and alongside Cathy, will ensure that Hebron has a voice in Hartford.

Structural changes in Hartford are necessary for municipalities to thrive, and Cathy and Ellen are not afraid to advocate for these changes and solve problems. Showing up matters, and what you do with that time matters too. I’m proud to cast my vote for Cathy Osten and Ellen Paul.

letters.headline: Vote for Ellen Paul Now
paragraphs: The time for voting has started. You can vote from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily from now until Nov. 1. Ellen Paul is the person I am voting for because her values closely resemble the Connecticut values I grew up with. Among these are trust for information, and respect, fairness and opportunity for everyone. We need to have responsible governance in the 55th District.
Please get out there and vote. With the state of our current economy, now is the time to make your voice heard. Vote.
Please join me in voting for Ellen Paul.

letters.headline: Osten and Paul
letters.note: Larson is an alternate member of the Marlborough Zoning Board of Appeals but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: I was brought up in Connecticut and spent most of my life in this state. However, I have spent some years in other states attending school and working. After living in other states, I moved back to Connecticut when I remembered how great this state is to live and work in eventually settling down in Marlborough. I’m mentioning my travels because the reason I’m voting for Cathy Osten is that in the all the various places I have lived, I have never met a harder working politician or one who is as very effective as she is in her role as a representative. Although she is busy as co-chairman of the Senate appropriation committee, she has made a monthly commitment to be in each of the 10 towns she represents to inform them about what is happening in Hartford. She does this even in those years that were not her election years. She has been effective in Hartford getting bills passed dealing with both sexual harassment against state workers and setting up a registry for child molesters. She has also gotten grants and bills passed that benefit the towns she represents. She knows the issues of the towns in her district having served as a first selectmen. As a mother herself, she is familiar with the issues parents face on a day to day basis. She also volunteered to serve in the armed forces and was assigned to be an intelligent officer in Japan giving her insight into both the military and national security.

To continue to be truly effective in bringing many benefits to her towns, Cathy needs partners in the House of Representative. Ellen Paul would be such a partner. Ellen has shown how hard she can work as she has knocked on over 2,500 doors; democratic doors, republican doors and independent doors. More importantly, Ellen has outlined her positions in detailed as to what she wishes to accomplish as our representative, something that her opponent has not done. Furthermore, as a member of what will likely be the majority party in the house, she will have a seat at the table when important decisions are being made unlike her GOP opponent. In my opinion she will be a great representative.
I hope that you will join me in voting for Cathy and Ellen.

letters.headline: Vote for Steve Weir
paragraphs: I am writing to express my support to reelect Steve Weir as our state representative for the 55th District. He represents the values that I want to see in our State leaders. I have known Steve and his family for many years and I have seen firsthand how he has diligently volunteered to help many causes that are important to him. I have watched him coach youth sports; dedicate time to our church serving on the Board of Trustees and offering the sermon when requested; foster many dogs; and with his wife, raise three amazing daughters who share the same set of values that I respect.

Steve has dedicated many hours to serving this community and his constituents. I know that he truly reads every piece of legislation that he will vote on, and carefully considers his decision before casting his vote. I trust that his vote reflects what he believes will be the best for his constituents.
If you want a candidate who is trustworthy, dedicated, and willing to help anyone when necessary – then I hope you will join me in casting your vote for Steve Weir.

letters.headline: Ellen’s Democratic Party
paragraphs: Ellen Paul is misleading, when she says “there is no greater priority then sending more money to municipalities for education.” Where would Ellen Paul get this increased funding for education? It would come from increased taxes, of course, because taxation is the sole source for state spending. We have: state income tax, state sales tax, state utilities tax, state tax on services, state tax on licenses, state network tax, state gas tax, and more! Will Ellen Paul support increasing these taxes, or will she support finding a new area to tax?

Ellen Paul does not have a magic formula for a new income source. The source is always tax revenue. When towns are sent state funding, it is really our money that has been taken from us, via taxation, and then sent back to us. Sent back to us with restrictions on how it can be used! Perhaps we citizens should keep more of our money, and our local towns could decide our own education spending, without state mandates? Another wild idea – perhaps we citizens should object to all the extreme taxation mentioned above, and demand tax reform ? Have any of those taxes been lowered, or eliminated in 16 years of Democratic Party control?

Ellen Paul will comply with her Democratic Party. The party that has controlled Connecticut politics for 16 years. The Democratic Party that has implemented its agenda, restrictions and regulations that we live under today. Ellen Paul will not bring change.

letters.headline: Vote Early!!
paragraphs: In Connecticut, we now have the opportunity to vote early, prior to election day on November 3, 2026. Early voting began on Monday, Oct. 19.
More days to vote. More flexibility for you and me, the voters!

Fourteen days of in-person voting, including two weekends. Hours are 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., with extended hours, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m., Oct. 27-29. Contact your town hall for voting location. Early voting is available through Nov. 1.
The voters in Connecticut supported early voting in a referendum question in 2022. And the state legislature passed the implementation legislation in 2023.
I know quite a few people who have already voted on day 1. I will be one of the many to vote early.
FYI: our current state representative, Steve Weir, voted ‘no’ for early voting. Our current state senator, Cathy Osten, voted ‘yes’ for early voting.
Your vote! Your right! Exercise it!

letters.headline: Steve Weir Is Every ‘Weir’
paragraphs: There is something to be said for a person who doesn’t simply talk about community but is part of it.

Steve Weir’s connection to Hebron and the surrounding area isn’t something that appears when campaign signs start going up like so many others that we see this time of year. What stands out is his presence in the community, his willingness to volunteer, talk with residents, listen, and simply show up.

Every year, elections bring mailers, campaign slogans, political talking points, and plenty of noise. But beneath all of that is a much simpler question: Who truly knows the people they hope to represent vs. who wants just the position.

Representation is about more than having your name printed on a ballot. It’s about being present when there isn’t an election around the corner. It’s about knowing your neighbors, participating in your community, volunteering alongside the people who live there, and understanding the things that matter to them because they matter to you, too.

Anyone who has had a conversation with Steve knows how deeply he cares about this community. You don’t need a campaign flyer to tell you. Talk to him. Ask him a question. Have a conversation at the door or when you see him around town. His connection to the community becomes apparent very quickly. He will listen to you. His candidacy is run on values and his love for this community, and that is what one should want in a representative.

As voters head to the polls, I hope we can look beyond political rhetoric and ask ourselves what kind of representation we value. Do we want someone who simply campaigns in our community, or someone who is genuinely part of our community?
It’s about being seen, involved, and present all year long.
And around Hebron and the surrounding towns, Steve Weir seems to be everywhere. Or maybe I should say… every “Weir.”

letters.headline: Steve Weir Works for Us!
paragraphs: When I think about whom I want representing the community, I think about someone who lives with the same concerns we all have. Steve Weir votes with commitment to fiscal responsibility which benefits the community’s best interest. When Steve votes on a bill, he votes for what’s on the inside, taking time to carefully read it and not just looking at the name of the bill.

I have known Steve for over three years and anytime I have a concern on a matter he doesn’t hesitate to call me and answer my questions. He is an honest person and will tell you the way it is. He will always find time to attend, volunteer his time at any type of event.
I will again be supporting Steve Weir for the House of Representatives, 55th District. I look forward to more of his honest leadership. Please join me by supporting Steve this November.

letters.headline: Common Sense That Makes Sense.
paragraphs: This election cycle, I’m seeing so much emphasis placed on the letter next to a candidate’s name. But shouldn’t we be looking beyond the D or the R and focusing on the person, their record, and their ability to make thoughtful, informed decisions?
I’ve had the opportunity to talk with Steve Weir about his voting record and hear him explain the reasoning behind certain bills. More than once, I’ve found myself thinking, “Yes, that makes sense.”
Those conversations have given me a better understanding of his approach to the issues and reinforced why I support him.

We need representatives who think critically, ask questions, and consider the bigger picture— not simply vote along party lines. We need people willing to look at the issues, weigh the options, and make decisions based on what they believe is right for the people they represent.
At the end of the day, leadership should be about more than party politics. It should be about thoughtful decisions, sound policies, and good old-fashioned common sense.
Steve Weir. Common Sense That Makes Sense.

letters.headline: I’m Voting For Ellen Paul
paragraphs: Ten days to go and still no answers!!

State Rep. Steve Weir has refused to publicly answer why he voted ‘no’ to increasing state dollars to towns for education, municipal expenses in FY 26-27; why he voted ‘no’ to supporting women’s reproductive/healthcare initiatives (HB7213-2025). Why he voted ‘no’ to extending programs for renewable energy sources (HB5340-2025).
All of these bills would lighten the burden on residents of all residents in Connecticut, yet Rep. Wier voted ‘no.’

We elect public officials to support our views and values. When elected officials are asked questions we should expect answers. To date we still don’t know Why he votes “NO” on bills that would help his constituents!

I have reviewed his recent mailers and past letters to the editors and agree 100% that Steve is a very nice man and a caring individual. He volunteers in his community. He is a protector of animals and often is involved helping members in the community.
However, his voting record in the House does not support these values.
We need a representative in Hartford that not only represents our values but votes to support them.
Ellen Paul is just that person!!

Ellen supports increased state funding for Towns and Schools. She understands that when programs don’t work that funding needs to be redirected or eliminated as a means of being fiscally responsible. She will make industries such as Eversource more accountable to their end users by creating policies that make consumers most important and demand that accountability and long-term planning become built into the process.

With the national and world economy in shambles, we need a leader who can make “the tough decisions.” As a former aid to Congressman Joe Courtney, Ellen has viewed these issues from a much more complex level than her opponent has.

Ellen has demonstrated skills in working across the aisle and building consensus for the good of all people. She learned these while working at the federal level and continues them today as executive director of the Connecticut Library Consortium.
Voters of the 55th House District need a change. Let’s make that change by electing Ellen Paul as our new state representative.
Ellen will “Support and Defend Connecticut Values”. That is why I am voting for Ellen Paul.
Please Join me!!!

letters.headline: In Appreciation of Steve Weir
paragraphs: I am writing to express my heartfelt gratitude and admiration for state Rep. Steve Weir. In a time when public trust in government can be difficult to earn, Rep. Weir consistently demonstrated the kind of principled, tireless dedication that reminds us why civic service matters. As a Hebron Lions member, I have been privileged to work with Steve at many Community Service events.

From the moment he took office, he made it his mission to listen — truly listen — to the people of our district. Whether attending community town halls, responding personally to constituent concerns, or showing up at local events, he has never lost sight of the fact that his role is to serve the families, businesses, and neighbors who call the 55th District home.

Steve’s legislative record speaks for itself. He has championed initiatives that strengthen our local economy, improve infrastructure, support our schools, and protect the well-being of our most vulnerable residents. He approaches every issue with thoughtfulness and integrity, seeking common ground where others might see only division. His willingness to work across the aisle has resulted in meaningful progress for our community — progress that improves daily life in tangible, lasting ways.

Beyond his legislative accomplishments, it is Steve’s character that sets him apart. He is accessible, honest, and genuinely invested in the future of our district. He does not simply represent us in the statehouse — he advocates for us with conviction and passion.
The 55th District is fortunate to have a representative of Steve Weir’s caliber. His hard work, dedication, and unwavering commitment to our community deserve recognition and our deepest
A Proud Constituent of the 55th District,

letters.headline: Madame Librarian/Egalitarian!
letters.note: Dunn is a member of the Marlborough Democratic Town Committee but said she is speaking as an individual.
paragraphs: Many of us remember how librarians used to be characterized; sit behind a desk, checking books in and out, often sternly saying “Ssh”, reprimanding most adamantly if a book was a day over due and so forth. At least that is my recollection from small town Iowa librarians, except, perhaps, for Marian in the “Music Man.”

The best librarians today like Ellen Paul, can be seen as innovative and visionary, experienced in acquiring books and maintaining the standards of their library’s collection. She successfully led East Hampton’s library for 6 years, increasing book lending, supporting, initiating and offering programs for the community.

Her career then took her in a new direction, leading the Connecticut Library Consortium. The consortium brings together over 1,000 libraries in Connecticut to find ways to better serve their communities. Recognized as a strategic collaborator, Ellen was designated a “Mover and Shaker” by the Library Journal Movers and Shakers 2026 The 2026 class honors emerging leaders, innovators, advocates, and community builders

This same vision and vigor are needed to represent the constituents of the 55th District. Let’s send an experienced collaborator and galvanizer of energy to Hartford to speak up and develop policies that improve the communities of the 55th. Ellen Paul knows how to analyze needs, develop strategies and carry out those plans. She is recognized across the state not just for thinking about how to support and champion libraries she gets out and does it. She will apply this highly valued skill to her duties as a representative of the people.

Constituents of the 55th, we finally can elect a representative who will jump right in and build relationships and prioritize the needs of seniors, working families, schools, housing and more East of the river.

In her capacity of director of the statewide Library Consortium, not only has she already advocated for and shepherded bills through committees and onto the floor for successful votes, she has two more successes in that regard than does her opponent who has none.
She has knocked on over 2,500 doors and listened to voters concerns and hopes that she will now take to Hartford.
A vote for Ellen Paul means a stronger voice among the decision makers in Hartford.

letters.headline: Voting for Weir
paragraphs: I would like to urge you to consider voting for Steve Weir for state representative, as I will be. Having known Steve for many years, I can speak to his passion for service to the community of the 55th District and I trust in his ethics. Discussing Connecticut political issues with Steve, I am amazed that the details of many bills are often presented at the last minute to his office, with little time before a vote. Steve takes pride in sifting through the many layers of detail, often revealing the unrelated “pork” tacked onto the larger body of the bill. This, of course, guides his vote.

Something you may not know is that Steve has voted with the majority 77% of the time. Therefore, I feel it is disingenuous to label him as “extreme” as it been suggested during this campaign season. I encourage you to speak with Steve about the rest of those bills as I have. The news media is not revealing all of the layers rolled into many of these bills. Anyone with an open mind will find these discussions enlightening.

I am so thankful that we have a thorough, trustworthy legislator in Steve. He asks the necessary questions when these bills have serious flaws and doesn’t vote only on the misleading and catchy surface headlines we see in the news.

Thank you, Steve, for your dedication. And thank you for educating me to the real, behindthe-scenes dealings at the capitol here in Hartford. I appreciate you helping to keep Connecticut’s political machine in check! You have my vote!

letters.headline: Who Really Represents Change?
letters.note: Beaulieu is a member of the RHAM Board of Education, but is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: There has been a great deal of talk lately about “change,” but many letters ignore one simple fact: Connecticut has been governed by Democratic majorities for the past 16 years. Yet voters are being told that voting against Steve Weir is somehow a vote for change. Don’t fall for that argument.

The status quo is not change. The policies that have shaped Connecticut for nearly two decades are not change. Steve Weir, Jason Guidone, Ryan Fazio, and George Austin represent a different direction and a new approach.

While some politicians celebrate expanding government programs, Jason Guidone and Steve Weir are focused on creating the economic opportunities that help people achieve independence and self-reliance. The path from government dependency to prosperity is through a stronger economy, more jobs, and greater opportunity.

In the past eight years, businesses have continued to leave the state, property crime remains a concern in many communities, and parents, teachers, students, and administrators have become increasingly frustrated by education policies driven from Hartford. Too often, residents hear that nothing can be done.
Something can be done. Elections are about choices.
If you want real change, vote for Steve Weir, Ryan Fazio, Jason Guidone, and George Austin.

letters.headline: Highly Recommend Paul
paragraphs: The upcoming election gives us all a chance to choose the best state representation – one that syncs with the needs and morals of our community.
I’ve had the honor of getting to know Ellen Paul and highly recommend supporting her.

I met Ellen at a town meeting in June and was immediately inspired by her energy and passion. As a librarian, Ellen has her pulse on the community’s needs and understands the issues that are crucial to voters in her district. Her profession has taught her to be curious by nature, to do her research, and look at the facts. She is a commonsense politician driven by firsthand knowledge from interacting with community members and by her own convictions, not by the man in the White House. She will be an excellent state representative for the 55th District.
When you vote in this election, vote for the candidates who are not beholden to the agendas of others, and instead will best serve you. When you vote, make sure Ellen gets your vote.

letters.headline: Supports Paul and Osten
letters.note: Vice Chair, Hebron Town Council
paragraphs: Serving in local government has given me a firsthand understanding of the challenges facing our communities. Every budget season brings difficult decisions about maintaining quality public schools, providing essential services, protecting taxpayers, and supporting the people who make our communities work.
These challenges make our representation in Hartford particularly important.

Ellen Paul, candidate for state representative in the 55th District, has made education funding and property tax relief central priorities of her campaign. She supports updating Connecticut’s Education Cost Sharing formula, increasing state support for special education, and ensuring that state mandates do not place unreasonable financial burdens on municipalities.

State Sen. Cathy Osten brings extensive experience in municipal government and public service. As Senate Chair of the Appropriations Committee, she has played a significant role in state budget decisions affecting education, municipal assistance, and essential public services. Her experience in local government provides a valuable perspective on the challenges facing Connecticut’s towns and cities.

From my experience, I know that strong schools, responsible budgets, and support for working families are not competing priorities. They are interconnected responsibilities that require cooperation between state and local government.

Hebron and the surrounding communities deserve a thoughtful discussion about how Connecticut can maintain excellent schools, make life more affordable, reduce the burden on local property taxpayers, and protect the services residents depend upon.

I support Ellen Paul for state representative and Cathy Osten for state senator because of their focus on the issues that matter to our communities. I encourage voters to consider their records, experience, and priorities as they make their decisions on Nov. 3.

letters.headline: Continuing the Democratic Success
letters.note: Golfin is co-vice chair of the Marlborough Democratic Town Committee and a member of the RHAM Board of Education, but is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: After many years of Democratic leadership in Hartford government, we can be proud of Connecticut’s performance relative to the rest of the nation. For instance, according to the State Department of Education, our students in 4th and 8th grade rank among the top in national test scores in reading and math; we have the second lowest rate of violent crime in the nation (FBI); we rank fifth in terms of life expectancy (CDC); and the U.S. Census Bureau indicates that our median household income is 17% higher than the national average while our high school graduation rate is above average. Yes, there is more to do, and Ellen Paul knows what our top concerns are because she has listened to us, having knocked on more than 3,000 doors so far. Ellen Paul is ready to continue to make Connecticut excel among the states.

For instance, Ellen will work to continue our great educational success and shift the tax burden more broadly with local property tax relief through a revision of the educational cost sharing formula. And she will work on affordable housing and lowering our energy costs while protecting our environment and our families.
Please join me in voting for Ellen Paul for the 55th House District on Nov. 3rd.

letters.headline: One Neighbor to Another
paragraphs: By now the mailers have piled up and the signs are everywhere, so let me try to put the choice in the 55th District plainly, one neighbor to another.

Ellen Paul is a librarian and nonprofit executive from Glastonbury. She leads the Connecticut Library Consortium, working with more than 1,000 libraries of every kind to deliver better services for less money. She wants to modernize the state’s school funding formula so our property taxes stop absorbing what the state should share. She wants more homes ordinary families can afford, utilities answerable to the people who pay the bills, and legislators bound by real accountability rules: term limits, no stock trading in office, regular town halls. Her whole career has been listening and building agreement, and it shows in how she campaigns. This is the kind of representation that the 55th district needs.
On Nov. 3, or before it if voting early suits you better, I hope you will join me in choosing Ellen Paul. Learn more at ellenforstaterep.com, and check your voting options at myvote.ct.gov.

letters.headline: Paul for State Representative
letters.note: Chair, Hebron Democratic Town Committee
paragraphs: I am writing as chair of the Hebron Democratic Town Committee to express my support for Ellen Paul for State Representative in Connecticut’s 55th District.

Ellen has been working tirelessly every day since January to connect with the people in our community. She has knocked on more than 3,000 doors, taking the time to meet residents, listen to their concerns, and hear what matters most to them. That kind of dedication speaks volumes about her commitment to representing the people of our district.

What stands out to me about Ellen is that she listens, she understands that being a representative is about more than making promises; it is about hearing people’s concerns, understanding their values, and working hard to represent them. Her values reflect the values that matter to so many of us in our community. She is a nice person and she listens.

Ellen is a librarian, the executive director of the Library Consortium, and also a wife and a mother of two children. Like so many families in our district, she understands the importance of family and the everyday concerns that affect our lives. She is putting in the time and effort to earn the trust of the people she hopes to represent. She will bring progress to our towns.

Now, it is up to us to do our part. We need to get out and vote! Elections are decided by the people who show up, and every vote matters. If we want a representative who takes the time to listen, works hard, and cares about our community, we need to make our voices heard at the polls.
Please join me in voting for Ellen Paul for state representative in the 55th District.
Let’s get out the vote and make our voices count on Nov. 3rd!

letters.headline: Asking for the Opportunity
paragraphs: Over the past several weeks, I have written about why I am running for state representative and what I have learned from knocking on more than 3,000 doors across our district.

I have heard concerns about property taxes and the cost of electricity. I have talked with parents wondering whether their children will be able to afford a home here and seniors who want to downsize without leaving the communities they love. I have heard how deeply people value our schools and how strongly they want to protect the farms, forests and open spaces that make Eastern Connecticut special.
Those conversations have reinforced something I believed before I ever decided to run: good government starts with listening.

I have spent my career in public service. I am a librarian, a nonprofit executive and a former staff member for Congressman Joe Courtney. I have worked with people across Connecticut and across the political aisle to solve problems, navigate complicated public policy and get things done.

That experience has taught me that government can work. But it requires people who are willing to listen, learn, compromise when appropriate, stand firm when necessary, and remember who they work for.

I believe in strong public schools and communities people can afford to call home. I believe in responsible government, equal rights under the law, and decisions grounded in facts and expertise. I believe we can disagree without treating one another as enemies. And I believe elected office is public service, not an entitlement.
Most of all, I believe representation requires showing up.

I have tried to do that throughout this campaign. I have knocked on doors regardless of the party registration behind them because I want to understand the people I am asking to represent. I will bring that same approach to Hartford.
I never expected to run for office. But I stepped forward because I believe this district deserves thoughtful, accessible and accountable representation.
Now I am asking for the opportunity to serve.
I want to earn your vote. And if elected, I intend to keep earning it every day.

letters.headline: Paul Gets My Vote
paragraphs: Ellen Paul gets my vote for representative in the 55th District.
Please visit her website, ellenforstaterep. com/#issues, to read about her positions on legislation that affects us all.
Some important quotes from Ellen Paul ..
“Affordable energy isn’t a luxury. It’s essential.”
“Growing older shouldn’t mean being priced out of the community you call home.”
“Connecticut’s Education Cost Sharing formula hasn’t been updated since 2013.”
“Government has a responsibility to set reasonable guardrails so that technology serves people, not the other way around.”
“When we invest in families, we invest in Connecticut’s future.”
“When bills reach my desk, I won’t look for a political angle. I’ll ask one question: does this make life better and safer for the people of the 55th District? If the answer is yes, so is my vote.”

“I’ll work to modernize the Education Cost Sharing formula so it reflects today’s costs and delivers real property tax relief for the families of Andover, Bolton, Glastonbury, Hebron, and Marlborough.”

“I’ll fight for stronger property tax relief for older homeowners and help for renters, real accountability for utility companies, and access to the health care, prescription help, transportation, and services that let seniors live safely and independently. When a bill helps our neighbors stay in their homes, I’ll vote yes.”
Yes, I believe that Ellen Paul will read bills thoroughly, and I believe that she will make decisions that help the people she will represent.
My vote is for Ellen Paul. With her in office, I will feel truly represented.

letters.headline: Ellen Ready to Deliver
letters.note: Wilkinson is a member of the Marlborough Democratic Town Committee but said she is speaking as an individual.
paragraphs: In her campaign, Ellen Paul has knocked on over 2,700 doors. Here’s what Ellen heard, and what she ready to fight for...

· Property tax relief: Ellen will work to modernize the Education Cost Sharing formula to reflect today’s costs and ease the burden on families in Andover, Bolton, Glastonbury, Hebron, and Marlborough.
· Lower electric bills: Ellen will vote for more homegrown energy and for accountability. More supply means more competition and fewer price spikes.
· Strong schools: Endorsed by the Connecticut Education Association, Ellen will fight for resources from early childhood through graduation.
· Fair treatment for workers: Ellen will stand with eastern Connecticut’s workers, because an economy only works when it works for the people doing the work.
· Growth without losing our landscapes: Ellen backs new homes and a stronger economy, and will vote to protect clean water, open space, and clean air.
· Secure, accessible voting: Ellen will never vote to make participating harder.
· A representative who answers to us: Ellen will back good ideas from either party, say so when their own party gets it wrong, and answers to five towns, not a caucus.
Ellen listened, understands what matters to us, and is ready to deliver. For a representative who will work for the 55th District, Ellen Paul will fight for you.

letters.headline: Common Sense: Steve Weir
paragraphs: Steve Weir is our best representative for the 55th District. Steve has honed a great deal of common sense through his career serving as a state police officer, businessman, and legislator. We need and must use every opportunity to bring common sense legislation to Connecticut I am a longtime resident of Hebron and Rep. Weir has been an excellent neighbor throughout.

Steve always listens closely to opinions and studies issues and makes common sense decisions that are in the best interest of the 55th District. Never have I heard, read or seen Steve use derogatory innuendo to sway an opinion or garner a vote. Doing so is far beyond what we expect of any person asking to represent us the problems that his opponent promises to fix are the problems generated by the Democrats dominated legislature.
Please join me and vote for Rep. Weir this November.

letters.headline: Osten and Paul for Marlborough
letters.note: Fidler is a member of the Marlborough Board of Finance but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: The Democratic ticket representing Marlborough offers the right combination of proven leadership and fresh perspective: incumbent Cathy Osten for the 19th State Senate District and Ellen Paul for the 55th House District. Together, they would bring the experience, energy, and commitment needed to serve our community.

Cathy Osten has consistently championed the needs of small towns throughout eastern Connecticut. As a multi-term state senator and cochair of the Appropriations Committee, she has helped shape state budget priorities that balance Connecticut’s needs with the growing financial pressures facing residents and municipalities. Her priorities have included additional Education Cost Sharing funding for local schools, $100 million in state grants to municipalities, increased support for HUSKY Health to help address rising healthcare costs for vulnerable residents, and investments in early childhood education and childcare to support families and providers.

Cathy also understands the importance of preserving the rural character and open spaces that make our communities special. She was instrumental in securing recent state grants totaling $390,000 for Marlborough and Hebron to support the Bernstein Trail and Blackledge River Greenway Trail. Her experience, leadership, and understanding of the challenges facing our region make her a valuable voice in Hartford.

At the same time, effective representation benefits from new ideas and a fresh perspective. Ellen Paul brings a strong record of public service, professional expertise, and a commitment to delivering results. A librarian, nonprofit executive, and former staff member for Congressman Joe Courtney, Ellen has worked across multiple levels of government and understands how to turn ideas into meaningful progress.

As executive director of the Connecticut Library Consortium, she works with more than 1,000 libraries to improve public services, reduce costs for taxpayers, and expand access to information. Her work with the General Assembly has helped advance landmark, bipartisan legislation protecting library access and intellectual freedom. Ellen’s priorities reflect the concerns of families throughout our region: property tax relief, strong public schools, lower energy costs, support for Connecticut seniors, stronger families, and preserving Eastern Connecticut’s rural character and green spaces. You can learn more about Ellen and her positions at www.ellenforstaterep.com.

Marlborough deserves representatives who understand our communities, recognize the pressures facing our families, and are committed to finding practical solutions. Together, these candidates would make a formidable team for Marlborough and Eastern Connecticut. Please join me in voting for Cathy Osten and Ellen Paul this Election Day.

letters.headline: More Than Politics
letters.note: Tyler is a member of the Hebron Zoning Board of Appeals but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: Our communities have changed considerably over the decades. Steve Weir and I both grew up in Glastonbury. Our families both moved to Hebron and our kids have gone through the RHAM school system together. In this community, families have built lasting friendships through the schools, sports, churches, and volunteer organizations.

These communities are about more than politics. They’re about neighbors helping neighbors, parents supporting their kid’s activities, and people giving their time to make their towns better places to live.

Steve Weir has been part of the Hebron community for more than 26 years. His involvement has extended well beyond elected office, including church activities, supporting local youth sports, AHM Youth and Family Services, small businesses, our schools, and assisting individual families in times of need.
That history deserves to be considered alongside his legislative record.

Serving in Hartford requires more than simply voting ‘yes’ or ‘no.’ Legislation can be complicated, and bills sometimes contain provisions that are unrelated to their stated purpose or carry unintended consequences. Careful scrutiny is not obstruction. Asking difficult questions, examining the details, and considering the consequences are important responsibilities of any legislator.

The increasingly negative tone of this campaign also deserves reflection. Political opponents have every right to disagree about legislation and public policy. We as voters deserve those debates. But campaign advertising that reduces complicated legislative decisions to inflammatory accusations can leave residents with an incomplete understanding of the issues.

Ultimately, a representative’s record should be evaluated in its entirety: legislative diligence, accessibility, constituent service, community involvement, and a willingness to listen to people across political lines.
Our district deserves a thoughtful discussion of those qualities and the issues affecting our towns, rather than a campaign dominated by personal attacks.

letters.headline: A Desire to Fix the Issues
paragraphs: My name is Steve Capetta and I have had the privilege of being married to Ellen Paul for over 12 years. Ellen has been community minded the entire time I have known her, from being part of a community volunteer organization 15 years ago when we met to her work today at the Connecticut Library Consortium, where she fights to both keep peoples’ access to choose the books they want and make sure libraries and towns aren’t forced to pay exorbitant prices for e-books.

Before declaring to run for state representative, Ellen and I used to spend the evenings discussing what was happening in the news after we put our kids to bed. As I am sure everyone else was, we were especially worried about what was happening nationally, especially in Minnesota. We were concerned about what type of world we were raising our daughters in and how much worse things look like they are going to be. Ellen decided she needed to do something about it and started writing letters to her representatives. When she saw a lack of action from Hartford, unlike most of us, myself included, she felt the need to get even more involved. She came to me soon after to discuss her running for state representative.

Ellen isn’t politically ambitious; she has a real desire to fix the issues facing our community, from rising prices to the quality and safety of our schools. She is driven by the desire to make the world better for our children, your children, and all of us. I know she is capable of doing this; she is the smartest and hardest-working person I have ever met.
I know Ellen will bring honesty, perseverance, and thoughtful leadership to Hartford. I hope you will join me in voting for Ellen Paul for State Representative of the 55th district.

letters.headline: Reelect Steve Weir!
paragraphs: Steve has always shown competency, is extremely thorough and takes his responsibilities as our state representative to the next level.
During the campaign season, he has proven over and over that he works for his district. Always kind, always considerate and always willing to listen.
The fact that he reads a bill from page one to the end before he decides what’s best for us, shows his commitment.
There’s no negativity; just positive results.

letters.headline: Why I Support Ellen Paul
paragraphs: Ellen Paul stands for the issues that matter to me. As a retired UConn faculty member, I understand the importance of public education in training the next generation. Paul is a strong supporter for public education and is endorsed by the Connecticut Education Association, the state’s largest organization advocating for teachers and students. She will work to update the Connecticut’s Education Cost Sharing formula so that it will strengthens public schools and provides meaningful tax relief for local families. Eastern Connecticut is blessed with farms, forests, lakes and protected open space. Paul supports preservation of our natural resources by thoughtful and well-planned development.
That is why I am voting for Ellen Paul for state representative on Nov. 3, and why I hope you will take a look at her yourself.

letters.headline: Two Excellent Women for CT
paragraphs: This letter is in support of two tireless workers, state Sen. Cathy Osten and Ellen Paul.

Senator Osten has been our state senator for the 19th District for the past 14 years. She has been instrumental in helping Hebron through several projects that she has appropriated money to: $2 million for a generator for RHAM High School to make it a Regional Emergency Shelter, $500,000 to offset the cost of a new fire truck, sidewalks in Hebron Center and around RHAM, and $1,00,000 to replace lead water pipes in Hebron Elementary School. She listens to the needs of our town, as she does in every town in the 19th District. Her attention to what we need makes our towns better places to live in. Her work at the State Capitol has created energy assistance programs, funding for veterans, manufacturing jobs, special-needs children, seniors and making sure every child in the State has breakfast waiting for them in their school. This is just a partial listing. Senator Osten fights daily to make Connecticut a better place to live for everyone.

Ellen Paul decided to run for the 55th District House of Representatives because she wants to make a difference. She is a person who brings consensus to groups in her role as executive director of the Connecticut Library Consortium. Ellen plans to bring that skill with her to the Capitol. She has already been instrumental in advocating for laws such as Connecticut’s content/e-book laws that protect our libraries from unfair publishing contracts. She is ready to fight for lower property taxes, protecting our public schools, and defending our right to read materials that we want to read. Ellen will champion women’s health issues if elected. In Ellen’s quest for the 55th District House Seat she has knocked on over 5,000 doors to mee the voters in her district.
Sen. Cathy Osten and candidate Ellen Paul deserve your vote on Nov. 3rd. Please vote for them.

letters.headline: Weir Open About Stance
paragraphs: I have known Steve Weir for about five years and over that relatively short period I have learned much about him and his values. Steve has lived in Hebron for more than two decades and was elected in November 2022 to represent Andover, Bolton, Glastonbury, Hebron and Marlborough. He isn’t a career politician. He’s a former small business owner and understands how State policy impacts people who employ our friends and neighbors while balancing budgets and watching expenses. And as the Ranking Republican on the Labor & Public Employees Committee, he provides real insight on legislative changes that can build a better economic climate and create more jobs in Connecticut. Something we could all be proud of.

Steve is open about where he stands on the issues, which I greatly appreciate. He has opposed state budgets he felt weren’t sustainable, and he has spoken out on protecting individual and religious freedoms. You may not agree with him on every issue, but you will always know where he stands and that he will be in the room when the votes are cast.
Join me and vote to re-elect state Rep. Steve Weir on Nov. 3.

letters.headline: Support for Steve Weir
paragraphs: I have known Steve Weir for more than 30 years, having grown up in the same town. As fellow small-business owners, we understand firsthand the challenges of operating a business in Connecticut, including navigating complex government regulations, managing rising costs, remaining financially viable, and keeping employees on the payroll. This practical experience is invaluable when shaping public policy and making decisions in Hartford.

Strong, growing businesses are essential to Connecticut’s economic health and the prosperity of its residents. High taxes and burdensome regulations have made it increasingly difficult for businesses to succeed, prompting some companies to relocate to states with a more favorable business climate. Connecticut needs leadership that understands these challenges and recognizes that a thriving economy benefits everyone.

Steve also brings valuable experience from his career as a police officer. He understands the challenges facing our first responders and what they need from government to protect our communities effectively. The willingness to put one’s life on the line to protect others speaks volumes about a person’s character, dedication, and commitment to public service. Steve also understands the devastating impact violent crime can have on a family. He recognizes the importance of holding criminals accountable and pursuing policies that protect innocent people from becoming victims.

Raising a family in Connecticut is neither easy nor inexpensive. Steve understands that every tax increase and unfunded mandate imposed by the state ultimately affects household budgets. Families are working hard to manage the rising costs of everyday life, including housing, groceries, and utilities. They deserve leadership that respects their hard work, takes their financial concerns seriously, and works to make Connecticut a more affordable place to live and raise a family.

I believe it is time to take a serious look at our state’s direction and consider a different approach. Connecticut needs policies that encourage economic growth, support working families, strengthen public safety, and make our state more competitive.

If you want a Connecticut with more affordable utility costs, lower taxes, a stronger business climate, safer communities, and an economy that attracts families and employers rather than driving them away, I encourage you to support Steve Weir’s reelection.

letters.headline: Paul Will Make a Difference
paragraphs: Before the campaign signs come down, it is worth asking a simple question: what do we actually want from the people we send to Hartford?

Ellen Paul, running for state representative in the 55th District, has given the clearest answer I have heard in years: “Elected office should be public service, not a lifetime job or an opportunity for personal profit.” Those are her words, and her platform matches them. She supports reasonable term limits. She would bar legislators from trading individual stocks while in office. She would have every legislator hold regular public town halls in the towns they represent, so that answering to voters is a habit, not a campaign-season performance.

It fits everything else in her career. Ellen is a librarian and nonprofit executive who leads the Connecticut Library Consortium, working with more than 1,000 libraries of every kind to improve services and save taxpayers money. She served on Congressman Joe Courtney’s staff. She has spent her working life listening, building coalitions, and delivering results without drama.

We spend a lot of energy every fall arguing about who politicians are. Here is a candidate telling us plainly what the job is, and volunteering to be held to it. That is what public service should look like. On Nov. 3, I am voting for Ellen Paul, and I hope you will look at her yourself: ellenforstaterep.com.

letters.headline: What Is It About Ellen?
paragraphs: I have asked myself what is it that makes me so sure Ellen Paul should represent the 55th in the state legislature. To be sure, she is outgoing, lovely, warm and friendly. It is a pleasure to engage when she knocks on the door to seek your vote. But in no way would that be enough.
It is the thoughtful and thought-provoking content of her message. You know what she stands for.

She has spoken at length to the legislature to affect policy. She has been successful in keeping libraries free to get e-books and keeping books on the shelves that others would ban. She acts on the belief that citizens should be free to read.
She is committed to her efforts to modernize Connecticut’s education cost sharing formula so it actually reflects today’s costs and results in real property tax relief for us.

She has proven herself to be a leader who brings people together for the common good and achieves benefit for everyone. She listens, cares, and acts. She sincerely wants to be a voice for our five towns.
She is a fierce believer in voting rights and is committed to making the ability to vote safe, convenient and accessible.
Above all, Ellen is clear and direct in stating her beliefs, intentions, and reasoning.
It is no wonder the Connecticut Education Association and the Connecticut Working Families Party have endorsed Ellen Paul. By my one vote, I will endorse her too.

letters.headline: Ellen, Due Nov. 3
letters.note: Sauyet is co-chair of the Andover Democratic Town Committee and a member of the RHAM Board of Education, but said he is writing as an individual.
paragraphs: In September I wrote here about the librarians who shaped my life, and said that November 3 would give me the chance to hand something back. That day is nearly here, so let me finish the story with what I’ve learned about Ellen Paul since.

She never expected to run for office. She was raised, she says, to believe that citizenship means more than voting, and that when you can make a difference, you step forward. She grew up in Mansfield and lives in Glastonbury with her husband and two daughters, and she has been stepping forward for years.

She spent four years working with a Republican senator, Tony Hwang, on a library e-book bill. When it passed the Senate 35 to 1 in 2025, she said she was “just overjoyed that we finally got it across the finish line.” That same year she helped pass the freedom-to-read law, which she says protects a library’s ability to carry the Bible as much as books about gender identity. In May, Library Journal named her one of its Movers and Shakers.
That is the habit I want in Hartford: find the people who disagree with you, listen, and get the work done anyway.

Her plans are practical. Modernize the school funding formula, untouched since 2013, so property taxes stop covering the gap. Build homes that teachers, nurses and young families can afford. Put ratepayers first on electric bills. Keep our farms and forests, because, as she puts it, some things can be rebuilt but our green places are gone forever once they’re gone. And require legislators to hold regular public town halls in the towns they represent.

She also believes some votes should be easy. Protecting children. Keeping seniors safe. When those bills come up, she promises to ask one question: does this make life better and safer for the people of the 55th? If so, she votes yes.
Early voting runs through Sunday, Nov. 1. On Tuesday, Nov. 3, polls are open from 6 a.m. to 8 p.m., and you can even register that day. Everything you need is at myvote.ct.gov.
More than once, a librarian handed me the right book at the right moment. On Tuesday, we can hand one the right job. Please vote for Ellen Paul.

letters.headline: Character Matters
paragraphs: I have known Steve Weir and his family for five years, ever since our daughters played volleyball together. I have come to know Steve as a genuinely good person whose character and values I respect. While I am proud to call him a friend, my support for his re-election to the state House of Representatives goes beyond our personal connection. It is based on who he is and the leadership he brings to his role.
When choosing a candidate, I look at character, values, and what that person stands for. I want someone honest, transparent, respectful, and committed to doing the job.

Throughout this campaign, Steve has remained focused on his constituents. Steve is willing to discuss his positions and voting record with anyone who asks. Voters should judge him on his record, not inflammatory labels.

As a machine shop owner, I appreciate Steve’s appointment to the Connecticut Career Pathways Commission, recognizing his industry experience and business expertise. The commission connects schools, higher education, workforce boards, and employers to address talent pipeline gaps. Having experienced the difficulty of finding skilled tradespeople firsthand, I am grateful Steve is helping create student opportunities while supporting Connecticut businesses and industries.

I have also heard claims that Steve does not care about senior citizens. In 2026, he introduced three bills proposing tax relief: HB 5104 concerning meals purchased from restaurants, caterers, and grocery stores; HB 5105 exempting residential handicap ramps from sales and use taxes; and HB 5106 exempting hospital beds used for home health care from those taxes. The latter two proposals are particularly relevant to older adults, people with disabilities, and families caring for loved ones. Though these were proposals, they address practical concerns affecting Connecticut residents.

Elections should be about character, experience, ideas, and a willingness to work—not political labels or personal attacks. Steve brings the integrity, respect, and practical experience our state needs. I encourage voters to look beyond the rhetoric and reelect Steve Weir.
bills: HB 5105 (2026, Weir): sales-tax exemption for home ramps
HB 5106 (2026, Weir): sales-tax exemption for home hospital beds

letters.headline: Vote Row A, Andover
letters.note: Co-Chair, Andover Democratic Committee
paragraphs: On Nov. 3rd, Andover voters will find a full slate on Row A. We are proud of every name on it, and we’d like to tell you why.

For State Representative for the 55th District: Ellen Paul. She has spent her career making a modest budget go a long way, first as director of the East Hampton Library and now as the executive director of the Connecticut Library Consortium, whose contracts are used by libraries in all 169 Connecticut towns! In 2025, Ellen worked with legislators of both parties to pass two state library laws. Congressman Joe Courtney, who has known her for 20 years, says, “Ellen will bring integrity to Hartford, and much-needed resources back to the district.” She is endorsed by the Connecticut Education Association, the state’s largest organization advocating for teachers and students.

For State Senator: MD Rahman. MD came to this country with little more than a dream, and he knows what it means to stretch every penny. In Hartford, he helped pass one of the largest tax cuts in state history, helped end state taxes on most kinds of retirement income, and helped secure $5.7 million more for schools in his district.

For Congress: Joe Courtney, who has championed lower prescription costs, voted to protect Medicare, led investments in our Navy, and brought good-paying union jobs and federal dollars home to eastern Connecticut.
For Probate Judge: Thomas Robinson, who has focused his legal practice in Manchester on the types of issues addressed by the probate court for almost 30 years.

And for the statewide offices: Governor Ned Lamont, Lieutenant Governor Susan Bysiewicz, Attorney General William Tong, Secretary of the State Stephanie Thomas, Treasurer Erick Russell, and Comptroller Sean Scanlon. Together they have balanced the state budget, cut taxes for seniors, raised the minimum wage, and invested in our public schools.
These are people who show up, do the work, and bring results home to towns like ours.
Early voting runs through Sunday, November 1st. On Tuesday, November 3rd, polls are open 6 a.m. to 8 p.m., and you can register and vote on the same day. Everything you need is at myvote.ct.gov.
However you vote, please vote. We hope you’ll vote Row A.

letters.headline: Supporting Steve Weir
paragraphs: My name is Christopher Aker, and I have lived in Hebron for 21 years with my wife and three children. And I love and respect community members and families for who they are – not their political affiliations. And because I have 400 words to accomplish my support for the re-election of this excellent incumbent Representative of the 55th, I am going to get right to it. And unlike others, I am not going to operate outside of my depth.

Steve has been unfairly attacked for his vote against making marriage illegal for youth under the age of 18. And not just because there was a ton of added garbage in the bill. I have been an assistant attorney general in the Child Protection Division of the OAG for 22 years. Before that I worked as a psychiatric social worker for almost 10 years. First at Garner Correctional Institute then at Riverview Hospital, a DCF hospital for children and youth – before its name was changed to Solnit South, an act of arrogance and disrespect for those who created and named an institution that was once nationally renowned for its clinical excellence and loving care of children and youth with psychiatric and behavioral disturbances.

I have dedicated my career to helping and protecting children and youth and I am an expert in child protection and juvenile law. Although promulgated with the best of intentions, the law prohibiting marriage for those under 18 years of age, is notional at best. This is because, Connecticut, in a wave of progressive initiatives, in some measure related to Miller v. Alabama, a 2012 SCOTUS decision, radically changed its juvenile justice legal framework, to include how “cross-over” children and youth are handled, culminating in 2017, with the evisceration of the Family with Service Needs statute.

Furthermore, in 2018, the Connecticut Juvenile Training School was closed and the jurisdiction, with respect to the disposition of juvenile delinquents, was transferred from DCF Parole to the Judicial Branch. Child abuse and neglect are inextricably linked to juvenile delinquency and outof-control children and youth. And these changes have produced disastrous consequences for these children and youth. Sex trafficking is rampant and the “under 18” legislation does nothing to address this horrific societal problem.
Children of all ethnicities and sexual orientations, to include transgendered individuals, are precious and deserve to be protected – and sometimes from themselves. Steve embraces this!
